knowledge_statements.title: Convex Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real-valued convexity on a convex subset of a real vector space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a real vector space, let \(C\subseteq X\) be convex, and let \(f:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\). The function \(f\) is convex on \(C\) if, for every \(x,y\in C\) and every \(\lambda\in(0,1)\), \[f\bigl(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y\bigr)\leq \lambda f(x)+(1-\lambda)f(y).\] Its effective domain is \(\operatorname{dom}f=\{x\in C:f(x)<+\infty\}\). The function is proper when \(\operatorname{dom}f\neq\varnothing\); otherwise it is identically \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended-real-valued function on a convex set is convex when, for any two points and any strictly intermediate convex-combination weight, its value at their convex combination does not exceed the corresponding weighted average of their values. Its effective domain consists of the points where it is finite, and it is proper when that domain is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is convex exactly when \(f(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y)\leq \lambda f(x)+(1-\lambda)f(y)\) for all \(x,y\in C\) and all \(\lambda\in(0,1)\).

notation.meaning: Effective domain where the function has a finite value.
Extended-real value used to exclude points from the effective domain.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate of an Infimal Convolution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The common affine minorant ensures the stated convex functions share a finite affine lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_1,f_2:\mathbb R\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be closed convex functions. Suppose there exists an affine function \(a\) such that \(a(x)\le f_i(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R\) and \(i\in\{1,2\}\). Then \[(f_1\ddagger f_2)^*=f_1^*+f_2^*,\] where \(\ddagger\) denotes infimal convolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two closed convex functions possessing a common affine lower bound, the Fenchel conjugate of their infimal convolution is the sum of their conjugates.
assumptions_latex: f_1,f_2\text{ are closed convex functions on }\mathbb R
\exists\text{ affine }a\ \forall x\in\mathbb R\ \forall i\in\{1,2\},\ a(x)\le f_i(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representation by supporting affine minorants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convex functions on Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ is convex, then for every $y\in\mathbb{R}^n$, $$f(y)=\max\left\{f(x)+\xi^T(y-x):x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ \xi\in\partial_c f(x)\right\}.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite convex function is the pointwise maximum of the affine supporting functions generated by all of its convex subgradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(y)=\max_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\,\xi\in\partial_c f(x)}\left(f(x)+\xi^T(y-x)\right)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometry and support representation of the convex epsilon-subdifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise properties of convex epsilon-subdifferentials for a convex function having Lipschitz constant K at the reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex with Lipschitz constant \(K\) at \(x\). Then: (i) \(\partial_0f(x)=\partial_cf(x)\); (ii) for \(0\leq\varepsilon_1\leq\varepsilon_2\), \(\partial_{\varepsilon_1}f(x)\subseteq\partial_{\varepsilon_2}f(x)\); (iii) for \(\varepsilon\geq0\), \(\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\) is nonempty, convex, and compact, and \(\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\subseteq B(0;K)\); (iv) \(\partial_\varepsilon f(x)=\{\xi\in\mathbb{R}^n: f'_\varepsilon(x;d)\geq\xi^Td\text{ for every }d\in\mathbb{R}^n\}\); and (v) \(f'_\varepsilon(x;d)=\max\{\xi^Td:\xi\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\}\) for every \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex function with Lipschitz constant K at x, the zero-subdifferential is the convex subdifferential. Epsilon-subdifferentials grow with epsilon, are nonempty compact convex subsets of the radius-K ball, and are characterized through the approximate directional derivative, which is their support function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial_0f(x)=\partial_cf(x),\quad \partial_{\varepsilon_1}f(x)\subseteq\partial_{\varepsilon_2}f(x),\quad \varnothing\neq\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\subseteq B(0;K),\quad \partial_\varepsilon f(x)=\{\xi:f'_\varepsilon(x;d)\geq\xi^Td\ \forall d\},\quad f'_\varepsilon(x;d)=\max_{\xi\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)}\xi^Td.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fenchel–Moreau Biconjugation Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes lower-semicontinuous convex functions as fixed points of Fenchel biconjugation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a function \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), \[f\text{ is convex and lower semicontinuous}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f^{**}=f.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended-real function is convex and lower semicontinuous exactly when it equals its Fenchel biconjugate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is convex and l.s.c.}\iff f^{**}=f.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Upper Boundedness and Interior Continuity Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An equivalence for extended-real-valued convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $F:V\to\overline{\mathbb R}$ be convex. The following are equivalent: (i) there exist a nonempty open set $\mathcal O\subseteq V$ and $a<+\infty$ such that $F$ is not everywhere equal to $-\infty$ on $\mathcal O$ and $F(x)\le a$ for every $x\in\mathcal O$; (ii) $F$ is proper, $\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}F)\ne\varnothing$, and $F$ is continuous on $\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}F)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex extended-real-valued function is bounded above on a nonempty open set, without being everywhere minus infinity there, if and only if it is proper and continuous on the nonempty interior of its effective domain.

\left[\exists\,\varnothing

ot\equiv-\infty	ext{ on }\mathcal O,\ F(x)\le a\  orall x\in\mathcal Oight]\iff\left[F	ext{ is proper},\ \operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}F)
e\varnothing,\ F\in C\!\left(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}F)ight)ight].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fenchel–Young Subgradient Equivalences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Four equivalent characterizations of a convex subgradient pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\) and \(x,u\in\mathcal H\). The following are equivalent: \[(x,u)\in\operatorname{gra}\partial f;\qquad (u,-1)\in N_{\operatorname{epi}f}(x,f(x));\qquad f(x)+f^*(u)=\langle x,u\rangle;\qquad (u,x)\in\operatorname{gra}\partial f^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper lower-semicontinuous convex function, u is a subgradient at x exactly when (u,−1) is normal to the epigraph at (x,f(x)), exactly when Fenchel–Young equality holds, and exactly when x is a subgradient of the conjugate at u.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x,u)\in\operatorname{gra}\partial f\iff(u,-1)\in N_{\operatorname{epi}f}(x,f(x))\iff f(x)+f^*(u)=\langle x,u\rangle\iff(u,x)\in\operatorname{gra}\partial f^*

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degeneracy After Attaining Minus Infinity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This exceptional behavior arises under the convention allowing functions to take both extended-real infinity values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\Gamma(\mathcal H)\). If \(-\infty\in f(\mathcal H)\), then \(f\) is nowhere real-valued; equivalently, \(f(\mathcal H)\subset\{-\infty,+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a lower semicontinuous convex function in this full extended-real convention attains minus infinity, it cannot take a finite real value anywhere.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\mathcal H)\subset\{-\infty,+\infty\}.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity Is Equivalent to Gradient Monotonicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order characterization for continuously differentiable functions on convex Euclidean domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex and let \(f:Q\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable. Then \(f\in\mathcal F^1(Q)\), equivalently \(f\) is convex on \(Q\), if and only if \[\langle \nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y),x-y\rangle\geq 0\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in Q.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuously differentiable function on a convex set is convex if and only if its gradient is a monotone mapping on that set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\in\mathcal F^1(Q)\iff \forall x,y\in Q,\quad \langle\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y),x-y\rangle\geq 0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Radial continuity from a domain point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The conclusion holds for arbitrary \(x\), including when \(f(x)=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\), \(x\in\mathcal H\), and \(y\in\operatorname{dom}f\). For each \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), set \(x_\alpha=(1-\alpha)x+\alpha y\). Then \(\lim_{\alpha\downarrow0}f(x_\alpha)=f(x)\) in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper lower-semicontinuous convex function, its values along the segment approaching any point x from a domain point y converge to f(x), including when f(x) is positive infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle\lim_{\alpha\downarrow0}f(x_\alpha)=f(x).\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimax Linearization Parameter for Two Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded definition for arbitrary real-valued functions on a nonempty set; convexity is not assumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\neq\varnothing\), let \(f_1,f_2:Q\to\mathbb R\), and set \(f(x)=\max\{f_1(x),f_2(x)\}\). A scalar \(\lambda^*\in[0,1]\) is a minimax linearization parameter for \((f_1,f_2)\) over \(Q\) if
\[
\min_{x\in Q}\max\{f_1(x),f_2(x)\}=\min_{x\in Q}\bigl(\lambda^*f_1(x)+(1-\lambda^*)f_2(x)\bigr),
\]
with both sides interpreted in \(\mathbb R\cup\{\pm\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two real-valued functions on a nonempty set, a minimax linearization parameter is a weight between zero and one for which minimizing the weighted sum gives the same extended-real value as minimizing their pointwise maximum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{x\in Q}\max\{f_1(x),f_2(x)\}=\min_{x\in Q}\left(\lambda^*f_1(x)+(1-\lambda^*)f_2(x)\right)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-Point Inequality Characterization of Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence for a real-valued function defined on a convex subset of Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex and let \(f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}\). Then \(f\) is convex on \(\Omega\) if and only if, for every \(x,y\in\Omega\) and every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), \[f(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y)\le \alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a convex domain, f is convex exactly when its value at every strict convex combination of two points does not exceed the corresponding convex combination of their values.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Graph-density of the subdifferentiability domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation of every finite-valued point with simultaneous convergence of arguments and function values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\). Then
\[
\operatorname{gra}\bigl(f+\iota_{\operatorname{dom}\partial f}\bigr)
\]
is dense in \(\operatorname{gra}f\). Equivalently, for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), there exists \((x_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\subset\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) such that \(x_n\to x\) and \(f(x_n)\to f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every point in the domain of a proper lower-semicontinuous convex function can be approximated by subdifferentiability points so that both the points and their function values converge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \overline{\operatorname{gra}(f+\iota_{\operatorname{dom}\partial f})}=\operatorname{gra}f

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fenchel conjugacy of the self-concordant scalar functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-derivative, conjugate-representation, Young-inequality, and equality identities for ω and ω*.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
\omega(t)=t-\ln(1+t)\quad(t\geq0),\qquad \omega_*(\tau)=-\tau-\ln(1-\tau)\quad(0\leq\tau<1).
\]
For every t\geq0 and \tau\in[0,1),
\[
\omega'(\omega_*'(\tau))=\tau,\qquad \omega_*'(\omega'(t))=t,
\]
\[
\omega(t)=\max_{0\leq\xi<1}\{\xi t-\omega_*(\xi)\},\qquad
\omega_*(\tau)=\max_{\xi\geq0}\{\xi\tau-\omega(\xi)\},
\]
\[
\omega(t)+\omega_*(\tau)\geq\tau t,
\]
and
\[
\omega_*(\tau)=\tau\omega_*'(\tau)-\omega(\omega_*'(\tau)),\qquad
\omega(t)=t\omega'(t)-\omega_*(\omega'(t)).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scalar functions ω and ω* used in self-concordant bounds are Fenchel conjugates: their derivatives are mutual inverses, they admit the stated maximization formulas, satisfy Young's inequality, and attain equality at conjugate derivative pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \omega'\circ\omega_*'=\operatorname{id}_{[0,1)},\quad \omega_*'\circ\omega'=\operatorname{id}_{[0,\infty)},\quad \omega^*=\omega_*,\quad \omega(t)+\omega_*(\tau)\geq\tau t\text{ with the stated equality identities}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\} be convex and h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\} be concave. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ray-Extrapolation Characterization of Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: For a function whose domain is convex, convexity is equivalent to the stated inequality at every feasible ray extrapolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) have a convex domain. Then \(f\) is convex if and only if, for all \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and every \(\beta\geq0\) such that \(y+\beta(y-x)\in\operatorname{dom}f\), \[f\bigl(y+\beta(y-x)\bigr)\geq f(y)+\beta\bigl(f(y)-f(x)\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a function with convex domain, convexity is equivalent to requiring every feasible extrapolation from y away from x to lie above the corresponding affine extrapolation of the values at x and y.

\[

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sublinear structure of the epsilon-directional derivative
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Properties asserted under the source's local Lipschitz hypothesis at the base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\varepsilon\ge0$, and let $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be convex with Lipschitz constant $K$ at $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Then $d\mapsto f'_{\varepsilon}(x;d)$ is positively homogeneous and subadditive, hence convex; its epigraph is a convex cone, and for every $d\in\mathbb{R}^n$, $$|f'_{\varepsilon}(x;d)|\le K\|d\|,\qquad f'_{\varepsilon}(x;-d)\ge-f'_{\varepsilon}(x;d).$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a point where the convex function has Lipschitz constant K, its epsilon-directional derivative is a bounded sublinear function of the direction. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Attainment for Some Convex Combination of Two Level-Bounded Convex Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The conclusion is existential: it asserts attainment for at least one parameter \(\lambda^*\in[0,1]\), not for every parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a finite-dimensional Euclidean space. Let \(f_1,f_2:Q\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) be proper, closed, and convex. Assume that, for every \(i\in\{1,2\}\) and \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\),
\[
L_i(\alpha):=\{x\in Q:f_i(x)\le\alpha\}
\]
is bounded whenever it is nonempty. Define
\[
\phi(\lambda):=\inf_{x\in Q}\bigl(\lambda f_1(x)+(1-\lambda)f_2(x)\bigr),\qquad \lambda\in[0,1].
\]
Then there exist \(\lambda^*\in[0,1]\) and \(x^*\in Q\) such that
\[
\phi(\lambda^*)=\lambda^*f_1(x^*)+(1-\lambda^*)f_2(x^*).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two proper closed convex functions on a nonempty closed convex set, if every nonempty constrained level set of each function is bounded, then at least one convex combination of the functions attains its infimum over the set.
assumptions_latex: Q\text{ is closed and convex in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space}
f_i:Q\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\text{ is proper, closed, and convex for }i\in\{1,2\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\lambda^*\in[0,1]\ \exists x^*\in Q:\ \phi(\lambda^*)=\lambda^*f_1(x^*)+(1-\lambda^*)f_2(x^*).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic Preservation Rules and the Zero-Scaling Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extracted nonnegative-scaling claim requires an additional condition at \(\beta=0\) under its prescribed-domain convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_1\) and \(f_2\) be closed convex functions. Then \(f_1+f_2\) and \(\max\{f_1,f_2\}\) are closed and convex on \(\operatorname{dom}f_1\cap\operatorname{dom}f_2\). For \(\beta>0\), \(\beta f_1\) is closed and convex with domain \(\operatorname{dom}f_1\). If \(\beta=0\) while this domain is retained, \(\beta f_1\) is closed exactly when \(\operatorname{dom}f_1\) is closed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity of a Linear Image Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity preservation under fiberwise lower boundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let A:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n be linear and let g\in\operatorname{Conv}(\mathbb R^m). Suppose that, for every x\in\mathbb R^n, g is bounded below on

\[
(Ag)(x):=\inf\{g(y):Ay=x\},
\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extrapolation Characterization of Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Both conditions are domain-conditional: interpolation or extrapolation is required only when the constructed point belongs to the function's domain; convexity here does not separately assert that the domain is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f$ have domain $\operatorname{dom}f\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$. The condition $f(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y)\leq\alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y)$ for all $x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f$ and $\alpha\in[0,1]$ such that $\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y\in\operatorname{dom}f$ holds if and only if, for all $x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f$ and $\beta\geq0$ such that $y+\beta(y-x)\in\operatorname{dom}f$, one has $f(y+\beta(y-x))\geq f(y)+\beta(f(y)-f(x))$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The domain-conditional chord inequality is equivalent to an extrapolation inequality: whenever extending from x through y remains in the domain, the function value at the extended point is at least the corresponding affine extrapolation of the two endpoint values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&(\forall x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f)(\forall\alpha\in[0,1])\;\bigl[\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y\in\operatorname{dom}f\Rightarrow f(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y)\leq\alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y)\bigr]\\ &\iff (\forall x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f)(\forall\beta\geq0)\;\bigl[y+\beta(y-x)\in\operatorname{dom}f\Rightarrow f(y+\beta(y-x))\geq f(y)+\beta(f(y)-f(x))\bigr].\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise suprema preserve proper convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arbitrary pointwise suprema of extended-real convex functions on the real line.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{f_j\}_{j\in J}\) be a family of convex functions \(f_j:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). If there exists \(x_0\in\mathbb R\) such that \(\sup_{j\in J}f_j(x_0)<+\infty\), then \(f(x)=\sup_{j\in J}f_j(x)\) is a proper convex function on \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pointwise supremum of a family of convex functions is proper and convex if the family is uniformly finite above at some common point.
assumptions_latex: f_j:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\text{ is convex for every }j\in J
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{j\in J}f_j\in\operatorname{Conv}(\mathbb R)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partial minimization preserves convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity of a marginal function on the projection of a convex feasible set. No attainment or closedness conclusion is asserted, and the infimum can equal minus infinity without an additional lower-boundedness assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\) be convex, let \(\phi:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be convex, and assume \(Q\subseteq\operatorname{dom}\phi\). Define \(\widehat Q=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists y\in\mathbb{R}^m,\ (x,y)\in Q\}\) and, for \(x\in\widehat Q\), \(f(x)=\inf\{\phi(x,y):(x,y)\in Q\}\), allowing the value \(-\infty\). Then for all \(x_1,x_2\in\widehat Q\) and \(\alpha\in[0,1]\), \[f(\alpha x_1+(1-\alpha)x_2)\leq \alpha f(x_1)+(1-\alpha)f(x_2).\] Hence \(f\) is convex on \(\widehat Q\) in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing a jointly convex function over one variable subject to a convex joint constraint produces a convex marginal function on the projected feasible set. The theorem does not guarantee attainment, closedness, or a finite lower value.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\inf\{\phi(x,y):(x,y)\in Q\}\) for \(x\in\widehat Q\), with no lower-boundedness or attainment assumption.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is convex on \(\widehat Q\); no closedness or attainment conclusion follows.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Differentiable Convex Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order definition on a convex Euclidean domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex and let \(f:Q\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable. The function \(f\) is convex on \(Q\) when, for every \(x,y\in Q\), \[f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A differentiable function on a convex set is convex when its first-order affine approximation at every point is a global lower bound throughout the set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\forall x,y\in Q)\quad f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dikin-Ball Containment and Local-Norm Distortion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core local metric geometry of a self-concordant function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be self-concordant, define \(\|h\|_x=\langle f''(x)h,h\rangle^{1/2}\), and let \(W^0(x;1)=\{x+h:\|h\|_x<1\}\). Then: (i) \(W^0(x;1)\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\) for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\); (ii) for all \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f\), \(\|y-x\|_y\geq \|y-x\|_x/(1+\|y-x\|_x)\); and (iii) if \(\|y-x\|_x<1\), then \(\|y-x\|_y\leq \|y-x\|_x/(1-\|y-x\|_x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every open unit ball in a self-concordant local norm lies in the domain. Local norms at two domain points satisfy a universal lower comparison, and an upper comparison holds when their displacement has local norm below one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W^0(x;1)\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f,\quad \|y-x\|_y\geq\frac{\|y-x\|_x}{1+\|y-x\|_x},\quad \|y-x\|_x<1\Rightarrow \|y-x\|_y\leq\frac{\|y-x\|_x}{1-\|y-x\|_x}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linearization of a Two-Function Convex Minimax Value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of a convex-combination parameter reproducing the minimum value of a pointwise maximum.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuous Subgradient Selection Implies Differentiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuity is required of a subgradient selection at the specified interior-domain point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be convex and let \(x_0\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\). Suppose there exists a selection \(g\), with \(g(x)\in\partial f(x)\), that is continuous at \(x_0\). Then \(f\) is differentiable at \(x_0\) and
\[
\nabla f(x_0)=g(x_0).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex function is differentiable at an interior-domain point if it admits a subgradient selection continuous there, and its gradient equals the selected subgradient at that point.
assumptions_latex: g(x)\in\partial f(x)\text{ and }g\text{ is continuous at }x_0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is differentiable at }x_0\quad\text{and}\quad\nabla f(x_0)=g(x_0)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularity, Level Sets, and Attainment for Closed Convex Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Five consequences of closed convexity, with the separate constrained hypotheses retained for the attainment and level-boundedness clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be closed and convex. Then: (i) for every sequence \(\{x_k\}\subset\operatorname{dom}f\) with \(x_k\to\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}f(x_k)\geq f(\bar x)\); (ii) for every sequence \(\{x_k\}\subset\operatorname{dom}f\) with \(x_k\to\bar x\notin\operatorname{dom}f\), \(f(x_k)\to+\infty\); and (iii) every level set of \(f\) is empty or closed and convex. Moreover, if \(f\) is closed and convex on \(Q\) and its constrained level sets are bounded, then \(\min_{x\in Q}f(x)\) is attained. If \(f\) is closed and convex on \(Q\) and \(X^*=\arg\min_{x\in Q}f(x)\) is nonempty and bounded, then every constrained level set of \(f\) on \(Q\) is empty or bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex function is lower semicontinuous, diverges along domain sequences approaching a point outside its domain, and has closed convex level sets. Bounded constrained level sets ensure attainment, while a nonempty bounded optimal set ensures that all constrained level sets are empty or bounded.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composite convex minimizers and mixed variational inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained minimization of a smooth-plus-nonsmooth convex functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a reflexive Banach space, let \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal C\subset V\) be closed and convex, and let \(F=F_1+F_2\), where \(F_1,F_2:\mathcal C\to\mathbb R\) are lower-semicontinuous convex functions and \(F_1\) is Gâteaux differentiable. For every \(u\in\mathcal C\), the following are equivalent: \[F(u)=\inf_{w\in\mathcal C}F(w);\] \[\langle F_1'(u),v-u\rangle+F_2(v)-F_2(u)\ge0\quad\forall v\in\mathcal C;\] \[\langle F_1'(v),v-u\rangle+F_2(v)-F_2(u)\ge0\quad\forall v\in\mathcal C.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex decomposition into a Gâteaux-differentiable term and a lower-semicontinuous convex term, a feasible point minimizes the sum exactly when it satisfies the composite Stampacchia inequality, equivalently its Minty form.
assumptions_latex: V\text{ is a reflexive Banach space}
\varnothing\ne\mathcal C\subset V\text{ is closed and convex}
F_1,F_2:\mathcal C\to\mathbb R\text{ are lower semicontinuous and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(u)=\inf_{w\in\mathcal C}F(w)\iff \bigl[\langle F_1'(u),v-u\rangle+F_2(v)-F_2(u)\ge0\ \forall v\in\mathcal C\bigr]\iff \bigl[\langle F_1'(v),v-u\rangle+F_2(v)-F_2(u)\ge0\ \forall v\in\mathcal C\bigr]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity of log-sum-exp compositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity preservation for the log-sum-exp aggregation of finitely many convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_i:\operatorname{dom}(f_i)\to\mathbb R\) be convex for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Then

\]

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The logarithm of the sum of the exponentials of finitely many convex functions is convex on their common domain.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Legendre–Fenchel Conjugate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the conjugate of an arbitrary extended-real function on Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any function \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), its Legendre–Fenchel conjugate is the function \(f^*:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) defined by \[f^*(y):=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^d}\bigl(\langle x,y\rangle-f(x)\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Legendre–Fenchel conjugate of f at y is the supremum, over all x, of the linear pairing of x and y minus f(x).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^*(y)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^d}\{\langle x,y\rangle-f(x)\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Farkas Lemma for a Nonnegative Equality System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the strict dual-test variant available when the matrix is nonsingular; vector inequalities are componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a conformable matrix $A$ and vector $b$, the following are equivalent: (a) there exists $x\geq 0$ such that $Ax=b$; (b) for every $y$ satisfying $y^{\top}A\geq \mathbf{0}^{\top}$, one has $y^{\top}b\geq 0$. If $A$ is nonsingular, these are also equivalent to: (c) for every $y$ satisfying $y^{\top}A>\mathbf{0}^{\top}$, one has $y^{\top}b\geq 0$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear system Ax=b has a componentwise nonnegative solution exactly when every vector whose product with A is componentwise nonnegative has a nonnegative product with b. If A is nonsingular, it suffices equivalently to test vectors whose product with A is strictly positive.
assumptions_latex: A\text{ is nonsingular for the equivalence with condition (c)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\exists x\geq 0:Ax=b)\iff(\forall y,\ y^{\top}A\geq\mathbf{0}^{\top}\Rightarrow y^{\top}b\geq0),\quad A\text{ nonsingular}\Rightarrow[(a)\iff(c)].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower and Upper Semicontinuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions on a real locally convex space, with the extended-real indicator specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $V$ be a real locally convex space. A function $F:V\to\mathbb R$ is lower semicontinuous if and only if $\{u\in V:F(u)\le a\}$ is closed for every $a\in\mathbb R$; equivalently, $F(\bar u)\le\liminf_{u\to\bar u}F(u)$ for every $\bar u\in V$. It is upper semicontinuous when $-F$ is lower semicontinuous. If $\chi_A$ denotes the extended-real indicator that is $0$ on $A$ and $+\infty$ outside $A$, then $\chi_A$ is lower semicontinuous if and only if $A$ is closed, and upper semicontinuous if and only if $A$ is open.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real-valued function is lower semicontinuous exactly when all of its sublevel sets are closed, equivalently when its value at each point is no greater than the nearby lower limit. Upper semicontinuity is lower semicontinuity of the negative. The extended-real indicator of a set is lower semicontinuous exactly for closed sets and upper semicontinuous exactly for open sets.
assumptions_latex: V\text{ is a real locally convex space}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is l.s.c.}\iff\forall a\in\mathbb R,\ \{F\le a\}\text{ is closed}\iff\forall\bar u\in V,\ F(\bar u)\le\liminf_{u\to\bar u}F(u);\quad \chi_A\text{ is l.s.c.}\iff A\text{ is closed},\quad \chi_A\text{ is u.s.c.}\iff A\text{ is open}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tangent and Normal Cones to a Convex Epigraph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric interpretations of subgradients and directional derivatives through the epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be convex and \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). Then \(s\in\partial f(x)\) if and only if \((s,-1)\in N_{\operatorname{epi}f}(x,f(x))\), and
\[N_{\operatorname{epi}f}(x,f(x))=\{(\lambda s,-\lambda):s\in\partial f(x),\ \lambda\ge 0\}.\]
Moreover,
\[T_{\operatorname{epi}f}(x,f(x))=\{(d,r)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R:r\ge f'(x;d)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite convex function, subgradients correspond to epigraph normals with last component minus one, and all epigraph normals are their nonnegative scalings. The epigraph tangent cone is the epigraph of the directional derivative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\operatorname{epi}f}(x,f(x))=\{(\lambda s,-\lambda):s\in\partial f(x),\lambda\ge0\},\qquad T_{\operatorname{epi}f}(x,f(x))=\{(d,r):r\ge f'(x;d)\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximum of a Convex Function over a Finite Convex Hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum-value reduction from a finite convex hull to its generating points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Delta=\operatorname{Conv}\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{m}\alpha_i x_i\mid \alpha_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^{m}\alpha_i=1\right\}\). If \(f\) is convex on a convex set containing \(\Delta\), then \(\max_{x\in\Delta}f(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}f(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum of a convex function over the convex hull of finitely many points equals the largest value of the function at the generating points.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is convex on a convex set containing }\Delta
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{x\in\Delta}f(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}f(x_i)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximum Bound on a Convex Combination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite Jensen consequence for convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be convex, let \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and let \(x=\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i x_i\), where \(\alpha_i\geq0\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i=1\). Then \[f(x)\leq\max_{1\leq i\leq m}f(x_i).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The value of a convex function at a finite convex combination cannot exceed the largest value at the generating points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x)\leq\max_{1\leq i\leq m}f(x_i)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Functional separation theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The source requires regularity conditions but does not specify them; that limitation is retained explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\} be convex and h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\} be concave, and assume the regularity conditions required for functional separation. If f(x)\geq h(x) for every x\in\mathbb{R}^n, then there exist \alpha^*\in\mathbb{R} and p^*\in\mathbb{R}^n such that f(x)\geq \alpha^*+\langle p^*,x\rangle\geq h(x) for every x\in\mathbb{R}^n.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subject to regularity conditions left unspecified in the extract, any convex function lying everywhere above a concave function admits a single affine function lying between them everywhere.
assumptions_latex: \text{the regularity conditions required by the source theorem hold}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists(\alpha^*,p^*)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^n\;\forall x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\quad f(x)\geq\alpha^*+\langle p^*,x\rangle\geq h(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotone convex composition preserves convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar outer composition on the convex domain of the inner function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\operatorname{dom}\psi\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex and let \(\psi:\operatorname{dom}\psi\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex. Let \(I\subseteq\mathbb{R}\) be an interval containing \(\operatorname{Im}\psi\), and let \(\phi:I\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and nondecreasing on \(\operatorname{Im}\psi\). Define \(f(x)=\phi(\psi(x))\). Then \(f\) is convex on \(\operatorname{dom}\psi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the image of a convex function lies in the interval of definition of a convex scalar function, and the outer function is nondecreasing on that image, then their composition is convex on the inner function's convex domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)=\phi(\psi(x))\) is convex on \(\operatorname{dom}\psi\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimal Scalarization of a Finite-Max Minimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An optimal-value identity under closedness, convexity, and bounded constrained-level-set hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), be closed and convex on \(Q\), and suppose the constrained level sets of the \(f_i\) are bounded. Define \(F(x)=\max_{1\leq i\leq m}f_i(x)\). Then there exists \(\lambda_*\in\Delta_m\), with coordinates \(\lambda_{*,i}\), such that \[\min_{x\in Q}F(x)=\min_{x\in Q}\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_{*,i}f_i(x).\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Minimizers Characterized by Convex-Envelope Contact
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A differentiable real-valued function on the real line need not be convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable. A point \(\bar x\in\mathbb R\) minimizes \(f\) on \(\mathbb R\) if and only if \[f'(\bar x)=0\quad\text{and}\quad \overline{\operatorname{co}}f(\bar x)=f(\bar x).\] In that case, \(\overline{\operatorname{co}}f\) is differentiable and is minimal at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point globally minimizes a differentiable real-valued function on the real line exactly when it is stationary and the function agrees there with its closed convex envelope. In that case the closed convex envelope is differentiable and is also minimized at that point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R}f(x)\iff\left[f'(\bar x)=0\ \land\ \overline{\operatorname{co}}f(\bar x)=f(\bar x)\right],\quad\text{and then }\overline{\operatorname{co}}f\text{ is differentiable with }\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}\overline{\operatorname{co}}f.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Properties of quadratic and absolute-value infimal regularizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional quadratic and absolute-value infimal convolutions of a proper convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\operatorname{Conv}(\mathbb R)\). For \(k>0\), define \(f_{(k)}(x)=\inf_{y\in\mathbb R}\{f(y)+\tfrac{k}{2}(x-y)^2\}\). Then \(f_{(k)}:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is convex, \(f_{(k)}\le f_{(k+1)}\le f\), and \(f_{(k)}\) is differentiable with \(|f_{(k)}'(x_1)-f_{(k)}'(x_2)|\le k|x_1-x_2|\). Every minimizer of \(f\) minimizes \(f_{(k)}\) with the same value; conversely, a minimizer of \(f_{(k)}\) lying in \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\) minimizes \(f\). Moreover, \(f_{(k)}(x)\to f(x)\) as \(k\to+\infty\), except possibly for \(x\in\partial\operatorname{dom}f\). For sufficiently large \(k\), define \(f_{[k]}(x)=\inf_{y\in\mathbb R}\{f(y)+k|x-y|\}\). Then \(f_{[k]}:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is convex, \(f_{[k]}\le f_{[k+1]}\le f\), and \(|f_{[k]}(x_1)-f_{[k]}(x_2)|\le k|x_1-x_2|\). For each \(x_0\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\), \(f_{[k]}(x_0)=f(x_0)\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic infimal regularization gives an increasing sequence of finite convex minorants with k-Lipschitz derivatives, preserves minimizers subject to the stated interior-domain converse, and converges pointwise away from a possible domain-boundary exception. Absolute-value infimal regularization gives increasing k-Lipschitz convex minorants and eventually agrees with the original function at each interior-domain point.
assumptions_latex: k\text{ is sufficiently large for the asserted finite-valued absolute-value regularization properties}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{gathered}f_{(k)}\in\operatorname{Conv}(\mathbb R),\quad f_{(k)}\le f_{(k+1)}\le f,\quad \operatorname{Lip}(f_{(k)}')\le k,\\ \operatorname*{argmin}f\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}f_{(k)},\quad f_{(k)}\to f\text{ pointwise off a possible }\partial\operatorname{dom}f\text{ exception},\\ f_{[k]}\in\operatorname{Conv}(\mathbb R),\quad f_{[k]}\le f_{[k+1]}\le f,\quad \operatorname{Lip}(f_{[k]})\le k,\\ \forall x_0\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f),\ \exists k_0\ \forall k\ge k_0,\ f_{[k]}(x_0)=f(x_0).\end{gathered}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed endpoint extension preserves strict convexity on an interval
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional lower-semicontinuous closure of a strictly convex proper function whose domain is an open interval, possibly with infinite endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g:\mathbb R\to]-\infty,+\infty]\) be strictly convex and proper, with \(\operatorname{dom}g=]\alpha,\beta[\), where \(\alpha,\beta\in[-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(\alpha<\beta\). Define
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}
g(x),&x\in]\alpha,\beta[,\\
\displaystyle\lim_{y\downarrow\alpha}g(y),&x=\alpha,\\
\displaystyle\lim_{y\uparrow\beta}g(y),&x=\beta,\\
+\infty,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
where an endpoint branch applies only when that endpoint is finite. Then \(f\) is strictly convex, \(f=\breve g\), and \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathbb R)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper strictly convex function with an open interval as its domain, extension to each finite endpoint by the corresponding one-sided limit and assignment of positive infinity elsewhere gives its lower-semicontinuous hull. The extension remains strictly convex.
assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb R\to]-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and strictly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\text{ is strictly convex},\quad f=\breve g,\quad f\in\Gamma_0(\mathbb R)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local upper bounds for standard self-concordant functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper bounds inside the unit local-norm neighborhood; the restriction r<1 is essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let f be standard self-concordant, x\in\operatorname{dom}f, and r=\|y-x\|_x<1. Then
\[
\langle\nabla f(y)-\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle\leq\frac{r^2}{1-r},
\]
and
\[
f(y)\leq f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\omega_*(r),
\qquad \omega_*(t)=-t-\ln(1-t).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within local-norm distance less than one from x, a standard self-concordant function has explicit upper bounds on gradient variation and its first-order Taylor remainder.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subgradient at a Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global affine-support definition on an open convex domain; convexity of the function is not assumed in the extracted statement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be open and convex, let \(f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(x\in\Omega\). A vector \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is a subgradient of \(f\) at \(x\) if \[f(y)\ge f(x)+g^\top(y-x)\qquad\text{for every }y\in\Omega.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector is a subgradient of a function at a point when the affine function with that slope through the function value is a global lower bound on the entire domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g\text{ is a subgradient of }f\text{ at }x\iff f(y)\ge f(x)+g^\top(y-x)\ \forall y\in\Omega

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defining inequality for real-valued convex functions on an open convex domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\subseteq X\) be open and convex. A function \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex if, for all \(u,u'\in U\) and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), \[f\bigl(\lambda u+(1-\lambda)u'\bigr)\leq \lambda f(u)+(1-\lambda)f(u').\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real-valued function on an open convex set is convex when its value at every convex combination of two domain points does not exceed the corresponding convex combination of their values.
assumptions_latex: U\subseteq X\text{ is open and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall u,u'\in U\ \forall\lambda\in[0,1],\quad f\bigl(\lambda u+(1-\lambda)u'\bigr)\leq\lambda f(u)+(1-\lambda)f(u')

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Lipschitz Continuity on the Domain Interior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise local regularity of a convex function on the interior of its effective domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be convex and let \(x_0\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\). Then there exist a neighborhood \(U\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\) of \(x_0\) and \(L\ge0\) such that \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le L\|x-y\|\) for all \(x,y\in U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex function is locally Lipschitz continuous at every interior point of its effective domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U\ni x_0,\ U\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f,\ \exists L\ge0\ \forall x,y\in U:\ |f(x)-f(y)|\le L\|x-y\|

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate of a Pointwise Supremum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indexed closed-convex functions on the real line with a common point where their supremum is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{g_j\}_{j\in J}\) be proper closed convex functions on \(\mathbb R\). If there exists \(x_0\in\mathbb R\) such that \(\sup_{j\in J}g_j(x_0)<+\infty\), then \[\left(\sup_{j\in J}g_j\right)^*=\overline{\operatorname{co}}\left(\inf_{j\in J}g_j^*\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a family of proper closed convex functions is jointly finite at some point, then the conjugate of its pointwise supremum is the closed convex hull of the pointwise infimum of the individual conjugates.
assumptions_latex: \forall j\in J,\ g_j\text{ is a proper closed convex function on }\mathbb R
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left(\sup_{j\in J}g_j\right)^*=\overline{\operatorname{co}}\left(\inf_{j\in J}g_j^*\right).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Segment-Inequality Characterization of Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A characterization for continuously differentiable real-valued functions on convex subsets of finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex and let \(f:Q\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable. Then \(f\in\mathcal F^1(Q)\), equivalently \(f\) is convex on \(Q\), if and only if, for every \(x,y\in Q\) and every \(\alpha\in[0,1]\), \[f\bigl(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y\bigr)\leq \alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuously differentiable function on a convex set is convex if and only if its value at every convex combination of two domain points is at most the corresponding convex combination of their function values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\in\mathcal F^1(Q)\iff \forall x,y\in Q\;\forall\alpha\in[0,1],\quad f(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y)\leq \alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected Component-Gradient Difference Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sum smoothness inequality, with the average objective and its minimizer supplied by the section notation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f(x)=\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m f_j(x), where each f_j:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R} is convex and \beta-smooth, and let x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin} f. If i is uniformly distributed on [m], then for every x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\[\mathbb{E}_i\bigl\|\nabla f_i(x)-\nabla f_i(x^*)\bigr\|_2^2\le 2\beta\bigl(f(x)-f(x^*)\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an average of beta-smooth convex component functions, the expected squared difference between a uniformly selected component gradient at x and at an optimizer is at most twice beta times the objective gap.
assumptions_latex: f_j:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is convex and }\beta\text{-smooth for every }j\in[m]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\quad \mathbb{E}_i\|\nabla f_i(x)-\nabla f_i(x^*)\|_2^2\le 2\beta\bigl(f(x)-f(x^*)\bigr)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Norm-Relative Lipschitz-Continuous Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines gradient Lipschitz continuity on an arbitrary subset. The extracted definition does not independently impose convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be differentiable, let \(Q\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\), let \(\|\cdot\|_*\) be the dual of \(\|\cdot\|\), and let \(L\ge 0\). Then \(f\in\mathcal F_L^{1,1}(Q,\|\cdot\|)\) means that
\[
\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|_*\le L\|x-y\|\qquad\forall x,y\in Q.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A differentiable function has an L-Lipschitz gradient on Q relative to a norm when every pair of points in Q satisfies the corresponding primal-dual norm inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\in\mathcal F_L^{1,1}(Q,\|\cdot\|)\iff \forall x,y\in Q,\ \|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|_*\le L\|x-y\|

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extended-Value Convex Functions and Domain Extension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines convexity on \(\mathbb R^d\) and records the standard \(+\infty\)-extension from a convex subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is convex if and only if, for every \(x,y\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(t\in[0,1]\), \[f((1-t)x+ty)\le (1-t)f(x)+tf(y).\] If \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is convex and \(g:\Omega\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is convex, then its extension equal to \(g\) on \(\Omega\) and \(+\infty\) outside \(\Omega\) is convex on \(\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended-real function is convex when it satisfies the convexity inequality for every pair of points and interpolation parameter in [0,1]. A convex function on a convex subset remains convex after assignment of +infinity outside that subset.
assumptions_latex: \Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d\text{ is convex for the extension statement}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f((1-t)x+ty)\le(1-t)f(x)+tf(y),\quad\text{and the }+\infty\text{-extension from a convex domain preserves convexity.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simplex Linearization of a Finite Convex Minimax Value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-family existence theorem requiring every nonempty constrained sublevel set of the pointwise maximum to be bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), be closed and convex on \(Q\). Assume that for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\), the set \(\{x\in Q:\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i(x)\le\alpha\}\) is bounded whenever it is nonempty. Define \(F(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i(x)\) and \(\Delta_m=\{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m:\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1\}\). Then there exists \(\lambda_*=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m)\in\Delta_m\) such that \[\min_{x\in Q}F(x)=\min_{x\in Q}\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i f_i(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite family of closed convex functions, if every nonempty sublevel set of their pointwise maximum is bounded, then some simplex weighting produces a weighted sum with the same minimum value as that maximum.
assumptions_latex: f_i\text{ is closed and convex on }Q\quad(i=1,\ldots,m)
\forall\alpha\in\mathbb{R},\quad \{x\in Q:\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i(x)\le\alpha\}\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow \{x\in Q:\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i(x)\le\alpha\}\text{ is bounded}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\lambda_*=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m)\in\Delta_m:\quad \min_{x\in Q}F(x)=\min_{x\in Q}\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i f_i(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interior Continuity on Barrelled Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuity of lower-semicontinuous convex functions on the interior of their effective domains in barrelled spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $V$ be a barrelled space and let $F:V\to\overline{\mathbb R}$ be lower semicontinuous and convex. Then $F$ is continuous on $\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}F)$. In particular, this holds when $V$ is a Banach space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every lower-semicontinuous convex function on a barrelled space, in particular on a Banach space, is continuous on the interior of its effective domain.
assumptions_latex: $F:V\to\overline{\mathbb R}$ is lower semicontinuous and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: $F\in C\!\left(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}F)\right)$; in particular, the conclusion holds when $V$ is Banach.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-Order Characterization of Differentiable Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence on an open convex Euclidean domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be open and convex, and let \(f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfy \(f\in\mathcal{C}^1(\Omega)\). Then \(f\) is convex on \(\Omega\) if and only if, for all \(x,y\in\Omega\), \[f(y)\geq f(x)+Df(x)(y-x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuously differentiable function on an open convex set is convex exactly when its first-order affine approximation at every point is a global lower bound on the function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is convex on }\Omega\iff f(y)\geq f(x)+Df(x)(y-x)\ \forall x,y\in\Omega

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded Convex Functions Are Lipschitz on Smaller Balls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A quantitative interior Lipschitz estimate obtained from upper and lower bounds on a concentric larger ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\operatorname{Conv}(\mathbb R^n)\), \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\delta>0\), and \(m,M\in\mathbb R\). If \(m\le f(x)\le M\) for every \(x\in B(x_0,2\delta)\), then for all \(y,y'\in B(x_0,\delta)\), \[|f(y)-f(y')|\le \frac{M-m}{\delta}\|y-y'\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a convex function is bounded below by m and above by M on a ball of radius 2δ, then it is Lipschitz on the concentric ball of radius δ, with Lipschitz constant at most (M−m)/δ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |f(y)-f(y')|\le \frac{M-m}{\delta}\|y-y'\|\quad\forall y,y'\in B(x_0,\delta)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Even Functions as Sign-Reversal-Invariant Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded definition; properness is assumed, but convexity is not.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,\infty]\) be proper. With \(\mathcal A=\{-I\}\), symmetry with respect to \(\mathcal A\) is equivalent to \[f(x)=f(-x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n.\] A function satisfying this identity is called even.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper extended-real-valued function is even exactly when it is invariant under global sign reversal; equivalently, it is symmetric with respect to the singleton set containing minus the identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\text{ is symmetric with respect to }\{-I\}\iff (\forall x\in\mathbb R^n)\;f(x)=f(-x)\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Involutive Polarity Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric bijection induced by polarity on the normalized closed convex class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On the class
\[
\mathcal F=\{f:\ f\text{ is nonnegative, closed, and convex, and }f(0)=0\},
\]
the map \(f\mapsto f^{\circ}\) is a symmetric one-to-one correspondence; equivalently, it maps \(\mathcal F\) bijectively to itself and satisfies \(f^{\circ\circ}=f\) for every \(f\in\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polarity is an involutive bijection on the class of nonnegative closed convex functions that vanish at the origin.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal F=\{f:\ f\ge0,\ f\text{ closed and convex},\ f(0)=0\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^{\circ}\in\mathcal F,\qquad f^{\circ\circ}=f,\qquad f\mapsto f^{\circ}\ \text{is bijective on }\mathcal F.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive linear combinations preserve convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite positive combinations with a common finite point; the closed-convex branch requires every summand to be closed convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f_1,\ldots,f_m:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\} be proper convex functions, let t_1,\ldots,t_m>0, and suppose that there exists x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n such that f_j(x_0)<+\infty for every j. knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite positive linear combination of proper convex functions with a common finite point is proper convex. It is closed convex if all summands are closed convex.
assumptions_latex: \text{For the closedness conclusion, every }f_j\text{ is closed convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f:=\sum_{j=1}^m t_jf_j\text{ is proper convex, and is closed convex in the closed-convex branch.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic Convexity Preservation Properties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real-valued convex functions in the source setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f be convex. For every \lambda>0, \lambda f is convex and D(\lambda f)=D(f); for every t\in\mathbb{R}, the sets \{x:f(x)\le t\}, \{x:f(x)<t\}, and D(f)=\{x:f(x)<\infty\} are convex. If f_1 and f_2 are convex and D(f_1)\cap D(f_2)\ne\varnothing, then f_1+f_2 and \max\{f_1,f_2\} are convex, and each has domain D(f_1)\cap D(f_2).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive scaling preserves convexity and the effective domain. Sublevel sets, strict sublevel sets, and the effective domain of a convex function are convex. The sum and pointwise maximum of two convex functions with intersecting domains are convex and have the intersection as their domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda f,\ f_1+f_2,\ \max\{f_1,f_2\}\text{ are convex with the stated domains, and the stated level sets of }f\text{ are convex.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex, Strictly Convex, and Concave Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity and strict convexity require a convex effective domain. Strictness applies only to distinct points and interpolation coefficients in the open interval; concavity is defined by sign reversal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}$ and $\operatorname{dom}f:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:f(x)<+\infty\}$. The function $f$ is convex if $\operatorname{dom}f$ is convex and $f(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y)\leq \alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y)$ for every $x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f$ and $\alpha\in[0,1]$. It is strictly convex if $\operatorname{dom}f$ is convex and the inequality is strict whenever $x\neq y$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$. It is concave if $-f$ is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended-real-valued function is convex when its effective domain is convex and its value at every segment interpolation is at most the corresponding interpolation of the endpoint values. It is strictly convex when the inequality is strict for distinct endpoints and an interior coefficient, and it is concave when its negative is convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}f\text{ convex}&\iff \operatorname{dom}f\text{ is convex and }(\forall x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f)(\forall\alpha\in[0,1])\;f(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y)\leq\alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y),\\ f\text{ strictly convex}&\iff \operatorname{dom}f\text{ is convex and }(\forall x\neq y\in\operatorname{dom}f)(\forall\alpha\in(0,1))\;f(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y)<\alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y),\\ f\text{ concave}&\iff -f\text{ is convex}.\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique Closed Convex Extension and Radial-Limit Formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension of a convex function from a nonempty open convex subset of its continuity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let h:\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty] be convex, and let \(D\subset\operatorname{cont}h\) be nonempty, open, and convex. Set \(f=(h+\iota_D)^{**}\). Then \(f\) is the unique function satisfying
\[
f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H),\qquad \operatorname{dom}f\subset\overline D,\qquad f|_D=h|_D.
\]
Moreover, for every \(x\in\mathcal H\) and every \(y\in D\),
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\lim_{\alpha\downarrow0}h((1-\alpha)x+\alpha y),&x\in\overline D,\\
+\infty,&x\notin\overline D.
\end{cases}
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The biconjugate of a convex function restricted to a nonempty open convex subset of its continuity set is the unique proper lower-semicontinuous convex extension agreeing there and having domain contained in the set's closure. Its values on the closure are radial limits from any point in the open set, and it is infinite outside the closure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f=(h+\iota_D)^{**}\text{ is uniquely characterized by }f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H),\ \operatorname{dom}f\subset\overline D,\ f|_D=h|_D,\text{ with the stated radial-limit formula}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Growth Criteria from the Positive Asymptotic Slope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes growth as x tends to positive infinity for a finite convex function on the real line.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex. Then
\[
\lim_{x\to+\infty}f(x)=+\infty\iff f'_{\infty}(1)>0,
\]
and
\[
\lim_{x\to+\infty}\frac{f(x)}{x}=+\infty\iff f'_{\infty}(1)=+\infty.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex real-valued function on the real line, the function tends to positive infinity exactly when its positive asymptotic slope is positive; its ratio to x tends to positive infinity exactly when that slope is positive infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left(\lim_{x\to+\infty}f(x)=+\infty\iff f'_{\infty}(1)>0\right)\land\left(\lim_{x\to+\infty}\frac{f(x)}{x}=+\infty\iff f'_{\infty}(1)=+\infty\right).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Supremum-of-Affine-Minorants Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes lower-semicontinuous convex extended-real functions by affine lower representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), the following are equivalent: \(f\) is convex and lower semicontinuous; and there exists a family of affine functions \((f_\alpha)_\alpha\) such that \[f(x)=\sup_\alpha f_\alpha(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^d.\] The family may be chosen as all affine functions \(a\) satisfying \(a\le f\) pointwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended-real function is convex and lower semicontinuous exactly when it is the pointwise supremum of affine functions; all of its affine minorants may be used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is convex and l.s.c.}\iff f=\sup_\alpha f_\alpha\text{ for affine }f_\alpha,\quad\{a:a\text{ affine and }a\le f\}\text{ is an admissible family.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness from agreement on the open positive half-space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions supported in the closed nonnegative half-space are determined by a common nontrivial restriction to its open positive half-space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,g\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H\oplus\mathbb R)\) satisfy \(\operatorname{dom}f\cup\operatorname{dom}g\subseteq\mathcal H\times\mathbb R_+\). If \(f|_{\mathcal H\times\mathbb R_{++}}=g|_{\mathcal H\times\mathbb R_{++}}\) and this common restriction is not identically \(+\infty\), then \(f=g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions with domains contained in the closed nonnegative half-space are equal if they agree nontrivially throughout the open positive half-space.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted Squared-Norm Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid for every norm on \(\mathbb R^n\), including the endpoint weights \(\alpha=0\) and \(\alpha=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\|\cdot\|\) be a norm on \(\mathbb R^n\). For every \(x,y\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\alpha\in[0,1]\),
\[
\alpha\|x\|^2+(1-\alpha)\|y\|^2
\ge \alpha(1-\alpha)(\|x\|+\|y\|)^2
\ge \alpha(1-\alpha)\|x-y\|^2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted sum of two squared norms dominates the weighted square of the sum of their norms, which in turn dominates the same weight times the squared distance between the vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha\|x\|^2+(1-\alpha)\|y\|^2\ge\alpha(1-\alpha)(\|x\|+\|y\|)^2\ge\alpha(1-\alpha)\|x-y\|^2

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global lower bounds for standard self-concordant functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local-norm lower bounds for gradient variation and first-order Taylor error, valid for arbitrary domain points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let f be standard self-concordant. For every x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f,
\[
\langle\nabla f(y)-\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle\geq\frac{\|y-x\|_x^2}{1+\|y-x\|_x},
\]
and
\[
f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\omega(\|y-x\|_x),
\qquad \omega(t)=t-\ln(1+t).
\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity, Strict Convexity, and Concavity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions for an extended-real-valued function using its effective domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity and multiplier subgradients of an affine-fiber value function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General convex marginalization along the fibers of a full-row-rank linear map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be convex, let \(Q\subset\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\) be closed and convex, and assume that the level sets of \(f\) on \(Q\) are bounded. Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(n>m\), have full row rank, and define \(\phi(u)=\min\{f(x):x\in Q,\ Ax=u\}\). Then \(\phi\) is convex. If \(\{x\in\operatorname{int}(Q):Ax=u\}\neq\varnothing\), then every \(y^*\) for which there exist \(x^*\in Q\) and \(g^*\in\partial f(x^*)\) satisfying \(Ax^*=u\) and \(\langle g^*-A^Ty^*,x-x^*\rangle\geq0\) for every \(x\in Q\) belongs to \(\partial\phi(u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimal value obtained by minimizing a convex function over affine fibers is convex. At fibers meeting the interior of Q, every equality multiplier satisfying the associated subgradient variational inequality is a subgradient of the value function.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi(u):=\min_{x\in Q,\ Ax=u}f(x)\text{ is convex},\qquad \{y^*:\exists x^*,g^*,\ Ax^*=u,\ g^*\in\partial f(x^*),\ \langle g^*-A^Ty^*,x-x^*\rangle\geq0\ \forall x\in Q\}\subseteq\partial\phi(u)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximum of a Convex Function on a Finite Convex Hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The generators need not be distinct or extreme; the equality concerns the convex hull of the stated finite family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be convex, let \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and set \[\Delta=\operatorname{Conv}\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i x_i:\alpha_i\geq0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i=1\right\}.\] Then \[\max_{x\in\Delta}f(x)=\max_{1\leq i\leq m}f(x_i).\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed convex integral functional on a Hilbert-valued L2 space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integral functional generated by a fixed closed proper convex integrand on a separable real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mu)\) be a measure space, let \(\mathrm H\) be a separable real Hilbert space, let \(\varphi\in\Gamma_0(\mathrm H)\), and set \(\mathcal H=L^2((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mu);\mathrm H)\). Assume either \(\mu(\Omega)<+\infty\) or \(\varphi\geq\varphi(0)=0\). Define
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\int_\Omega\varphi(x(\omega))\,\mu(d\omega),&\varphi\circ x\in L^1((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mu);\mathbb R),\\
+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Then \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed proper convex integrand on a separable real Hilbert space induces a closed proper convex integral functional on the corresponding Hilbert-valued L2 space, provided either the measure is finite or the integrand is nonnegative and vanishes at zero.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathrm H\) is a separable real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence of a Minimax Linearization Weight
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded finite-family theorem under closedness, convexity, and bounded constrained-level-set assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\) be a nonempty closed convex set and let \(f_i:Q\to\mathbb R\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), be closed convex functions. Assume that for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\),
\[
\{x\in Q:\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i(x)\le\alpha\}
\]
is bounded. If \(F(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i(x)\), then there exists
\[
\lambda_*\in\Delta_m:=\{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m:\textstyle\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1\}
\]
such that
\[
\min_{x\in Q}F(x)=\min_{x\in Q}\sum_{i=1}^m(\lambda_*)_i f_i(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many closed convex functions on a nonempty closed convex set, if every sublevel set of their pointwise maximum is bounded, then some simplex weight makes the minimum of their weighted sum equal the minimum of their pointwise maximum.
assumptions_latex: f_i:Q\to\mathbb R\text{ is closed and convex for }i=1,\ldots,m
\forall\alpha\in\mathbb R,\ \{x\in Q:\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i(x)\le\alpha\}\text{ is bounded}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\lambda_*\in\Delta_m:\quad \min_{x\in Q}\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i(x)=\min_{x\in Q}\sum_{i=1}^m(\lambda_*)_i f_i(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Convexity and Convexity on a Subset
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The restricted definitions apply to a nonempty subset of the effective domain; the source does not assume that the subset itself is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper. It is strictly convex if, for all distinct \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and all \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), \[f(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y)<\alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y).\] If \(\varnothing\neq C\subset\operatorname{dom}f\), then \(f\) is convex on \(C\) when the corresponding inequality with \(\leq\) holds for every \(x,y\in C\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and it is strictly convex on \(C\) when the strict inequality holds whenever \(x\neq y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper function is strictly convex when every nontrivial convex combination of distinct domain points has value strictly below the corresponding combination of endpoint values. Convexity and strict convexity on a nonempty subset use the analogous inequalities for points in that subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}f\text{ strictly convex}&\iff(\forall x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f)(\forall\alpha\in(0,1))\;x\neq y\Rightarrow f(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y)<\alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y),\\f\text{ convex on }C&\iff(\forall x,y\in C)(\forall\alpha\in(0,1))\;f(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y)\leq\alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y),\\f\text{ strictly convex on }C&\iff(\forall x,y\in C)(\forall\alpha\in(0,1))\;x\neq y\Rightarrow f(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y)<\alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y).\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convex functions on Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be convex. For every $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$, $$\partial_c f(x)=\{\xi\in\mathbb{R}^n: f'(x;d)\ge \xi^Td\ \text{for every }d\in\mathbb{R}^n\},$$ and, for every $d\in\mathbb{R}^n$, $$f'(x;d)=\max_{\xi\in\partial_c f(x)}\xi^Td.$$

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic operations preserving convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the stipulated value for opposite infinities in the extended-real sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let functions take values in \(\overline{\mathbb R}\). (i) If \(F:V\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is convex and \(\lambda>0\), then \(\lambda F\) is convex. (ii) If \(F,G:V\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) are convex, then \(F+G\) is convex, with \((F+G)(u):=+\infty\) when \(F(u)\) and \(G(u)\) are opposite infinities. (iii) For any family \((F_i)_{i\in I}\) of convex functions \(V\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), the pointwise supremum \[F(u)=\sup_{i\in I}F_i(u)\] is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexity is preserved by multiplication by a positive scalar, by extended-real addition using the stated convention for opposite infinities, and by the pointwise supremum of any family of convex functions.

(F_i)_{i\in I}\text{ is any family of convex functions }V\to\overline{\mathbb R}\text{ in (iii)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda F,\quad F+G,\quad\text{and}\quad \sup_{i\in I}F_i\text{ are convex in their respective cases}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed convex affine-composite perspective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perspective construction whose scale and argument are affine functions of the underlying Hilbert-space variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal K\) be a real Hilbert space, \(\varphi\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal K)\), \(L\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H,\mathcal K)\), \(r\in\mathcal K\), \(u\in\mathcal H\), and \(\rho\in\mathbb R\). Define
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}
(\langle x,u\rangle-\rho)\,\varphi\!\left(\dfrac{Lx-r}{\langle x,u\rangle-\rho}\right),&\langle x,u\rangle>\rho,\\
(\operatorname{rec}\varphi)(Lx-r),&\langle x,u\rangle=\rho,\\
+\infty,&\langle x,u\rangle<\rho.
\end{cases}
\]
If there exists \(z\in\mathcal H\) such that \(Lz\in r+(\langle z,u\rangle-\rho)\operatorname{dom}\varphi\) and \(\langle z,u\rangle\geq\rho\), then \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine composition of the closed perspective of a closed proper convex function is itself closed, proper, and convex when a point satisfies the stated domain-compatibility and nonnegative-scale conditions. The zero-scale value is supplied by the recession function, and negative scales receive positive infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) and \(\mathcal K\) are real Hilbert spaces.
\(L\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H,\mathcal K)\), \(r\in\mathcal K\), \(u\in\mathcal H\), and \(\rho\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Subdifferential and Its Fundamental Properties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combines the subdifferential definition with the existence, differentiability, conjugacy, inverse, and monotonicity properties stated in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a convex function \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), \[\partial f(x):=\{p\in\mathbb R^d:f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle p,y-x\rangle\ \forall y\in\mathbb R^d\}.\] If \(x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\), then \(\partial f(x)\ne\varnothing\); if \(f\) is differentiable at \(x\), then \(\partial f(x)=\{\nabla f(x)\}\). When \(f=f^{**}\), \[p\in\partial f(x)\iff x\in\partial f^*(p)\iff f(x)+f^*(p)=\langle x,p\rangle.\] For such a conjugate pair, \(f\in C^1\) if and only if \(f^*\) is strictly convex. If \(h\) is strictly convex, then \((\partial h)^{-1}\) is single-valued on its domain. Finally, if \(p_i\in\partial f(x_i)\) for \(i=1,2\), then \[\langle p_1-p_2,x_1-x_2\rangle\ge0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex subdifferential consists of all slopes defining global affine lower supports. It is nonempty in the interior of the effective domain and is the gradient singleton at differentiability points. For a biconjugate-closed function, subgradients are reciprocal under Fenchel conjugacy and characterize equality in the Fenchel–Young inequality. The extract also states the C1/strict-convexity conjugacy equivalence, single-valued inverse subdifferentials for strictly convex functions, and monotonicity of every convex subdifferential.
assumptions_latex: f=f^{**}\text{ for the reciprocal conjugacy and }C^1\text{/strict-convexity assertions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial f(x)=\{p:f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle p,y-x\rangle\ \forall y\};\quad x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\Rightarrow\partial f(x)\ne\varnothing;\quad f\text{ differentiable at }x\Rightarrow\partial f(x)=\{\nabla f(x)\};\quad p\in\partial f(x)\iff x\in\partial f^*(p)\iff f(x)+f^*(p)=\langle x,p\rangle;\quad\langle p_1-p_2,x_1-x_2\rangle\ge0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hölder inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The second factor in the extracted display is normalized to the conjugate-exponent norm of \(y\), as required by the stated hypotheses and the named inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mu)\) be a measure space, let \(p\in]1,+\infty[\), and set \(p^*=p/(p-1)\). For every \(x\in L^p(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mu)\) and \(y\in L^{p^*}(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mu)\),
\[
\int_\Omega |x(\omega)y(\omega)|\,\mu(d\omega)
\leq
\left(\int_\Omega |x(\omega)|^p\,\mu(d\omega)\right)^{1/p}
\left(\int_\Omega |y(\omega)|^{p^*}\,\mu(d\omega)\right)^{1/p^*}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On any measure space, the integral of the absolute value of the product of an L-p function and an L-p-star function is at most the product of their respective norms, where p-star is the conjugate exponent p divided by p minus one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \int_\Omega|xy|\,d\mu\leq\|x\|_p\|y\|_{p^*}.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower-semicontinuous closure of a perspective function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed extension of a convex perspective across the zero-scale boundary by the recession function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\varphi\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\), and define
\[
f(\xi,x)=\begin{cases}
\xi\varphi(x/\xi),&\xi>0,\\
+\infty,&\xi\leq0.
\end{cases}
\]
Set
\[
g(\xi,x)=\begin{cases}
\xi\varphi(x/\xi),&\xi>0,\\
(\operatorname{rec}\varphi)(x),&\xi=0,\\
+\infty,&\xi<0.
\end{cases}
\]
Then \(\breve f=g\in\Gamma_0(\mathbb R\oplus\mathcal H)\).

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\breve f=g\in\Gamma_0(\mathbb R\oplus\mathcal H)\), with \(g(0,x)=(\operatorname{rec}\varphi)(x)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex and strictly convex functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real-valued functions defined on a convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\) be convex and let \(f\) be defined on \(\Omega\). The function \(f\) is convex if, for every \(x_1,x_2\in\Omega\) and every \(\alpha\in[0,1]\), \[f(\alpha x_1+(1-\alpha)x_2)\le \alpha f(x_1)+(1-\alpha)f(x_2).\] It is strictly convex if, for every distinct \(x_1,x_2\in\Omega\) and every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the inequality is strict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function on a convex set is convex when its value at every convex combination is at most the corresponding convex combination of its values. It is strictly convex when this inequality is strict for distinct points and coefficients strictly between zero and one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is convex under the nonstrict inequality, and strictly convex under the stated strict inequality}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuously Differentiable Convex and Concave Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions on a convex Euclidean domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex and let \(f:Q\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable. Then \(f\in\mathcal F^1(Q)\) when, for all \(x,y\in Q\), \[f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle.\] The function \(f\) is concave on \(Q\) when \(-f\) is convex on \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuously differentiable function on a convex domain is convex when every tangent affine function is a global lower bound. It is concave when its negative is convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\in\mathcal F^1(Q)\iff(\forall x,y\in Q)\;f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle,\qquad f\text{ is concave on }Q\iff -f\text{ is convex on }Q
