knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong, weak, sequential, and relative lower semicontinuity
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(D\subset H\), and let \(f:H\to[-\infty,+\infty]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hilbert-space taxonomy distinguishing ambient versus relative topology, strong versus weak topology, and nets versus sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x\in H\), \(f\) is strongly lower semicontinuous if every net \(x_a\to x\) in norm satisfies \(f(x)\leq\liminf_a f(x_a)\); it is weakly lower semicontinuous if every net \(x_a\rightharpoonup x\) satisfies the same inequality. Replacing nets by sequences defines strong sequential and weak sequential lower semicontinuity. Relative lower semicontinuity on \(D\) means that the corresponding condition is imposed only on nets or sequences contained in \(D\), with convergence in the subspace topology. Global lower semicontinuity means the selected condition holds at every point of \(H\). For convex \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), the four ambient regimes—strong, strong sequential, weak, and weak sequential—are equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower semicontinuity has several regimes. Strong lower semicontinuity uses norm-convergent nets, while weak lower semicontinuity uses weakly convergent nets. Sequential variants test only sequences. Relative lower semicontinuity restricts the approaching points to a specified subset and uses its subspace topology. A regime is global when it holds at every ambient point. For convex extended-real functions on a Hilbert space that never take negative infinity, all four ambient strong, weak, net, and sequential regimes coincide.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected convergence class determines the lower-semicontinuity regime through \(f(x)\leq\liminf f(x_a)\); for convex \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), the four ambient Hilbert-space regimes coincide.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Strong lower semicontinuity is equivalent to norm-closedness of \(\operatorname{epi}f\).
Weak lower semicontinuity is equivalent to weak closedness of \(\operatorname{epi}f\) in \(H\times\mathbb R\).
special_cases_latex: In metric spaces, strong lower semicontinuity and strong sequential lower semicontinuity coincide for arbitrary functions.
For convex functions on Hilbert space, norm-closed convex level sets are also weakly closed.
immediate_consequences_latex: Weak lower semicontinuity implies strong lower semicontinuity because norm convergence implies weak convergence.
For convex Hilbert-space functions, verifying any one of the four ambient regimes verifies them all.
boundary_notes: Relative lower semicontinuity on \(D\) need not imply ambient lower semicontinuity at boundary points of \(D\).
Outside sequential spaces, sequential lower semicontinuity can be strictly weaker than net-based lower semicontinuity.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The class \(\Gamma_0(H)\) consists of all functions \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) that are convex, lower semicontinuous, and proper. Properness means \[\operatorname{dom}f=\{x\in H:f(x)<+\infty\}\neq\varnothing\] and \(f(x)>-\infty\) for every \(x\in H\). Thus members of \(\Gamma_0(H)\) have nonempty effective domain and closed convex epigraphs, without taking the value \(-\infty\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Properness dichotomy for the lower-semicontinuous hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the lower-semicontinuous hull of a convex function according to whether it has any finite value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be convex. If \(\operatorname{lsc}f\) is finite at some point, then both \(\operatorname{lsc}f\) and \(f\) are proper. Otherwise, \[ (\operatorname{lsc}f)(x)=\begin{cases}-\infty,&x\in\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{dom}f),\\+\infty,&x\notin\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{dom}f).\end{cases} \]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex function, if its lower-semicontinuous hull has one finite value, then both the hull and the original function are proper. If it has no finite value, it equals minus infinity on the closure of the effective domain and plus infinity outside that closure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\exists x_0:(\operatorname{lsc}f)(x_0)\in\mathbb R\bigr)\implies f,\operatorname{lsc}f\text{ proper};\quad\text{otherwise }(\operatorname{lsc}f)(x)=-\infty\text{ on }\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{dom}f)\text{ and }+\infty\text{ off it}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure and radial-limit properties of a convex function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional extended-real convex functions, without an initial properness assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to[-\infty,+\infty] be convex. Then \operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{dom}f)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{dom}(\operatorname{cl}f)), \operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)=\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}(\operatorname{cl}f)), and (\operatorname{cl}f)(x)=f(x) for every x\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f). Moreover, \operatorname{cl}f is proper if and only if f is proper. For every x\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f) and y\in\mathbb{R}^n, (\operatorname{cl}f)(y)=\lim_{\alpha\downarrow0}f(y+\alpha(x-y)).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex function and its closure have domains with the same closure and relative interior, agree on that relative interior, and are proper simultaneously. The closed value at any point is obtained as the radial limit from any relative-interior domain point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{dom}f)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{dom}(\operatorname{cl}f)),\quad \operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)=\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}(\operatorname{cl}f)),\quad (\operatorname{cl}f)|_{\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)}=f|_{\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)},\quad \operatorname{cl}f\text{ is proper}\iff f\text{ is proper},\quad (\operatorname{cl}f)(y)=\lim_{\alpha\downarrow0}f(y+\alpha(x-y))

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recession criterion for closed exact infimal convolution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closedness, properness, and pointwise attainment of an infimal convolution under strict recession compatibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f_1,f_2:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty] be closed proper convex functions. If f_1^{0+}(z)+f_2^{0+}(-z)>0 for every z\neq 0, then f_1\square f_2 is closed, proper, and convex. Moreover, for every x\in\mathbb{R}^n there exists y\in\mathbb{R}^n such that (f_1\square f_2)(x)=f_1(x-y)+f_2(y)=\inf_{u\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{f_1(x-u)+f_2(u)\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If two closed proper convex functions have strictly positive combined recession value in every nonzero pair of opposite directions, their infimal convolution is closed, proper, and convex, and its defining infimum is attained at every point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_1\square f_2\text{ is closed, proper, and convex, and }\forall x\in\mathbb{R}^n\;\exists y\in\mathbb{R}^n:\ (f_1\square f_2)(x)=f_1(x-y)+f_2(y)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closedness and recession calculus for finite convex sums
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two finite-sum regimes: closed summands, and possibly nonclosed summands satisfying a common relative-interior condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f_1,\ldots,f_m:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty] be proper convex functions. If every f_i is closed and \sum_{i=1}^m f_i\not\equiv+\infty, then \sum_{i=1}^m f_i is closed, proper, and convex, and \left(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\right)^{0+}=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i^{0+}. If the f_i are not all closed but \bigcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f_i)\neq\varnothing, then \operatorname{cl}\left(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\right)=\sum_{i=1}^m\operatorname{cl}f_i.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite sum of proper closed convex functions is closed and proper when it is not identically positive infinity, and its recession function is the sum of the recession functions. When the summands are not all closed, a common relative-interior domain point makes closure commute with the finite sum.
assumptions_latex: m\in\mathbb{N},\quad f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper and convex for }i=1,\ldots,m
\text{First regime: }f_i\text{ is closed for every }i\text{ and }\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\not\equiv+\infty
\text{Second regime: the }f_i\text{ are not all closed and }\bigcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f_i)\neq\varnothing
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left[\sum_i f_i\text{ is closed proper convex and }(\sum_i f_i)^{0+}=\sum_i f_i^{0+}\right]\quad\text{or, in the second regime,}\quad\operatorname{cl}(\sum_i f_i)=\sum_i\operatorname{cl}f_i

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex primitive of an extended-real nondecreasing function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes existence, identification of both one-sided derivatives, and uniqueness up to an additive real constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a\in\mathbb{R}, and let \varphi:\mathbb{R}\to[-\infty,+\infty] be nondecreasing with \varphi(a)\in\mathbb{R}. If \varphi_- and \varphi_+ denote its left and right limits, then f(x)=\int_a^x\varphi(t)\,dt is a well-defined closed proper convex function on \mathbb{R} satisfying f'_- =\varphi_-\leq\varphi\leq\varphi_+=f'_+. If g is any closed proper convex function on \mathbb{R} such that g'_-\leq\varphi\leq g'_+, then g=f+\alpha for some \alpha\in\mathbb{R}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended-real nondecreasing function that is finite at a chosen base point has a well-defined integral primitive that is closed, proper, and convex. Its left and right derivatives are the corresponding one-sided limits of the integrand and bracket the integrand. Any other closed proper convex function whose one-sided derivatives bracket the same integrand differs from this primitive by a real constant.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Domain and radial-limit properties of convex-function closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The identities apply to an arbitrary extended-real convex function, without assuming it is initially closed or proper.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to[-\infty,\infty]\) be convex. Then \[\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{dom}f)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{dom}f^{\mathrm{cl}}),\qquad \operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)=\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f^{\mathrm{cl}}),\] and \[f^{\mathrm{cl}}(x)=f(x)\quad\text{for all }x\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f).\] Moreover, \(f^{\mathrm{cl}}\) is proper if and only if \(f\) is proper. If \(x\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\), then for every \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), \[f^{\mathrm{cl}}(y)=\lim_{\alpha\downarrow0}f\bigl(y+\alpha(x-y)\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing a convex function preserves the closure and relative interior of its domain, agrees with the function on that relative interior, and preserves properness. Values of the closure at any point are obtained by approaching that point along a segment from a relative-interior domain point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{dom}f)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{dom}f^{\mathrm{cl}}),\quad \operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)=\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f^{\mathrm{cl}}),\quad f^{\mathrm{cl}}|_{\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)}=f|_{\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bregman distance and admissible distance-generating function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General Bregman geometry together with the set-relative assumptions used by mirror methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\omega:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex and differentiable on \(\operatorname{dom}(\partial\omega)\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact-level condition for closed partial minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation of closed proper convexity and compact attainment under infimal projection.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity and one-sided continuity of convex derivatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the extended-real conventions outside the effective domain and all four one-sided limit identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}\to(-\infty,+\infty] be closed, proper, and convex. Extend f'_+ and f'_- by assigning -\infty at points strictly to the left of \operatorname{dom}f and +\infty at points strictly to its right. Then f'_+ and f'_- are nondecreasing on \mathbb{R} and finite on \operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f). Whenever z_1<x<z_2, one has f'_+(z_1)\leq f'_-(x)\leq f'_+(x)\leq f'_-(z_2). Moreover, for every x\in\mathbb{R}, \lim_{z\downarrow x}f'_+(z)=\lim_{z\downarrow x}f'_-(z)=f'_+(x) and \lim_{z\uparrow x}f'_+(z)=\lim_{z\uparrow x}f'_-(z)=f'_-(x).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed proper convex function on the real line, extend both one-sided derivatives by minus infinity strictly to the left of its domain and plus infinity strictly to the right. Both derivatives are nondecreasing and finite in the domain interior. The left derivative at a point is no greater than the right derivative, derivatives at earlier and later points provide the stated bounds, and the right- and left-hand limits of either derivative equal the right and left derivatives, respectively.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is closed, proper, and convex}
f'_\pm(x)=-\infty\text{ strictly to the left of }\operatorname{dom}f
f'_\pm(x)=+\infty\text{ strictly to the right of }\operatorname{dom}f
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f'_\pm\text{ are nondecreasing and finite on }\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f),\quad f'_+(z_1)\leq f'_-(x)\leq f'_+(x)\leq f'_-(z_2)\ (z_1<x<z_2),\quad \lim_{z\downarrow x}f'_\pm(z)=f'_+(x),\ \lim_{z\uparrow x}f'_\pm(z)=f'_-(x).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Distance Bound Between Nested Convex Sublevel Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated set-distance estimate for two strict superoptimal levels of a convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}} be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with \operatorname{argmin}f\ne\varnothing. Set \alpha_0=\min f and \rho_0=d(0,\operatorname{argmin}f). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative Continuity on the Domain in One Dimension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The result is specific to extended-real proper closed convex functions on the real line. It asserts sequential continuity relative to the effective domain, including its finite boundary points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure formula for a generated positively homogeneous convex function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The notation \((f\lambda)(x)\) denotes the scaled perspective used in the generation construction, and \(\lambda=0^+\) denotes its recession-boundary value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be closed, proper, and convex with \(f(0)>0\), and let \(k\) be the positively homogeneous convex function generated by \(f\). Then \(k\) is proper and, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \[(\operatorname{cl}k)(x)=\inf\{(f\lambda)(x):\lambda>0\text{ or }\lambda=0^+\},\] with the infimum attained. If \(0\in\operatorname{dom}f\), then \(k\) is closed and the \(\lambda=0^+\) term may be omitted, although the resulting infimum over \(\lambda>0\) need not be attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed proper convex function that is positive at the origin generates a proper positively homogeneous convex function. The closure of the generated function is the attained infimum of the scaled perspectives over positive scales and the recession-boundary scale. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Everywhere Supporting Subgradients Imply Convexity and Relative Lower Semicontinuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closedness of the epigraph is relative to $Q\times\mathbb{R}$. Ambient epigraph closedness follows if $Q$ is additionally closed; without that assumption the source's ambient-closedness parenthetical is not valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be nonempty and convex, and let $f:Q\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}$ be proper and finite throughout $Q$. If $\partial_Q f(x)=\{g\in\mathbb{R}^n:f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle\ \forall y\in Q\}$ is nonempty for every $x\in Q$, then $f$ is convex and lower semicontinuous relative to $Q$. Equivalently, $\operatorname{epi}_Q f=\{(x,t)\in Q\times\mathbb{R}:t\ge f(x)\}$ is closed in $Q\times\mathbb{R}$. If $Q$ is closed, then $\operatorname{epi}_Q f$ is also closed in $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every point of a nonempty convex domain admits a supporting affine minorant valid throughout that domain, then the function is convex and lower semicontinuous relative to the domain. Ambient epigraph closedness additionally requires the domain to be closed.
assumptions_latex: f:Q\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\text{ is proper and finite on }Q
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is convex and lower semicontinuous relative to }Q,\qquad \operatorname{epi}_Qf\text{ is closed in }Q\times\mathbb{R}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Conjugate and Fenchel–Young Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The properness conclusion requires the usual affine-minorant condition, which is automatic for proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper function \(\varphi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), its convex conjugate is \(\varphi^*(y)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}(\langle x,y\rangle-\varphi(x))\). The function \(\varphi^*\) is convex and lower semicontinuous, and it is proper when \(\varphi\) admits a finite affine minorant. For every \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\langle x,y\rangle\le\varphi(x)+\varphi^*(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex conjugate is the supremum of all affine pairings minus the original function. It is convex and lower semicontinuous, is proper under the standard affine-minorant condition, and satisfies the Fenchel–Young inequality.
assumptions_latex: For properness of \(\varphi^*\), \(\varphi\) has a finite affine minorant; in particular, this holds for proper lower-semicontinuous convex \(\varphi\) in finite dimensions
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varphi^*(y)=\sup_x(\langle x,y\rangle-\varphi(x))\) and \(\langle x,y\rangle\le\varphi(x)+\varphi^*(y)\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epigraph, Effective Domain, and Properness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real-valued functions on subsets of finite-dimensional real spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f:X\to[-\infty,+\infty]\), with \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), define \(\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,w)\in X\times\mathbb R:f(x)\le w\}\) and \(\operatorname{dom}f=\{x\in X:f(x)<+\infty\}\). The function is proper if \(f(x)<+\infty\) for some \(x\in X\) and \(f(x)>-\infty\) for every \(x\in X\); otherwise it is improper. Equivalently, \(f\) is proper exactly when \(\operatorname{epi}f\) is nonempty and contains no vertical line.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The epigraph consists of all finite-height points lying on or above the function, and the effective domain consists of points where the function is below positive infinity. The function is proper when it is finite somewhere and never equals negative infinity; equivalently, its epigraph is nonempty and has no vertical line.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is proper}\iff \bigl(\exists x\in X:\ f(x)<+\infty\bigr)\land\bigl(\forall x\in X:\ f(x)>-\infty\bigr)\iff \operatorname{epi}f\ne\varnothing\text{ and }\operatorname{epi}f\text{ contains no vertical line}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent criteria for global Lipschitz continuity of a convex function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real-valued lower-semicontinuous convex functions on a Hilbert space; the Lipschitz bound may be zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R\) be lower semicontinuous and convex, and let \(\beta\in\mathbb R_+\). The following are equivalent:
\[
\begin{aligned}
&f\text{ is Lipschitz continuous with constant }\beta;\\
&\operatorname{ran}\partial f\subseteq B(0;\beta);\\
&\operatorname{dom}f^*\subseteq B(0;\beta);\\
&\operatorname{rec}f\leq\beta\|\cdot\|.
\end{aligned}
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global beta-Lipschitz continuity is equivalent to all subgradients having norm at most beta, the conjugate domain lying in the radius-beta ball, and the recession function being bounded above by beta times the norm.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R\text{ is lower semicontinuous and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is }\beta\text{-Lipschitz}\iff\operatorname{ran}\partial f\subseteq B(0;\beta)\iff\operatorname{dom}f^*\subseteq B(0;\beta)\iff\operatorname{rec}f\leq\beta\|\cdot\|

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain membership and a variational inequality for the minimizer of a strongly convex Bregman proximal subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\omega:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex and differentiable on \(\operatorname{dom}(\partial\omega)\). Let \(\psi:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex with \(\operatorname{dom}(\psi)\subseteq\operatorname{dom}(\omega)\), and suppose \(\omega+\delta_{\operatorname{dom}(\psi)}\) is \(\sigma\)-strongly convex for some \(\sigma>0\). If \(b\in\operatorname{dom}(\partial\omega)\) and \[a=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb E}\{\psi(x)+B_\omega(x,b)\},\] then \(a\in\operatorname{dom}(\partial\omega)\) and, for every \(u\in\operatorname{dom}(\psi)\), \[\langle\nabla\omega(b)-\nabla\omega(a),u-a\rangle\leq\psi(u)-\psi(a).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated convexity, domain, differentiability, and strong-convexity assumptions, the Bregman proximal minimizer belongs to the generator's subdifferential domain and satisfies the displayed variational inequality for every point in the domain of psi.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quantitative local bounds and Lipschitz regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two neighborhood estimates for a proper convex extended-real-valued function on a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, let \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and let \(\rho>0\). (i) If \(\eta=\sup f(B(x_0;\rho))<+\infty\), then for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), \[\forall x\in B(x_0;\alpha\rho),\qquad |f(x)-f(x_0)|\le \alpha\bigl(\eta-f(x_0)\bigr).\] (ii) If \(\delta=\operatorname{diam}f(B(x_0;2\rho))<+\infty\), then \(f\) is Lipschitz continuous relative to \(B(x_0;\rho)\) with Lipschitz constant \(\delta/\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper convex function, an upper bound on a ball gives a quantitative oscillation bound on every concentrically contracted ball. If the range over the ball of radius 2ρ has finite diameter δ, the function is Lipschitz on the ball of radius ρ with constant δ/ρ.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{(i) }\forall x\in B(x_0;\alpha\rho),\ |f(x)-f(x_0)|\le\alpha(\eta-f(x_0));\qquad \text{(ii) }\operatorname{Lip}_{B(x_0;\rho)}(f)\le\delta/\rho.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complete nondecreasing curve and its characterizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the curve by filling the interval between the left and right limits at every abscissa and records its order-theoretic and topological characterizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \varphi:\mathbb{R}\to[-\infty,+\infty] be nondecreasing and have at least one finite value, and let \varphi_-,\varphi_+ be its left and right limits. A complete nondecreasing curve is \Gamma=\{(x,x^*)\in\mathbb{R}^2:\varphi_-(x)\le x^*\le\varphi_+(x)\}. If I=\{x:\exists x^*\ (x,x^*)\in\Gamma\}, then \Gamma may contain horizontal and vertical segments, the map (x,x^*)\mapsto x+x^* is a bijection from \Gamma onto \mathbb{R} and is continuous with continuous inverse, and \Gamma is equivalently a maximal totally ordered subset of \mathbb{R}^2 under the coordinatewise partial order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete nondecreasing curve is obtained from an extended-real nondecreasing function having a finite value by including, at each real point, every finite ordinate between its left and right limits. Such a curve may have horizontal and vertical segments. Addition of the two coordinates gives a homeomorphism from the curve onto the real line, and these curves are exactly the maximal subsets of the plane that are totally ordered coordinatewise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x,x^*)\mapsto x+x^*\text{ is a homeomorphism }\Gamma\to\mathbb{R},\quad \Gamma\text{ is a maximal coordinatewise totally ordered subset of }\mathbb{R}^2.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique Attainment of a Strongly Convex Composite Minimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A convex-analysis existence, uniqueness, and domain-attainment result for an extended-real composite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $\omega,\psi:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]$ be proper, closed, and convex. Suppose that $\omega$ is differentiable on $\operatorname{dom}(\partial\omega)$, that $\operatorname{dom}(\psi)\subseteq\operatorname{dom}(\omega)$, and that $\omega+\delta_{\operatorname{dom}(\psi)}$ is $\sigma$-strongly convex for some $\sigma>0$. Then
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb E}\{\psi(x)+\omega(x)\}
\]
is uniquely attained at a point in $\operatorname{dom}(\psi)\cap\operatorname{dom}(\partial\omega)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the two functions are proper, closed, and convex, their effective domains are nested as stated, and the mirror term restricted to the effective domain of the other function is strongly convex, then their sum has a unique minimizer belonging to both the effective domain of the first function and the subdifferentiability domain of the mirror term.
assumptions_latex: \omega:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}
\psi:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb E}\{\psi(x)+\omega(x)\}=\{x^\star\}\quad\text{for some }x^\star\in\operatorname{dom}(\psi)\cap\operatorname{dom}(\partial\omega)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Convexity from Pointwise Subdifferential Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition placing a proper extended-real function in the closed convex class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $Q_1\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and let $f:Q_1\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ be proper, with
\[
\operatorname{dom}f:=\{x\in Q_1:f(x)<+\infty\}.
\]
Suppose that for every $x\in\operatorname{dom}f$ there is a nonempty set $Y(x)$ satisfying
\[
\partial f(x)=\operatorname{conv}Y(x).
\]
Then $f$ is closed and convex on $Q_1$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper extended-real function is closed and convex if, at every point of its effective domain, its subdifferential is the convex hull of a nonempty chosen set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coderivative lower estimate for a convex marginal function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies at every attained minimizing pair and requires no qualification condition for the inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal K\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(g:\mathcal H\oplus\mathcal K\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, and let \(F:\mathcal H\rightrightarrows\mathcal K\) have a convex graph. Define \(f(x)=\inf_{y\in F(x)}g(x,y)\), and suppose that \(f\) is proper. For every \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), \[\bigcup_{\substack{\bar y\in F(\bar x),\ g(\bar x,\bar y)=f(\bar x),\\(u,v)\in\partial g(\bar x,\bar y)}}\left(u+D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(v)\right)\subseteq\partial f(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper convex marginal function, every sum of a partial subgradient of the joint objective and a corresponding coderivative value at an attaining feasible point is a subgradient of the marginal function.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H,\mathcal K\text{ are real Hilbert spaces}\)
\(g:\mathcal H\oplus\mathcal K\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper and convex}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigcup_{\substack{\bar y\in F(\bar x),\ g(\bar x,\bar y)=f(\bar x),\\(u,v)\in\partial g(\bar x,\bar y)}}\left(u+D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(v)\right)\subseteq\partial f(\bar x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Domain One-Dimensional Convex Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensionality defined through the affine hull of the effective domain, rather than scalar-functional dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A closed proper convex function \(h:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,\infty]\) is domain one-dimensional if \(\operatorname{aff}(\operatorname{dom}h)\) is a point or a line; equivalently, there exist \(a,b\in\mathbb R^n\), with \(a=0\) allowed for the point case, such that \[\operatorname{aff}(\operatorname{dom}h)=\{\gamma a+b\mid\gamma\in\mathbb R\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed proper convex function is domain one-dimensional when the affine hull of its effective domain is either a single point or a line.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,\infty]\) is closed, proper, and convex
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists a,b\in\mathbb R^n:\ \operatorname{aff}(\operatorname{dom}h)=\{\gamma a+b\mid\gamma\in\mathbb R\}\), where \(a=0\) represents the point case

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Radial limit identity for closed proper convex functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Radial recovery of values, including boundary and exterior values, within the closed proper convex class.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closedness and Attainment of Linear Infimal Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded finite-dimensional theorem for marginalizing a closed proper convex function along a linear map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty] be closed, proper, and convex, let A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m be linear, and define (Ah)(y)=\inf\{h(x)\mid Ax=y\}. Assume that Az\neq0 whenever h^{0+}(z)\leq0 and h^{0+}(-z)>0. Then Ah is closed, proper, and convex, (Ah)^{0+}=A(h^{0+}), where A(h^{0+})(y)=\inf\{h^{0+}(z)\mid Az=y\}, and for every y with (Ah)(y)\neq+\infty there exists x with Ax=y and h(x)=(Ah)(y).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed proper convex function remains closed, proper, and convex after infimal projection along a linear map if the map annihilates no direction having nonpositive forward recession value and strictly positive reverse recession value. Recession commutes with this projection, and every marginal value below positive infinity is attained on its fiber.
assumptions_latex: h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is closed, proper, and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ah\text{ is closed, proper, and convex},\qquad (Ah)^{0+}=A(h^{0+}),\qquad (Ah)(y)\neq+\infty\implies\exists x\in\mathbb{R}^n\ \left(Ax=y\ \wedge\ h(x)=(Ah)(y)\right).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz continuity on closed bounded relative-interior subsets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional relative-interior regularity for a proper convex extended-real-valued function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\mathcal H\) is finite-dimensional, let \(f:\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, and let \(C\) be a nonempty closed bounded subset of \(\operatorname{ri}\operatorname{dom}f\). Then \(f\) is Lipschitz continuous relative to \(C\); equivalently, there exists \(L<+\infty\) such that \[\forall u,v\in C,\qquad |f(u)-f(v)|\le L\|u-v\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In finite dimensions, a proper convex function is Lipschitz on every nonempty closed bounded subset contained in the relative interior of its effective domain.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists L<+\infty\ \forall u,v\in C,\quad |f(u)-f(v)|\le L\|u-v\|.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recession-lineality condition for closed partial minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closedness, properness, convexity, and attainment under a recession condition on one fiber sublevel set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^{n+m}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be closed, proper, and convex, and define \(f(x)=\inf_{z\in\mathbb{R}^m}F(x,z)\). Suppose that for some \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\bar\gamma\in\mathbb{R}\), the set \(S=\{z\mid F(\bar x,z)\le\bar\gamma\}\) is nonempty and satisfies \(\operatorname{rec}S=\operatorname{lin}S\). Then \(f\) is closed, proper, and convex, and for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathbb{R}^m}F(x,z)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If one nonempty fiber sublevel set has no recession directions beyond its lineality space, partial minimization preserves closed proper convexity and every finite-valued fiber attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is closed, proper, and convex, and }\forall x\in\operatorname{dom}f,\ \operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathbb{R}^m}F(x,z)\ne\varnothing

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise constrained subgradients imply closedness on a convex set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition for closedness on a nonempty convex subset of the effective domain; the conclusion retains the source's set-relative formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be nonempty and convex, and let $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ be proper and convex with $Q\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f$. For $x\in Q$, define
\[
\partial_Qf(x)=\{g\in\mathbb{R}^n:f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle\ \forall y\in Q\}.
\]
If $\partial_Qf(x)\neq\varnothing$ for every $x\in Q$, then $f$ is a closed convex function on $Q$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a proper convex function has, at every point of a nonempty convex subset of its effective domain, an affine supporting slope valid throughout that subset, then the function is closed and convex on that subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is a closed convex function on }Q

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closedness and recession calculus for pointwise suprema
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arbitrarily indexed pointwise suprema, including a relative-interior condition for commuting closure with the supremum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let I be an arbitrary index set, let f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty] be proper convex for every i\in I, and set f=\sup_{i\in I}f_i pointwise. If f is finite somewhere and every f_i is closed, then f is closed and proper and f^{0+}=\sup_{i\in I}f_i^{0+}. If the f_i are not all closed but there exists \bar x\in\bigcap_{i\in I}\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f_i) with f(\bar x)<+\infty, then \operatorname{cl}f=\sup_{i\in I}\operatorname{cl}f_i.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an arbitrary family of proper convex functions, a pointwise supremum that is finite somewhere is closed and proper when every member is closed, and its recession function is the supremum of their recession functions. If some members are nonclosed, a common relative-interior point where the supremum is finite makes closure commute with the supremum.
assumptions_latex: I\text{ is an arbitrary index set},\quad f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper and convex for every }i\in I
\text{First regime: }f(x)<+\infty\text{ for some }x\text{ and every }f_i\text{ is closed}
\text{Second regime: the }f_i\text{ are not all closed and }\exists\bar x\in\bigcap_{i\in I}\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f_i)\text{ with }f(\bar x)<+\infty
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left[f\text{ is closed and proper and }f^{0+}=\sup_{i\in I}f_i^{0+}\right]\quad\text{or, in the second regime,}\quad\operatorname{cl}f=\sup_{i\in I}\operatorname{cl}f_i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the equivalent epigraphical and recession formulations and carefully qualifies the bounded-domain sufficient condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convex function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is co-finite if it is closed and proper and \(\operatorname{epi}f\) contains no nonvertical half-line. A closed proper convex function with bounded effective domain is co-finite.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower-semicontinuous convex envelope and affine minorants
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(f:H\to[-\infty,+\infty]\). Pointwise ordering of extended-real functions is used.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hilbert-space closed convex envelope, including the affine-minorant representation when continuous affine minorants exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The lower-semicontinuous convex envelope of \(f\) is \[\breve f=\sup\{g:g\leq f,\ g\text{ is lower semicontinuous and convex}\}.\] It is the greatest lower-semicontinuous convex function majorized by \(f\), and \(\operatorname{epi}\breve f\) is closed and convex. Define the affine-minorant family \[\mathcal A_f=\{(u,\alpha)\in H\times\mathbb R:\langle x,u\rangle+\alpha\leq f(x)\ \forall x\in H\}.\] If \(f\) possesses a continuous affine minorant, then \[\breve f(x)=f^{**}(x)=\sup_{(u,\alpha)\in\mathcal A_f}\bigl(\langle x,u\rangle+\alpha\bigr).\] Thus closed convexification is equivalently the supremal calculus of all continuous affine lower supports.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lower-semicontinuous convex envelope of a function is the pointwise supremum of all lower-semicontinuous convex functions lying below it. It is therefore the largest closed convex minorant. When the original function admits at least one continuous affine minorant, the envelope equals its biconjugate and can be computed as the supremum of all continuous affine functions lying below the original function everywhere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\breve f=\sup\{g\leq f:g\text{ is lower semicontinuous and convex}\}\), and, when \(\mathcal A_f\ne\varnothing\), \(\breve f=f^{**}=\sup_{(u,\alpha)\in\mathcal A_f}(\langle\cdot,u\rangle+\alpha)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\breve f\) is characterized by \(\breve f\leq f\) and \(g\leq\breve f\) for every lower-semicontinuous convex \(g\leq f\).
When an affine minorant exists, \(\operatorname{epi}\breve f=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(\operatorname{epi}f)\) under the standard properness conditions.
special_cases_latex: If \(f\) is already lower semicontinuous and convex, then \(\breve f=f\).
For a proper lower-semicontinuous convex function, \(f\) is the supremum of its continuous affine minorants.
immediate_consequences_latex: The envelope operator is monotone: \(f\leq h\Rightarrow\breve f\leq\breve h\).
The envelope is idempotent: \(\breve{\breve f}=\breve f\).
boundary_notes: If no continuous affine minorant exists, the affine supremum may degenerate and must not be substituted for the defining envelope without qualification.
The envelope is a minorant of \(f\), despite occasional terminology calling it a hull.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex and closed-convex function hulls
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper. Assume that the indicated families of minorants are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise hierarchy of convexification and lower-semicontinuous convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The convex envelope and lower-semicontinuous convex envelope of \(f\) are respectively \[\operatorname{conv}f=\sup\{g:g\leq f,\ g\text{ convex}\}\] and \[\overline{\operatorname{conv}}f=\sup\{g:g\leq f,\ g\text{ convex and lower semicontinuous}\}.\] They satisfy the hull hierarchy \[\overline{\operatorname{conv}}f\leq\operatorname{conv}f\leq f.\] Epigraphically, under the usual properness and affine-minorization condition, \[\operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{conv}f)=\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{epi}f),\qquad \operatorname{epi}(\overline{\operatorname{conv}}f)=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(\operatorname{epi}f),\] with vertical completion implicit in the epigraph convention. The closed convex envelope is also \(f^{**}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex envelope of a proper function is the greatest convex function below it. The closed convex envelope is the greatest function below it that is both convex and lower semicontinuous. The closed convex envelope lies below the convex envelope, which lies below the original function. Under the standard affine-minorization condition, their epigraphs are the convex hull and closed convex hull of the original epigraph, and the closed convex envelope equals the Fenchel biconjugate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\overline{\operatorname{conv}}f\leq\operatorname{conv}f\leq f\), with \(\overline{\operatorname{conv}}f=f^{**}\) when \(f\) has a continuous affine minorant.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}f\) is the pointwise supremum of convex minorants of \(f\).
\(\overline{\operatorname{conv}}f\) is the pointwise supremum of lower-semicontinuous convex minorants of \(f\).
special_cases_latex: If \(f\) is convex, then \(\operatorname{conv}f=f\).
If \(f\in\Gamma_0(H)\), then \(\overline{\operatorname{conv}}f=\operatorname{conv}f=f\).
For \(f=\iota_S\), the envelopes correspond to indicators of \(\operatorname{conv}S\) and \(\overline{\operatorname{conv}}S\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Both hull operators are monotone and idempotent on their respective fixed-point classes.
Closed convexification can change boundary values and can enlarge the effective domain to points represented by closed convex epigraph limits.
boundary_notes: The epigraph identities require attention to improper degeneracies and the existence of affine minorants.
Convexification alone need not produce a lower-semicontinuous function.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex and closed convex hulls of a function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Names the ordinary and closed convex envelopes and extends their epigraph construction to pointwise infima of families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be not identically \(+\infty\) and admit an affine minorant. Its convex hull \(\operatorname{co}g\) is the common function obtained equivalently from \(\operatorname{co}(\operatorname{epi}g)\), from the supremum of convex minorants of \(g\), or from finite barycentric mixtures of values of \(g\). Its closed convex hull is denoted \(\overline{\operatorname{co}}g\) or \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{co}g\). More generally, if every member of \(\{g_j\}_{j\in J}\) has the same affine minorant, the epigraph of the convex, respectively closed convex, hull of \(\inf_{j\in J}g_j\) is generated by convexifying, respectively closed-convexifying, \(\bigcup_{j\in J}\operatorname{epi}g_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex hull of an extended-real function is its greatest convex minorant, equivalently its epigraphical or barycentric convexification; adding closure gives its closed convex hull. For a family sharing an affine lower bound, convexifying the pointwise infimum is governed by convexification of the union of the family’s epigraphs.
assumptions_latex: g\text{ is minorized by an affine function}
\forall j\in J,\ g_j\text{ is minorized by one common affine function}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{co}g\text{ and }\overline{\operatorname{co}}g=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{co}g\text{ denote the convex and closed convex hulls of }g.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent representations of the convex hull of a function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional extended-real convexification by epigraphs, convex minorants, and barycentric mixtures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be not identically \(+\infty\), and suppose that \(g(x)\ge \langle s,x\rangle-b\) for some \((s,b)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\) and every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). Define
\[
f_1(x)=\inf\{r:(x,r)\in\operatorname{co}(\operatorname{epi}g)\},
\]
\[
f_2(x)=\sup\{h(x):h\text{ is convex on }\mathbb R^n,\ h\le g\},
\]
and
\[
f_3(x)=\inf\left\{\sum_{j=1}^k\alpha_jg(x_j):k\ge1,\ \alpha\in\Delta_k,\ x_j\in\operatorname{dom}g,\ \sum_{j=1}^k\alpha_jx_j=x\right\}.
\]
Then \(f_1,f_2,f_3\) are convex and \(f_1=f_2=f_3\) on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper extended-real function with an affine lower bound has a convex hull that can equivalently be constructed from the convex hull of its epigraph, as the supremum of all convex minorants, or through finite barycentric mixtures of its values.
assumptions_latex: \exists(s,b)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\ \forall x\in\mathbb R^n:\ g(x)\ge\langle s,x\rangle-b
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_1,f_2,f_3\text{ are convex and }f_1=f_2=f_3\text{ on }\mathbb R^n.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure or Lower-Semicontinuous Hull of a Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General extended-real definition; the hull's codomain permits both infinite values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), its closure or lower-semicontinuous hull \(\operatorname{cl}f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{\pm\infty\}\) is defined by \[(\operatorname{cl}f)(x):=\liminf_{y\to x}f(y),\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^n.\] Equivalently, \[\operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{cl}f)=\overline{\operatorname{epi}f}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lower-semicontinuous hull is the pointwise lower limit of the function and, equivalently, its epigraph is the closure of the original epigraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\operatorname{cl}f)(x)=\liminf_{y\to x}f(y),\qquad \operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{cl}f)=\overline{\operatorname{epi}f}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex hull of a finite pointwise minimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barycentric representation of the convex envelope of a finite minimum of convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_1,\ldots,g_m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be convex functions minorized by the same affine function. Then, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
\left[\operatorname{co}\left(\min_{1\le j\le m}g_j\right)\right](x)
=\inf\left\{\sum_{j=1}^m\alpha_jg_j(x_j):\alpha\in\Delta_m,\ x_j\in\operatorname{dom}g_j,\ \sum_{j=1}^m\alpha_jx_j=x\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex hull of the pointwise minimum of finitely many convex functions sharing an affine lower bound equals the infimum of weighted function values over simplex weights and component points whose weighted average is the argument.
assumptions_latex: g_j:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\text{ is convex for }j=1,\ldots,m
\exists(s,b)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\ \forall j\ \forall x:\ g_j(x)\ge\langle s,x\rangle-b
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left[\operatorname{co}\left(\min_{1\le j\le m}g_j\right)\right](x)=\inf_{\substack{\alpha\in\Delta_m,\ x_j\in\operatorname{dom}g_j\\\sum_j\alpha_jx_j=x}}\sum_{j=1}^m\alpha_jg_j(x_j)\quad\forall x\in\mathbb R^n.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The lower-semicontinuous hull of \(f\) is the envelope \[\operatorname{cl}f(x)=\sup_{U\in\mathcal N(x)}\inf_{y\in U}f(y).\] It satisfies \(\operatorname{cl}f\leq f\), is lower semicontinuous, and has the maximality property \[g\leq f\ \text{and }g\text{ lower semicontinuous}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad g\leq\operatorname{cl}f.\] In a metrizable space, \(\operatorname{cl}f(x)=\liminf_{y\to x}f(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lower-semicontinuous hull is the greatest lower-semicontinuous minorant, obtained from neighborhood infima or, metrically, the limit inferior.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Order Laws for the Lower-Semicontinuous Hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-theoretic laws of lower-semicontinuous regularization without convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Whenever the stated hulls remain \((-\infty,+\infty]\)-valued, \[f\le g\Longrightarrow \operatorname{cl}f\le\operatorname{cl}g,\qquad \operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{cl}f)=\operatorname{cl}f.\] Moreover, \(\operatorname{cl}f=f\) if and only if \(f\) is lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower-semicontinuous hull formation is monotone, idempotent, and fixes exactly the lower-semicontinuous functions.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) have hulls in the stated codomain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Hull formation is monotone and idempotent, with lower-semicontinuous functions as its fixed points.

assumptions_latex: The greatest lower-semicontinuous minorant of \(f\) is \((-\infty,+\infty]\)-valued.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For extended-real functions \(f,g:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) whose lower-semicontinuous hulls remain in this codomain, \[f\le g\Longrightarrow \operatorname{cl}f\le \operatorname{cl}g,\qquad \operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{cl}f)=\operatorname{cl}f.\] Moreover, \(\operatorname{cl}f=f\) if and only if \(f\) is lower semicontinuous.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent representations of the closed convex hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional closed convexification through closed epigraph hulls, closed convex minorants, and affine minorants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be not identically \(+\infty\) and admit an affine minorant. Define
\[
\bar f_1(x)=\inf\{r:(x,r)\in\overline{\operatorname{co}}(\operatorname{epi}g)\},
\]
\[
\bar f_2(x)=\sup\{h(x):h\text{ is closed and convex on }\mathbb R^n,\ h\le g\},
\]
and
\[
\bar f_3(x)=\sup\{\langle s,x\rangle-b:\langle s,y\rangle-b\le g(y)\text{ for all }y\in\mathbb R^n\}.
\]
Then \(\bar f_1,\bar f_2,\bar f_3\) are closed and convex, coincide on \(\mathbb R^n\), and equal \(\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{co}g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper extended-real function with an affine lower bound, its closed convex hull is equivalently obtained from the closed convex hull of its epigraph, as the supremum of its closed convex minorants, or as the supremum of all affine minorants.
assumptions_latex: \exists(s,b)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\ \forall x\in\mathbb R^n:\ g(x)\ge\langle s,x\rangle-b
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar f_1=\bar f_2=\bar f_3=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{co}g),\qquad \bar f_i\text{ is closed and convex for }i=1,2,3.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epigraphical closure of an extended-real function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure as a closed-minorant envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(h:\mathbf E\to[-\infty,+\infty]\), its closure \(\operatorname{cl}h\) is defined by \[\operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{cl}h)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{epi}h).\] It is the largest closed function satisfying \(\operatorname{cl}h\le h\). If \(h\) is convex, then \(\operatorname{cl}h\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closure of an extended-real function is the function whose epigraph is the closure of the original epigraph. It is the greatest closed minorant of the function, and closure preserves convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{cl}h)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{epi}h),\qquad \operatorname{cl}h=\max\{g:g\le h,\ g\text{ closed}\},\qquad h\text{ convex}\Rightarrow\operatorname{cl}h\text{ convex}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexification Alone Need Not Close
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Example showing that the closure stage may strictly change the convex envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f=\delta_{(0,1)}:\mathbb R\to(-\infty,+\infty]\). Since \((0,1)\) is convex,
\[\operatorname{conv}f=f=\delta_{(0,1)},\]
but \(f\) is not lower semicontinuous and
\[\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{conv}f)=\delta_{[0,1]}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The indicator of an open interval is already convex, but closing its convex envelope adds the endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}f=\delta_{(0,1)}\neq\delta_{[0,1]}=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{conv}f)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The closed convex hull \(\operatorname{clconv}f\) is proper if and only if there exist \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}\) such that \(\langle a,x\rangle+b\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Thus properness of \(f\) alone does not ensure properness of its closed convex hull. For example, if \(f(x)=-x^2\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), then no finite affine function minorizes \(f\) globally, and \(\operatorname{clconv}f\equiv-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper function has a proper closed convex hull exactly when it has a global affine lower bound; the function minus x squared shows failure otherwise.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure Without Lower Semicontinuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite-dimensional boundary for existence of continuous affine minorants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be an infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space admitting a discontinuous linear functional \(\ell:H\to\mathbb R\). Then \(f=\ell\) is finite, proper, and convex, but it has no global minorant of the form \(x\mapsto\langle x,u\rangle+\beta\) with \(u\in H\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discontinuous linear functional is a proper finite convex function with no continuous affine global minorant.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is an infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space admitting a discontinuous linear functional \(\ell:H\to\mathbb R\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Touching Minorants and Subgradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed claim is mathematically sound but canonically belongs to subgradient theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(u\in H\),
\[f(x)\geq f(\bar x)+\langle x-\bar x,u\rangle\quad\text{for every }x\in H\]
if and only if \(u\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine global minorant touches a convex function at a point exactly when its slope is a subgradient there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u\in\partial f(\bar x)\iff f(\cdot)\geq f(\bar x)+\langle\cdot-\bar x,u\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.title: Touching Minorants and Subgradients

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[f^*(u)=\sup_{x\in H}\{\langle x,u\rangle-f(x)\},\]
the inequality \(\langle x,u\rangle+\beta\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in H\) holds if and only if \(\beta\leq-f^*(u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine minorants with slope u have precisely the intercepts bounded above by minus the conjugate value at u.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle\cdot,u\rangle+\beta\leq f\iff\beta\leq-f^*(u)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuous affine minorant and exact affine support
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global continuous affine lower bounds, with exactness at a specified point distinguished from mere minorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A continuous affine function \(a:H\to\mathbb R\) is an affine minorant of \(f\) if there exist \(u\in H\) and \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\) such that \[a(y)=\langle y,u\rangle+\alpha\leq f(y)\qquad(\forall y\in H).\] It is exact at \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) if additionally \(a(x)=f(x)\), equivalently \[f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle y-x,u\rangle\qquad(\forall y\in H).\] In this case \(u\) is a subgradient of \(f\) at \(x\). Every \(f\in\Gamma_0(H)\) possesses at least one continuous affine minorant, and if \(x\in\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom}f\), it possesses one exact at \(x\). Moreover, such an \(f\) is the pointwise supremum of all its continuous affine minorants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous affine minorant of a proper function is a continuous affine function lying below it at every point. It is exact at a point when it also matches the function there. Exact minorization is the subgradient inequality. Every proper lower-semicontinuous convex function on a Hilbert space has at least one continuous affine minorant; at every interior point of its domain it has an exact one. The function itself is the pointwise supremum of all these affine minorants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a(y)=\langle y,u\rangle+\alpha\) minorizes \(f\) exactly when \(a\leq f\); it is exact at \(x\) exactly when \(f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle y-x,u\rangle\) for all \(y\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(f\) has an affine minorant with slope \(u\) iff \(f-\langle\cdot,u\rangle\) is bounded below.
Exact affine minorization at \(x\) is equivalent to \(u\in\partial f(x)\).
special_cases_latex: A differentiable convex function has the exact affine minorant \(y\mapsto f(x)+\langle y-x,\nabla f(x)\rangle\).
For \(f=\iota_C\), exact affine minorants at \(x\in C\) correspond to normal vectors to \(C\) at \(x\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A proper lower-semicontinuous convex function is bounded below on every bounded subset of \(H\).
For \(f\in\Gamma_0(H)\), \(f=\sup\{a:a\text{ is a continuous affine minorant of }f\}\).
boundary_notes: Exact affine minorants need not exist at arbitrary boundary points of the effective domain.
A discontinuous linear functional on an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space can have no continuous affine minorant.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine-envelope representation of closed proper convex functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine-support representation and its linear-support specialization for sublinear functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proper, lower-semicontinuous convex function f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}} is the pointwise supremum of its affine supports and, if \operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\ne\varnothing, has an affine support at every x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f). Equivalently, f is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex iff it is the pointwise supremum of a nonempty family of affine functions and is not identically +\infty. For a proper lower-semicontinuous sublinear function the supporting affine functions may be taken linear; conversely, the pointwise supremum of any nonempty family of linear functions, provided it is not identically +\infty, is proper, lower semicontinuous, and sublinear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every proper closed convex function is the upper envelope of all its affine lower supports, with a support at every interior domain point. Conversely, any nonempty affine envelope that is not identically positive infinity is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. In the sublinear case the supports are linear, and nontrivial suprema of linear functions give exactly such functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is proper, lsc, and convex}\iff f=\sup_{i\in I}(\langle a_i,\cdot\rangle+b_i)\text{ for a nonempty family and }f\not\equiv+\infty.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed realization of a convex function operation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(\Phi\) be an operation producing an extended-real function from inputs \((f_i)_{i\in I}\), and let \(\breve g\) denote the lower-semicontinuous convex envelope of \(g\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of closure calculus as post-operation closed convex regularization; exact commutation laws require operation-specific qualification conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The closed realization of a function operation \(\Phi\) is defined by \[\overline{\Phi}(f_i:i\in I)=\breve{\bigl(\Phi(f_i:i\in I)\bigr)}.\] Thus \(\overline{\Phi}\) is the greatest lower-semicontinuous convex function lying below the raw output \(\Phi(f_i)\). For pointwise supremum, closure is unnecessary when every input is lower semicontinuous and convex: \[\sup_{i\in I}f_i\in\Gamma(H).\] For positive finite sums with compatible proper domains, the sum is likewise closed and convex. For operations involving infima, infimal convolution, linear images, or marginalization, the raw output can fail to be lower semicontinuous; its canonical closed value is therefore its envelope \(\breve{\Phi(f_i)}\), equivalently its biconjugate when a continuous affine minorant exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given any operation on extended-real functions, its closed realization is obtained by applying the lower-semicontinuous convex envelope to the operation's raw output. This produces the largest closed convex function below that output. Pointwise suprema of closed convex functions are already closed and convex, and compatible finite positive sums are also closed. Infimum-type operations, infimal convolutions, images, and marginal functions may lose closedness, so closure must generally be applied unless a qualification condition guarantees exact preservation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\overline{\Phi}(f_i)=\breve{\Phi(f_i)}\) defines the closure calculus for \(\Phi\); when \(\Phi(f_i)\in\Gamma(H)\), \(\overline{\Phi}(f_i)=\Phi(f_i)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\Phi(f_i)\) has a continuous affine minorant, then \(\overline{\Phi}(f_i)=\Phi(f_i)^{**}\).
Epigraphically, the closed realization replaces the raw epigraph by its closed convex hull under the standard properness conditions.
special_cases_latex: For \(g=\sup_i f_i\) with \(f_i\in\Gamma(H)\), \(\breve g=g\).
For a finite positive sum of lower-semicontinuous convex functions with nonempty common domain, the raw sum is lower semicontinuous and convex.
immediate_consequences_latex: Closed realization is idempotent: \(\breve{\breve g}=\breve g\).
No closure correction occurs precisely when the raw output is already lower semicontinuous and convex.
boundary_notes: Closure does not generally commute with infimum, image, or infimal convolution without additional assumptions.
The definition records the canonical regularized output and does not assert an unconditional algebraic identity between separate closures and the closure of an operation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epigraphic Closure and Convex Closure of a Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines function closure and closed convex closure epigraphically and records the closedness and domain gaps possible before closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(f:X\to[-\infty,\infty]\). The closure \(\operatorname{cl}f\) is defined by \(\operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{cl}f)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{epi}f)\), equivalently \((\operatorname{cl}f)(x)=\inf\{w\mid (x,w)\in\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{epi}f)\}\). The convex closure \(\overline{\operatorname{co}}f\) is defined by \(\operatorname{epi}(\overline{\operatorname{co}}f)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{epi}f))\). If \(F(x)=\inf\{w\mid (x,w)\in\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{epi}f)\}\), then \(F\) is convex and \(\operatorname{cl}F=\overline{\operatorname{co}}f\). The function \(F\) need not be closed, and \(\operatorname{dom}F\) may be strictly contained in \(\operatorname{dom}(\overline{\operatorname{co}}f)\), although their domain closures coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing an epigraph defines the closure of a function, while closing the convex hull of the epigraph defines its convex closure. The function generated by the unclosed convex hull is convex but may be nonclosed and may have a smaller domain, although the two domain closures coincide.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{cl}f)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{epi}f),\quad \operatorname{epi}(\overline{\operatorname{co}}f)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{epi}f)),\quad \operatorname{cl}F=\overline{\operatorname{co}}f,\quad \operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{dom}F)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{dom}(\overline{\operatorname{co}}f)).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K be a simple proper concave-convex function on \mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}^n. Then \operatorname{cl}_2\operatorname{cl}_1K\sim\operatorname{cl}_1\operatorname{cl}_2K,\qquad \operatorname{cl}_2\operatorname{cl}_1K\leq\operatorname{cl}_1\operatorname{cl}_2K. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugates of Linear Images and Precompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Here Af denotes the infimal image of f under A, gA=g\circ A, and A^*g^* denotes the infimal image of g^* under the adjoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m be linear. For every convex f on \mathbb{R}^n, (Af)^*=f^*\circ A^*. For every convex g on \mathbb{R}^m, ((\operatorname{cl}g)\circ A)^*=\operatorname{cl}(A^*g^*). If A^{-1}(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g))\neq\varnothing, then (g\circ A)^*=A^*g^* and, for every x^*,\quad (g\circ A)^*(x^*)=\inf\{g^*(y^*):A^*y^*=x^*\}, where the infimum is attained unless its value is +\infty vacuously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of a convex function's linear image is its conjugate composed with the adjoint. The conjugate of a precomposition by a linear map is the closed infimal adjoint image of the conjugate. If the range of the map meets the relative interior of the function's domain, closure is unnecessary and the fiberwise infimum is attained, except for the vacuous positive-infinity case.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Variablewise Closures of a Concave-Convex Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines convex closure in the second variable, concave closure in the first variable, and the associated closedness terminology.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K be a concave-convex function on \mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}^n. The convex closure of K in its second variable, denoted \operatorname{cl}_vK or \operatorname{cl}_2K, is obtained by closing v\mapsto K(u,v) as a convex function for each fixed u. The concave closure of K in its first variable, denoted \operatorname{cl}_uK or \operatorname{cl}_1K, is obtained by closing u\mapsto K(u,v) as a concave function for each fixed v. The function K is convex-closed when K=\operatorname{cl}_2K and concave-closed when K=\operatorname{cl}_1K.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The second-variable closure closes every convex slice obtained by fixing the first variable, while the first-variable closure closes every concave slice obtained by fixing the second variable. Equality with the corresponding closure defines convex-closedness or concave-closedness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{cl}_2K:=\operatorname{cl}_vK,\qquad \operatorname{cl}_1K:=\operatorname{cl}_uK;\qquad K\text{ is convex-closed}\iff K=\operatorname{cl}_2K,\quad K\text{ is concave-closed}\iff K=\operatorname{cl}_1K.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure commutes with qualified linear precomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The relative-interior range qualification is retained as an essential hypothesis of the closure identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^m\to[-\infty,\infty]\) be convex, and let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) satisfy \[\operatorname{range}(A)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\neq\varnothing.\] Define \(F:\mathbb R^n\to[-\infty,\infty]\) by \(F(x)=f(Ax)\). Then \(F\) is convex and \[(\operatorname{cl}F)(x)=(\operatorname{cl}f)(Ax)\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear precomposition preserves convexity. When the linear range meets the relative interior of the effective domain, epigraphic closure commutes with that precomposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is convex and }\operatorname{cl}(f\circ A)=(\operatorname{cl}f)\circ A

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support Functions of Minkowski Sums and Intersections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function specialization of sum–infimal-convolution conjugacy for nonempty convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let C_1,\ldots,C_m\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be nonempty convex sets. Then \sigma_{C_1+\cdots+C_m}=\sigma_{C_1}+\cdots+\sigma_{C_m} and \sigma_{\operatorname{cl}C_1\cap\cdots\cap\operatorname{cl}C_m}=\operatorname{cl}(\sigma_{C_1}\square\cdots\square\sigma_{C_m}). If \bigcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{ri}C_i\neq\varnothing, closure can be omitted in the second identity and, for every x^*,\quad \sigma_{C_1\cap\cdots\cap C_m}(x^*)=\inf_{x_1^*+\cdots+x_m^*=x^*}\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_{C_i}(x_i^*), with the infimum attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support function of a Minkowski sum is the sum of the individual support functions. The support function of the intersection of the closed sets is the closed infimal convolution of their support functions. If the sets' relative interiors have a common point, closure is unnecessary and the decomposition infimum is attained for every dual vector.
assumptions_latex: C_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is nonempty and convex for }i=1,\ldots,m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sigma_{\sum_i C_i}=\sum_i\sigma_{C_i},\qquad \sigma_{\bigcap_i\operatorname{cl}C_i}=\operatorname{cl}(\square_i\sigma_{C_i}),\qquad \sigma_{\bigcap_i C_i}(x^*)=\min_{\sum_i x_i^*=x^*}\sum_i\sigma_{C_i}(x_i^*)\text{ under the stated qualification}.

The support function of an inverse image of a set's closure is the closed infimal adjoint image of the original support function. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epigraphic closure and convex closure of an extended-real function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines closure by closing the epigraph and convex closure by taking the closed convex hull of the epigraph; it also records the nonclosed intermediate convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(f:X\to[-\infty,\infty]\). Define the closure \(\operatorname{cl}f:\mathbb R^n\to[-\infty,\infty]\) by \[(\operatorname{cl}f)(x)=\inf\{w\in\mathbb R:(x,w)\in\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{epi}f)\}.\] Then \(\operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{cl}f)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{epi}f)\); if \(f\) is convex, \(\operatorname{cl}f\) is closed and convex. The convex closure \(\overline{\operatorname{co}}f\) is defined by \[\operatorname{epi}(\overline{\operatorname{co}}f)=\operatorname{cl}\!\left(\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{epi}f)\right).\] If \[F(x)=\inf\{w\in\mathbb R:(x,w)\in\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{epi}f)\},\] then \(F\) is convex and \(\overline{\operatorname{co}}f=\operatorname{cl}F\). The function \(F\) need not be closed, and \(\operatorname{dom}F\) may be strictly contained in \(\operatorname{dom}(\overline{\operatorname{co}}f)\), although their domain closures coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing a function's epigraph defines its closure, while closing the convex hull of its epigraph defines its convex closure. The function induced by the unclosed convex hull is convex but may be nonclosed and may have a strictly smaller domain than its closure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{cl}f)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{epi}f),\qquad \operatorname{epi}(\overline{\operatorname{co}}f)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{epi}f))

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local convex continuity and boundedness regimes
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, and fix \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise Hilbert-space correspondence for proper convex functions; local boundedness means boundedness on a norm neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The following four local regularity conditions at \(x_0\) define the same regime: \[(i)\ f\text{ is locally Lipschitz near }x_0;\qquad (ii)\ f\text{ is continuous at }x_0;\] \[(iii)\ f\text{ is bounded on a neighborhood of }x_0;\qquad (iv)\ f\text{ is bounded above on a neighborhood of }x_0.\] Explicitly, condition (iv) means that there exist \(\rho>0\) and \(M\in\mathbb R\) such that \(f(x)\leq M\) for every \(x\in B(x_0;\rho)\). Local Lipschitz continuity means that there exist \(r>0\) and \(L\geq0\) such that \[|f(x)-f(y)|\leq L\|x-y\|\qquad(x,y\in B(x_0;r)).\] If these equivalent conditions hold at one point, then \(f\) is locally Lipschitz throughout \(\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom}f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper convex function on a Hilbert space, four pointwise notions coincide: local Lipschitz continuity, continuity, boundedness on a neighborhood, and boundedness above on a neighborhood. Local upper boundedness requires one finite upper bound on some norm ball around the point. Local Lipschitz continuity requires a uniform Lipschitz constant on a possibly smaller ball. Once this regime occurs, the function is locally Lipschitz at every point in the interior of its effective domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(x_0\), local Lipschitz continuity, continuity, local boundedness, and local upper boundedness of proper convex \(f\) are equivalent.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x_0\in\operatorname{cont}f\iff(\exists\rho>0)\;\sup_{B(x_0;\rho)}f<+\infty\).
Under any equivalent condition, \(x_0\in\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom}f\).
special_cases_latex: If \(f\in\Gamma_0(H)\), then \(\operatorname{cont}f=\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom}f\).
In finite dimensions, every proper convex function is continuous on \(\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom}f\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A locally upper-bounded convex function is automatically locally bounded below as well.
On compact subsets of the relative interior in finite dimensions, a proper convex function is Lipschitz.
boundary_notes: The correspondence is local and does not imply a global Lipschitz constant.
At boundary points of the effective domain, local boundedness and continuity can fail.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuity on the relative interior of the effective domain
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex. Let \(A=\operatorname{aff}(\operatorname{dom}f)\), equipped with the relative Euclidean topology.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional intrinsic-domain continuity; relative continuity is continuity of the restriction to the affine hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The relative interior of the effective domain is \[\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)=\{x\in\operatorname{dom}f:(\exists\varepsilon>0)\;B(x;\varepsilon)\cap A\subset\operatorname{dom}f\}.\] The function \(f\) is relatively continuous at \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) when its restriction \(f|_A:A\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is continuous at \(x\). Every proper convex function on \(\mathbb R^n\) is finite and relatively continuous at each \(x\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\). More strongly, for every nonempty compact \(K\subset\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\), there exists \(L_K\geq0\) such that \[|f(x)-f(y)|\leq L_K\|x-y\|\qquad(x,y\in K).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relative interior of the effective domain consists of points having a neighborhood inside the domain when neighborhoods are taken within the domain's affine hull. Relative continuity means ordinary continuity after restricting the function to that affine hull. Every proper finite-dimensional convex function is relatively continuous throughout the relative interior of its effective domain and is Lipschitz on each compact subset contained there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f|_A\) is continuous on \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\), and it is Lipschitz on every compact subset of that relative interior.
equivalent_formulations_latex: After identifying \(A\) with a Euclidean space of dimension \(\dim A\), relative-interior continuity becomes ordinary interior continuity.
\(x\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\) iff some relative ball \(B(x;\varepsilon)\cap A\) lies in \(\operatorname{dom}f\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\operatorname{aff}(\operatorname{dom}f)=\mathbb R^n\), then \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\).
If \(f\) is real-valued on \(\mathbb R^n\), then it is continuous everywhere.
immediate_consequences_latex: A lower-dimensional effective domain does not obstruct continuity when the correct relative topology is used.
All discontinuities of a proper finite-dimensional convex function are confined to the relative boundary of its domain.
boundary_notes: Relative continuity does not imply ambient continuity when the affine hull is a proper subspace and the function equals \(+\infty\) off that subspace.
No continuity conclusion is asserted at relative-boundary points.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuity and radial recovery of a convex function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuity on the ambient interior of the effective domain, recovery of the closure along interior-to-point segments, and additional relative continuity under lower semicontinuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) be convex. Then \(f\) is continuous on \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\), agrees there with \(\operatorname{cl}f\), and \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}(\operatorname{cl}f))\). The functions also both equal \(+\infty\) outside \(\operatorname{dom}(\operatorname{cl}f)\), hence outside \(\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{dom}f)\). If \(x_0\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\), then for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[(\operatorname{cl}f)(x)=\lim_{\tau\nearrow1}f((1-\tau)x_0+\tau x).\] If, in addition, \(f\) is lower semicontinuous, then its restriction is continuous relative to the convex hull of every finite subset of \(\operatorname{dom}f\), in particular relative to every line segment contained in its domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex function is continuous on the interior of its effective domain and coincides there with its closure. Its closure can be recovered by approaching any point radially from an interior-domain point. If the function is lower semicontinuous, it is also relatively continuous on every finite-domain convex hull, especially on domain line segments.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is lower semicontinuous for the finite-hull continuity conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is continuous on }\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f),\quad f=\operatorname{cl}f\text{ there},\quad \operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}(\operatorname{cl}f)),\quad (\operatorname{cl}f)(x)=\lim_{\tau\nearrow1}f((1-\tau)x_0+\tau x)
