children.title: Quadratic Growth
children.top_down_role: Second-order growth relative to a minimizer set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Growth Does Not Imply Strong Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the converse from quadratic growth to strong convexity or uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x_1,x_2)=x_1^2\) on \(\mathbb R^2\), the minimizer set is \(S=\{0\}\times\mathbb R\) and \[f(x)-\min f=\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2.\] Thus \(f\) has global quadratic growth with \(\alpha=2\) under the convention \((\alpha/2)\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\), but it is neither strictly nor strongly convex and has nonunique minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Squared distance to a line has exact quadratic growth but is flat along its minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)-f^*=\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\), while \(f\) is not strongly convex and \(S\) is not a singleton.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Growth Does Not Imply Strong Convexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Growth Implies a Subgradient Residual Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order residual consequence of quadratic growth for proper closed convex functions on a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f(x)-f^*\ge(\alpha/2)\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\) on a region containing \(S\). Then every point \(x\) in that region and every \(g\in\partial f(x)\) satisfy \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\frac{2}{\alpha}\lVert g\rVert.\] Equivalently, \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le(2/\alpha)\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\) whenever the subdifferential is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex quadratic growth converts small subgradient residual into a quantitative distance bound to the solution set.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex on a Hilbert space.
Quadratic growth with modulus \(\alpha>0\) holds on the stated region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le(2/\alpha)\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\) at points with nonempty subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Growth Implies a Subgradient Residual Bound

assumptions_latex: \(f:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on a Hilbert space.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)-f^*\geq(\alpha/2)\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^2\)

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) has quadratic growth on \(C\) with constant \(\alpha>0\) if, for every \(x\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}f\), \[ f(x)-f^*\geq\frac{\alpha}{2}\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^2. \] A local quadratic-growth condition at the solution set requires the same inequality only for points satisfying \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\leq r\), for some \(r>0\). The definition concerns growth away from the entire minimizer set and does not require the minimizer to be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic growth lower-bounds objective suboptimality by a positive multiple of squared distance to the complete minimizer set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic growth about a minimizer set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a normed space, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) have finite attained minimum \(f_*\), and let \(S=\operatorname{argmin}f\ne\varnothing\). Let \(U\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\) contain \(S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued quadratic growth; global or local scope is determined by U.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) satisfies quadratic growth with modulus \(\mu>0\) on \(U\) if \[f(x)-f_*\geq\frac{\mu}{2}\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\qquad\text{for every }x\in U.\] The best quadratic-growth modulus on \(U\) is \[\mu_U^{\mathrm{qg}}=\inf_{x\in U\setminus S}\frac{2(f(x)-f_*)}{\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2},\] with the convention that the infimum is \(+\infty\) when \(U\setminus S\) is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic growth requires the objective gap to dominate one half of a positive constant times the squared distance to the full solution set. The best modulus is the infimum of the resulting gap-to-squared-distance ratio.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in U:\quad f(x)\geq f_*+\frac\mu2\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inequality is equivalently the objective-gap error bound \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\sqrt{2(f(x)-f_*)/\mu}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(S=\{x_*\}\), the right-hand side becomes \(f_*+\frac\mu2\|x-x_*\|^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Quadratic growth makes every sufficiently small objective gap quantitatively control distance to the solution set.
boundary_notes: Quadratic growth is weaker than strong convexity because it compares only with the minimizer set.
The factor \(1/2\) is a normalization convention.
review_flags: No inspected source provided the precise set-valued quadratic-growth definition and best-modulus formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic growth about a minimizer set

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Power-type objective growth of order p
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a normed space, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) attain its finite minimum \(f_*\), let \(S=\operatorname{argmin}f\ne\varnothing\), and let \(U\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\) contain \(S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponent-parameterized growth relative to a possibly non-singleton solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p>0\) and \(c>0\), the function \(f\) has power-type growth of order \(p\) with constant \(c\) on \(U\) if \[f(x)-f_*\geq c\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^p\qquad(x\in U).\] Its best order-\(p\) constant is \[c_{p,U}=\inf_{x\in U\setminus S}\frac{f(x)-f_*}{\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^p}.\] The exponent, constant, norm, solution set, and localization set are all part of the declared growth class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Power growth of order \(p\) means that the objective gap dominates a positive constant times the \(p\)-th power of distance to the minimizer set throughout a specified region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in U:\quad f(x)-f_*\geq c\,\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^p.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The condition is equivalently \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq c^{-1/p}(f(x)-f_*)^{1/p}\) on \(U\).
special_cases_latex: Order \(p=1\) is sharp growth.
Order \(p=2\) is quadratic growth, with \(c=\mu/2\) under the common quadratic normalization.
immediate_consequences_latex: An objective accuracy \(f(x)-f_*\leq\varepsilon\) implies \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq(\varepsilon/c)^{1/p}\).
boundary_notes: Comparisons between different exponents depend on whether distances are below or above one.
Exponents below one may be incompatible with common convex interior geometries and therefore require explicit scope.

notation.meaning: best power-growth constant for exponent p on U

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) satisfies a Hölderian growth error bound on \(U\) with exponent \(\theta\in(0,1]\) if, for every \(x\in U\cap\operatorname{dom}f\), \[ \operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\leq c\bigl(f(x)-f^*\bigr)^\theta. \] Equivalently, with \(p=1/\theta\) and \(\kappa=c^{-1/\theta}\), one has \(f(x)-f^*\geq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^p\). children.title: Growth Exponent Regimes
children.top_down_role: Qualitative regimes arising from different growth exponents.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sublinear Exponents Are Excluded at Accessible Isolated Convex Minima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex lower boundary for growth exponents; isolated-domain degeneracies are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex on a normed space. Suppose \(\bar x\) is an isolated minimizer and \(\operatorname{dom}f\) contains a point distinct from \(\bar x\). For every \(0<p<1\), there are no \(\kappa,\varepsilon>0\) such that \[f(x)-f(\bar x)\geq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname*{argmin}f)^p\] for all \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\cap B_\varepsilon(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a nontrivially accessible isolated minimizer of a convex function, local power growth cannot have exponent below one.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{dom}f\) contains a point distinct from \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No local bound \(f-f^*\geq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,S)^p\) with \(\kappa>0\) can hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Sublinear Exponents Are Excluded at Accessible Isolated Convex Minima

assumptions_latex: \(X^*\neq\varnothing\), and \(0<\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\leq r\) on the local comparison region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_1\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^{p_1}\geq\kappa_1r^{p_1-p_2}\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^{p_2}\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local ordering and interpretation of power-growth exponents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On the region \(d(x)\leq r\), exponents are ordered by \[ d(x)^{p_1}\geq r^{p_1-p_2}d(x)^{p_2}\qquad(0<p_1<p_2). \] Hence power growth of the smaller order \(p_1\) implies local power growth of every larger order \(p_2\), after rescaling the modulus. Near \(X^*\), smaller exponents therefore express stronger growth. This ordering is only local: for \(d(x)>1\), the ordering of powers reverses, so exponent comparison alone does not yield a global implication on an unbounded domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near the solution set, smaller growth exponents are stronger and imply larger exponents; on unbounded domains, powers reverse order at large distances.
knowledge_statements.title: Growth Exponent Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local ordering of powers is correct and appropriately recorded as a property, but the claimed regime interpretation lacks cited evidence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sublinear Growth Exponents Are Excluded at Accessible Isolated Convex Minima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity boundary for exponents below one; degenerate isolated-domain cases are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex on a normed space, let \(\bar x\) be an isolated minimizer, and suppose there exists \(y\in\operatorname{dom}f\setminus\{\bar x\}\). Then no constants \(\kappa,\\varepsilon>0\) and exponent \(0<p<1\) can satisfy \[ f(x)-f(\bar x)\geq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname*{argmin}f)^p \] for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\cap B_\varepsilon(\bar x)\). Indeed, along \(x_t=(1-t)\bar x+ty\), convexity makes the objective gap at most linear in \(t\), whereas isolation makes the distance to the solution set proportional to \(t\); for \(p<1\), the proposed lower bound is asymptotically larger than linear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a nontrivially accessible isolated minimizer of a convex function, local power growth cannot have exponent below one.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{dom}f\) contains a point distinct from \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No local lower bound \(f-f^*\geq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,S)^p\) with \(\kappa>0\) can hold.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global, neighborhood-local, and level-set-local growth
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) attain its finite minimum \(f_*\) on a metric space \((X,d)\), let \(S=\operatorname{argmin}f\ne\varnothing\), and let \(\omega:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty]\) vanish at zero.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition distinguishes only the quantification region; it does not change the growth modulus itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The growth inequality \(f(x)-f_*\geq\omega(d(x,S))\) is global if it holds for all \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\). It is neighborhood-local if there exists \(r>0\) such that it holds whenever \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(d(x,S)<r\). It is level-set-local if there exists \(\delta>0\) such that it holds whenever \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(f(x)\leq f_*+\delta\). The constants \(r\) or \(\delta\) belong to the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A growth condition is global when quantified over the entire effective domain, neighborhood-local when restricted to a metric tube around the solution set, and level-set-local when restricted to a sufficiently low objective sublevel set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[\begin{aligned}\text{global: }&x\in\operatorname{dom}f,\\\text{neighborhood-local: }&d(x,S)<r,\\\text{level-set-local: }&f(x)-f_*\leq\delta,
\end{aligned}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad f(x)-f_*\geq\omega(d(x,S)).\]
special_cases_latex: For \(\omega(t)=ct^p\), these regimes give global, local, and sublevel-local power growth.
immediate_consequences_latex: A global certificate is automatically valid in every neighborhood and sublevel restriction.
A level-set-local certificate controls all sufficiently accurate objective approximations.
boundary_notes: Neighborhood-local and level-set-local regimes need not coincide without continuity or compactness assumptions.
The localization radius may be uniform around the whole solution set or pointwise; this record uses the uniform setwise version.
review_flags: No inspected source stated this three-way localization taxonomy with the same uniform conventions.
knowledge_statements.title: Global, neighborhood-local, and level-set-local growth

A global growth regime with growth function \(\omega:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty)\) holds when \(\omega(0)=0\), \(\omega(t)>0\) for every \(t>0\), and
\[
f(x)-f^*\geq \omega\!\left(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\right)
\quad\text{for every }x\in\operatorname{dom}f.
\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Local Quadratic Growth Without Global Quadratic Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth convex separation of local and global quadratic-growth regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\sqrt{1+x^2}-1\) on \(\mathbb R\), \(\operatorname*{argmin}f=\{0\}\) and, when \(|x|\le1\), \[f(x)=\frac{x^2}{\sqrt{1+x^2}+1}\ge\frac{x^2}{\sqrt2+1}.\] Hence local quadratic growth holds. However, \(\lim_{|x|\to\infty}f(x)/x^2=0\), so no positive global quadratic-growth modulus exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The function square-root of one plus x squared, minus one, is locally quadratic at its minimizer but only linear at infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local quadratic growth holds at \(0\), but \(\inf_{x\ne0}f(x)/x^2=0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak sharpness of a minimizer set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a normed space, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) have finite attained minimum \(f_*\), let \(S=\operatorname{argmin}f\ne\varnothing\), and let \(U\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\) contain \(S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order, set-valued sharp growth; uniqueness is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The solution set \(S\) is weakly sharp for \(f\) on \(U\) with modulus \(\alpha>0\) if \[f(x)-f_*\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\qquad\text{for every }x\in U.\] The best sharpness modulus is \[\alpha_U=\inf_{x\in U\setminus S}\frac{f(x)-f_*}{\operatorname{dist}(x,S)}.\] When \(S=\{x_*\}\), this is isolated sharpness of \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak sharpness is linear objective growth away from the minimizer set. It permits multiple minimizers and measures transverse separation from the entire solution set rather than from a selected minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in U:\quad f(x)\geq f_*+\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inequality is equivalently the Lipschitz objective-gap error bound \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq(f(x)-f_*)/\alpha\).
special_cases_latex: For a singleton solution set, \(f(x)-f(x_*)\geq\alpha\|x-x_*\|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every point with objective gap at most \(\varepsilon\) lies within distance \(\varepsilon/\alpha\) of \(S\).
boundary_notes: Weak sharpness does not mean differentiability or strong convexity.
The adjective weak refers to allowing a non-singleton solution set, not to a smaller positive modulus.

\quad\text{for every }x\in D\cap\operatorname{dom}f.
\]
The property is global when \(D=X\), and local when \(D\) is a neighborhood of \(S\). The definition permits multiple minimizers and measures sharpness relative to the entire set \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak sharpness means that the objective gap grows at least linearly with distance to the possibly non-singleton minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Sharp Minima

source_witnesses.locator: 10 Convex Functions: Variants p. 177
source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Growth Is Not Weak Sharpness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical failure of local and global linear growth for a smooth convex minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(x)=x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\), \(S=\{0\}\), but
\[
\inf_{x\ne0}\frac{f(x)-\min f}{\operatorname{dist}(x,S)}
=\inf_{x\ne0}|x|=0.
\]
Moreover, the same infimum is zero after restriction to any neighborhood of zero. Thus no \(\alpha>0\) gives local or global weak sharpness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic minimum is not weakly sharp because its objective gap is second order rather than linear near the solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maximal local and global weak-sharpness moduli at \(S=\{0\}\) are zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Growth Is Not Weak Sharpness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Regional Weak-Sharpness Modulus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best modulus on a fixed region, encompassing the global case and any specified local region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\), let \(f^*=\min f\), and let \(D\supseteq S\). Then
\[
\alpha_D:=\sup\{\alpha\geq0:f(x)-f^*\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\ \forall x\in D\cap\operatorname{dom}f\}
=\inf_{x\in(D\cap\operatorname{dom}f)\setminus S}
\frac{f(x)-f^*}{\operatorname{dist}(x,S)},
\]
where the infimum of the empty set is \(+\infty\). Weak sharpness on \(D\) holds with a positive modulus exactly when \(\alpha_D>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On any fixed region, the best weak-sharpness constant is the infimum of objective gap divided by distance to the minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_D=\inf_{x\in(D\cap\operatorname{dom}f)\setminus S}(f(x)-f^*)/\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\), and positive weak sharpness on \(D\) is equivalent to \(\alpha_D>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Regional Weak-Sharpness Modulus

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Weak-Sharpness Modulus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximal global modulus expressed as the minimum normalized objective growth away from the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper with nonempty minimizer set \(S\) and minimum \(f^*\). The maximal global weak-sharpness modulus is
\[
\alpha_*:=\sup\{\alpha\geq0:f(x)-f^*\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\ \forall x\}
=\inf_{x\in\operatorname{dom}f\setminus S}
\frac{f(x)-f^*}{\operatorname{dist}(x,S)},
\]
with the infimum of the empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). Positive global weak sharpness holds exactly when \(\alpha_*>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The best weak-sharpness constant is the infimum of the objective gap divided by distance to the minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_*=\inf_{x\in\operatorname{dom}f\setminus S}(f(x)-f^*)/\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\), and weak sharpness holds with a positive modulus exactly when \(\alpha_*>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Weak-Sharpness Modulus

children.title: Isolated Sharp Minima
children.top_down_role: Sharpness centered on isolated solutions.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space, and \(\alpha>0\) and \(r>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) is an isolated sharp minimizer when \(f(x)-f(\bar x)\geq\alpha\lVert x-\bar x\rVert\) for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) satisfying \(\lVert x-\bar x\rVert<r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local linear growth centered at one solution.

source_refs.locator: 10 Convex Functions: Variants p. 177

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A point \(\bar x\) is an isolated sharp minimizer of \(f\) if there exist \(\alpha>0\) and \(r>0\) such that
\[
f(x)-f(\bar x)\geq \alpha\lVert x-\bar x\rVert
\quad\text{whenever }x\in\operatorname{dom}f
\text{ and }\lVert x-\bar x\rVert<r.
\]
This inequality implies that \(\bar x\) is the unique minimizer in the open ball of radius \(r\), although other minimizers may exist outside that ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An isolated sharp minimizer has a local linear objective increase in every direction away from that single solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Isolated Sharp Minima

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Local Sharpness Globalizes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global consequence of a locally isolated sharp minimum under convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be convex on a normed space. If \[f(x)-f(\bar x)\ge\alpha\lVert x-\bar x\rVert\] for every domain point satisfying \(\lVert x-\bar x\rVert<r\), where \(\alpha,r>0\), then the same inequality holds for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\). Consequently, \(\operatorname*{argmin}f=\{\bar x\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex objective, locally isolated sharpness extends globally and forces a unique global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on a normed space.
The centered sharp-growth inequality holds on some ball about \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)-f(\bar x)\ge\alpha\lVert x-\bar x\rVert\) globally and \(\operatorname*{argmin}f=\{\bar x\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Local Sharpness Globalizes

children.title: Subdifferential Sharpness Certificates
children.top_down_role: First-order certificate families associated with sharp minimizer geometry.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional-Derivative Sharpness Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional directional characterization of global weak sharpness for a convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\). For \(\alpha>0\),
\[
f(x)-\min f\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\quad(\forall x)
\]
holds if and only if
\[
f'(s;d)\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(d,T_S(s))
\quad(\forall s\in S,\ d\in\mathbb R^n).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global weak sharpness is equivalent to each directional derivative at a minimizer dominating the direction's distance from the tangent cone.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f-\min f\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,S)\) globally if and only if \(f'(s;d)\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(d,T_S(s))\) for all \(s\in S\) and \(d\in\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: one-sided directional derivative of f at s in direction d
tangent cone to S at s

knowledge_statements.title: Directional-Derivative Sharpness Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subgradient-Norm Consequence of Weak Sharpness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary first-order residual separation outside the minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\), and suppose
\[
f(x)-\min f\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n
\]
for some \(\alpha>0\). Then every \(x\notin S\) and every \(g\in\partial f(x)\) satisfy
\[
\|g\|\geq\alpha.
\]
Consequently, if \(\partial f(x)\neq\varnothing\), then \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\geq\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under global weak sharpness, every subgradient outside the solution set has norm at least the sharpness modulus.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\notin S\) and \(g\in\partial f(x)\), \(\|g\|\geq\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient-Norm Consequence of Weak Sharpness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Centered-Ball Subdifferential Certificate for a Sharp Minimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional first-order certificate for global linear growth away from a single minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, let \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\), and let \(B\) be the closed Euclidean unit ball. For \(\alpha>0\),
\[
f(x)\ge f(\bar x)+\alpha\|x-\bar x\|\quad(\forall x\in\mathbb R^n)
\]
holds if and only if
\[
\alpha B\subseteq\partial f(\bar x).
\]
Consequently, some positive modulus exists exactly when \(0\in\operatorname{int}\partial f(\bar x)\), and the largest admissible modulus is \(\sup\{r\ge0:rB\subseteq\partial f(\bar x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global linear growth from a minimizer is equivalent to its subdifferential containing a centered ball, whose inradius is the best sharpness modulus.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(B\) is the closed Euclidean unit ball and \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)\ge f(\bar x)+\alpha\|x-\bar x\|\) for every \(x\) if and only if \(\alpha B\subseteq\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Centered-Ball Subdifferential Certificate for a Sharp Minimizer

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\), and \(B\) is the closed Euclidean unit ball.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global weak sharpness with modulus \(\alpha\) is equivalent to \(\alpha(B\cap N_S(s))\subseteq\partial f(s)\) for every \(s\in S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex certificate for global weak sharpness.

source_refs.locator: 9.2 Proper Lower Semicontinuous Convex Functions p. 160
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\alpha>0\), the global weak-sharpness inequality
\[
f(x)-\min f\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)
\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n
\]
is equivalent to the pointwise first-order inclusions
\[
\alpha\bigl(B\cap N_S(s)\bigr)\subseteq\partial f(s)
\quad\text{for every }s\in S.
\]
Thus each unit normal direction to the solution set, scaled by \(\alpha\), must be supported by a subgradient at the corresponding minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak sharpness is certified when every scaled unit normal to the solution set is a subgradient at the corresponding minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Subdifferential Sharpness Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform nonzero-subgradient certificate for sharpness
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional normed space, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(S=\operatorname{argmin}f\ne\varnothing\). Let \(U\subseteq\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) contain \(S\), and define \(r_{\partial f}(x)=\operatorname{dist}_*(0,\partial f(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex subdifferential residual certificate away from the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) has a subdifferential sharpness certificate with modulus \(\alpha>0\) on \(U\) if \[\operatorname{dist}_*(0,\partial f(x))\geq\alpha\qquad\text{for every }x\in U\setminus S.\] Its certificate modulus is \[\alpha_{\partial,U}=\inf_{x\in U\setminus S}\operatorname{dist}_*(0,\partial f(x)).\] At solution points, convex optimality gives \(0\in\partial f(x)\), so the certificate is intentionally imposed only off \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subdifferential sharpness certificate is a uniform positive lower bound on the smallest dual norm of a subgradient at every nonsolution point in the declared region. At minimizers the residual is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x\in U\setminus S\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \inf_{v\in\partial f(x)}\|v\|_*\geq\alpha.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The condition is \(\inf_{x\in U\setminus S}r_{\partial f}(x)>0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(f\) is differentiable away from \(S\), the residual becomes \(\|\nabla f(x)\|_*\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The certificate rules out sequences of nonsolution points in \(U\) whose minimal subgradient norms converge to zero.
boundary_notes: For merely local sharpness, U must be restricted accordingly.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(f\) is polyhedral convex and attains its minimum, then its minimizer set \(S\) is polyhedral and there exists a constant \(\alpha>0\) such that

f(x)-\min f\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)
\quad\text{for every }x\in\operatorname{dom}f.
\]
Hence the finitely many affine pieces defining the epigraph induce a uniform global linear-growth modulus relative to the entire solution set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual error bound for a solution set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a metric space, let \(S\subseteq X\) be nonempty and closed, and let \(R:X\to[0,+\infty]\) be a residual satisfying \(R(x)=0\) exactly when \(x\in S\). Let \(U\subseteq X\) contain \(S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract error-bound definition encompassing objective, stationarity, composite, and feasibility residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The residual \(R\) provides an error bound for \(S\) on \(U\) with modulus \(\eta:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty]\) if \(\eta(0)=0\) and \[d(x,S)\leq\eta(R(x))\qquad\text{for every }x\in U.\] A linear error bound has \(\eta(t)=\kappa t\) for some \(\kappa>0\), while a Hölder error bound has \(\eta(t)=\kappa t^\theta\) with \(\theta\in(0,1]\). The residual, solution set, region, and modulus are all part of the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An error bound controls distance to the solution set by a specified function of a computable or analytic residual whose zero set is exactly the solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in U:\quad d(x,S)\leq\eta(R(x)),\qquad R^{-1}(0)=S.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\eta\) is strictly increasing, the inequality is equivalently \(R(x)\geq\eta^{-1}(d(x,S))\).
special_cases_latex: Taking \(R(x)=f(x)-f_*\) gives an objective-gap error bound.
For convex optimization, taking \(R(x)=\operatorname{dist}_*(0,\partial f(x))\) gives a subgradient-residual error bound.
immediate_consequences_latex: A sequence in \(U\) with \(R(x_k)\to0\) satisfies \(d(x_k,S)\to0\) whenever \(\eta(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\).
boundary_notes: Residual consistency \(R^{-1}(0)=S\) does not itself imply an error bound.
Local and global error bounds must be distinguished through U.
review_flags: No inspected source supplied this abstract residual-modulus definition with all stated variants.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual error bound for a solution set

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) satisfies a subgradient-residual error bound on \(U\) with modulus \(\eta:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty]\), where \(\eta(0)=0\), if \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\eta\bigl(\operatorname{dist}_*(0,\partial f(x))\bigr)\qquad\text{for every }x\in U.\] A linear subgradient error bound has \(\eta(t)=\kappa t\); equivalently, \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}_*(0,\partial f(x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subgradient-residual error bound controls distance to the minimizer set by the smallest dual norm among all convex subgradients at the point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in U:\quad \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\eta\left(\inf_{v\in\partial f(x)}\|v\|_*\right).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The linear form is metric subregularity of the convex subdifferential at residual value zero, uniformly over the specified portion of its zero set.
special_cases_latex: If \(f\) is differentiable on \(U\), then \(R_{\partial}(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|_*\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(R_{\partial}(x_k)\to0\) and \(\eta(t)\to0\) at zero, then \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)\to0\).
boundary_notes: Points outside \(\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) are excluded.
For nonconvex functions, the chosen generalized subdifferential must be specified and the zero set may include nonoptimal stationary points.

children.title: Composite Residual Certificate Family

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composite residual error-bound certificate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional normed space, let \(F=f+g:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), where \(f\) is convex and differentiable on an open set containing \(\operatorname{dom}g\), and let \(g\) be proper, closed, and convex. Write \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}F\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex composite minimization; the definition is local on a specified set and allows any residual map whose zeros coincide locally with minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family \(\{R_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\), with \(R_\lambda:\Omega\to X\), is a composite residual certificate family for \(F=f+g\) on \(U\subseteq\Omega\) if, for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda\), \(R_\lambda(x)=0\iff x\in S\) for \(x\in U\), and there are \(\kappa_\lambda>0\) and \(q_\lambda>0\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq \kappa_\lambda\|R_\lambda(x)\|^{q_\lambda}\qquad(x\in U).\] A canonical proximal-gradient member is \(R_\gamma(x)=\gamma^{-1}\bigl(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(x-\gamma\nabla f(x))\bigr)\), \(\gamma>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite residual certificate family consists of residual maps whose zeros are exactly the composite minimizers on the stated region and whose magnitudes quantitatively control distance to the solution set. For the proximal-gradient residual, the residual is the scaled difference between the current point and its forward-backward update.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and differentiable on a neighborhood of \(\operatorname{dom}g\).
\(g\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}(f+g)\neq\varnothing\).
\(U\subseteq\Omega\) is the region on which the zero-set identity and error bound are asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_\lambda^{-1}(0)\cap U=S\cap U\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa_\lambda\|R_\lambda(x)\|^{q_\lambda}\) for every \(x\in U\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(q_\lambda=1\), the certificate is the metric-subregularity inequality \(\operatorname{dist}(x,R_\lambda^{-1}(0))\leq\kappa_\lambda\operatorname{dist}(0,R_\lambda(x))\) on \(U\).
special_cases_latex: If \(g=0\), then \(R_\gamma=\nabla f\).
If \(f=0\), then \(R_\gamma(x)=\gamma^{-1}(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}x)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Any sequence \(x_k\in U\) satisfying \(\|R_\lambda(x_k)\|\to0\) also satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)\to0\).
boundary_notes: The zero-set identity alone is only a stationarity certificate and does not provide an error bound.
The constants and exponent may be local and may depend on the residual parameter.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A proximal residual bound with constant \(\kappa>0\) holds on \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) if
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)
\leq\kappa\left\lVert x-T_t(x)\right\rVert
\quad\text{for every }x\in D.
\]
The residual is directly computable from one forward-backward step. Moreover, \(x=T_t(x)\) is equivalent to \(0\in\nabla g(x)+\partial h(x)\), hence to \(x\in S\) under the stated convex assumptions.

children.title: Composite Residual Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Comparative geometry among residual certificates for composite models.

assumptions_latex: \(F=g+h\), where \(g\) is convex with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(h\) is proper lower-semicontinuous convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert x-x^+\rVert=t\lVert G_t(x)\rVert\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^+))\leq(1+Lt)\lVert G_t(x)\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of displacement, gradient-mapping, and post-step stationarity residuals.

source_refs.locator: 10.4 Analysis of the Proximal Gradient Method-The Convex Case p. 281

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The proximal displacement and gradient mapping satisfy the exact identity
\[
\lVert x-x^+\rVert=t\lVert G_t(x)\rVert.
\]
Proximal optimality also gives
\[
G_t(x)-\nabla g(x)+\nabla g(x^+)\in\partial F(x^+).
\]
Consequently, Lipschitz continuity of \(\nabla g\) yields
\[
\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\partial F(x^+)\bigr)
\leq(1+Lt)\lVert G_t(x)\rVert.
\]
Thus a gradient-mapping residual controls a subgradient residual at the computed proximal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal displacement equals the stepsize times the gradient mapping, which also bounds stationarity at the new proximal point.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite Residual Comparisons

source_witnesses.locator: 10.4 Analysis of the Proximal Gradient Method-The Convex Case p. 281

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Composite Residual Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact stationarity equivalence for the forward-backward fixed point and gradient mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t>0\), \[G_t(x)=0\iff x=\operatorname{prox}_{th}(x-t\nabla g(x))\iff 0\in\nabla g(x)+\partial h(x)=\partial F(x).\] If \(F\) is convex, these conditions are equivalent to \(x\in\operatorname*{argmin}F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero proximal displacement, zero gradient mapping, a forward-backward fixed point, composite stationarity, and convex optimality are equivalent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G_t(x)=0\iff0\in\partial F(x)\iff x\in\operatorname*{argmin}F.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Composite Residual Equivalence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Current-Point Stationarity Dominates the Gradient Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison from a composite subgradient at the current point to the proximal-gradient residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^+=\operatorname{prox}_{th}(x-t\nabla g(x))\) and \(G_t(x)=t^{-1}(x-x^+)\). For every \(v\in\partial h(x)\), \[\|G_t(x)\|\leq\|\nabla g(x)+v\|.\] Consequently, \[\|G_t(x)\|\leq\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal-gradient mapping at x is no larger than the smallest composite subgradient residual at x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lVert G_t(x)\rVert\leq\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x)).

children.title: Feasibility Error Bounds
children.top_down_role: Distance control through violations of constraint systems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility error bound for a constraint system
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be metric spaces, let \(G:X\rightrightarrows Y\), fix \(\bar y\in Y\), and define the feasible set \(C=G^{-1}(\bar y)=\{x:\bar y\in G(x)\}\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric-space formulation, local or global according to the chosen region; Hölder and linear bounds are distinguished by the exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The system \(\bar y\in G(x)\) has a Hölder feasibility error bound of order \(q>0\) on \(U\subseteq X\) with constant \(\kappa>0\) if \[\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leq\kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,G(x))^q\qquad\text{for every }x\in U,\] with \(\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,\varnothing)=+\infty\). It has a local error bound at \(\bar x\in C\) when this holds on some neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\), and a global error bound when \(U=X\). The case \(q=1\) is a linear feasibility error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility error bound controls the distance from any tested point to the feasible set by a constant times a power of its constraint violation. It is local if asserted only near a feasible reference point and global if asserted throughout the ambient space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,G(x))^q\) for all \(x\in U\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(q=1\) and local \(U\), the inequality is metric subregularity of \(G\) at \((\bar x,\bar y)\).
For scalar inequalities \(g_i(x)\leq0\), one may take \(G(x)=g(x)+\mathbb R_+^m\), giving residual \(\operatorname{dist}(g(x),-\mathbb R_+^m)\).
special_cases_latex: For an equation \(F(x)=0\), the bound becomes \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(0))\leq\kappa\|F(x)\|^q\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If the residual tends to zero along points in \(U\), their distances to \(C\) tend to zero.
boundary_notes: An error bound does not require uniqueness of a feasible point.
A local bound need not extend globally with one uniform constant.

source_refs.locator: Example 9.44 and Example 9.47, constraint systems and metric-regularity error estimates

children.title: Hoffman Bounds for Polyhedral Systems
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral feasibility error-bound family.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(C\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(d\in\mathbb R^p\).
\(S=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:Az\leq b,\ Cz=d\}\neq\varnothing\), and fixed norms are used on \(\mathbb R^n\), \(\mathbb R^m\), and \(\mathbb R^p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(H>0\), depending only on \(A\), \(C\), and the chosen norms, such that \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq H(\lVert(Ax-b)_+\rVert+\lVert Cx-d\rVert)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: Hoffman constant for the matrices and norms

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional error bound for mixed linear inequalities and equalities.

source_refs.locator: 3.4 Polyhedral Functions p. 76
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms II: Advanced Theory and Bundle Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(C\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\) be fixed. There exists a constant \(H>0\), depending only on \(A\), \(C\), and the chosen norms, such that for every \(b\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(d\in\mathbb R^p\) for which
\[
S=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:Az\leq b,\ Cz=d\}
\]
is nonempty,
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)
\leq H\left(\lVert(Ax-b)_+\rVert+\lVert Cx-d\rVert\right)
\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
Here \((Ax-b)_+\) denotes the componentwise positive part.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hoffman's theorem bounds distance to any nonempty mixed linear constraint system by the combined inequality and equality residuals, with a constant determined by the fixed matrices and norms.
knowledge_statements.title: Hoffman Bounds for Polyhedral Systems

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4 Polyhedral Functions p. 76

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hoffman error-bound modulus
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(d\in\mathbb R^p\). Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\leq b,\ Bx=d\}\neq\varnothing\), with fixed norms on the variable and residual spaces.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, consistent polyhedral systems; the bound is global and its modulus depends on the matrices and chosen norms, not on the right-hand side within the consistent family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A number \(H\geq0\) is a Hoffman constant for the system matrices \((A,B)\) if, for every right-hand side \((b,d)\) for which \(P\neq\varnothing\) and every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \[\operatorname{dist}(x,P)\leq H\left\|\bigl((Ax-b)_+,\,Bx-d\bigr)\right\|.\] The least admissible constant is the Hoffman modulus \(H(A,B)\). Here \((u_+)_i=\max\{u_i,0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Hoffman bound is a global linear feasibility error bound for a consistent finite system of linear inequalities and equalities. Distance to the solution polyhedron is bounded by a matrix-dependent constant times the norm of the positive inequality violations together with the equality residuals.
assumptions_latex: All norms are fixed on the finite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,P)\leq H(A,B)\|((Ax-b)_+,Bx-d)\|\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(S(x)=(Ax-b,Bx-d)+\mathbb R_+^m\times\{0\}\), the bound is global metric subregularity of the polyhedral multifunction \(S\) at the origin.
special_cases_latex: For inequalities only, \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\{Ax\leq b\})\leq H(A)\|(Ax-b)_+\|\).
For equalities only, the estimate reduces to a linear-system residual bound.
immediate_consequences_latex: A sequence with vanishing linear constraint residual has vanishing distance to the feasible polyhedron.
boundary_notes: Consistency is essential because distance to an empty feasible set is infinite.
The numerical value of the least constant changes with the selected norms.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Residual Bounds Can Fail Without Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a local Lipschitz feasibility error bound for a smooth convex nonpolyhedral inequality without strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be \(g(x)=x^2\) and let \(C=\{x:g(x)\leq0\}=\{0\}\). No neighborhood \(U\) of \(0\) and \(\kappa>0\) satisfy \[\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leq\kappa[g(x)]_+\qquad(x\in U).\] Nevertheless, \[\operatorname{dist}(x,C)=[g(x)]_+^{1/2}\] for every \(x\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the curved constraint x²≤0, distance is the square root of violation, so no local linear violation bound exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No local bound \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leq\kappa[g(x)]_+\) exists, while \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)=[g(x)]_+^{1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Residual Bounds Can Fail Without Regularity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded Linear Regularity under Relative-Interior Intersection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-region distance error bound for a finite family of closed convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty closed convex sets satisfying
\[
\bigcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{ri}C_i\neq\varnothing,
\qquad C:=\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i.
\]
For every bounded set \(B\subset\mathbb R^n\), there exists \(\kappa_B>0\) such that
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leq\kappa_B\max_{1\leq i\leq m}\operatorname{dist}(x,C_i)
\quad\text{for every }x\in B.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite family of closed convex sets with a common relative-interior point is linearly regular on every bounded region.
assumptions_latex: \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\subset\mathbb R^n\) are nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For some \(\kappa_B>0\), \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\bigcap_iC_i)\leq\kappa_B\max_i\operatorname{dist}(x,C_i)\) for every \(x\in B\).
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Linear Regularity under Relative-Interior Intersection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semialgebraic Hölder Feasibility Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-region Hölder error bound for finite continuous semialgebraic constraint systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_1,\ldots,g_m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuous semialgebraic functions and let \(C=\{x:g_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\neq\varnothing\). For every compact \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\), there exist \(c_K>0\) and \(\theta_K\in(0,1]\) such that
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leq c_K\left(\max_{1\leq i\leq m}[g_i(x)]_+\right)^{\theta_K}
\qquad(x\in K).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous semialgebraic constraints admit a Hölder feasibility error bound on every compact region.
assumptions_latex: \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\) are continuous semialgebraic functions on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(c_K>0\) and \(\theta_K\in(0,1]\) such that \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leq c_K(\max_i[g_i(x)]_+)^{\theta_K}\) for all \(x\in K\).
knowledge_statements.title: Semialgebraic Hölder Feasibility Bounds

assumptions_latex: There exists \(x^s\) such that \(g_i(x^s)<0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every compact \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), there exists \(\kappa_K>0\) such that \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leq \kappa_K\max_i[g_i(x)]_+\) for all \(x\in K\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-set residual bound for finite convex inequality systems satisfying Slater’s condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), where every \(g_i\) is finite and convex. If there exists \(x^s\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(g_i(x^s)<0\) for all \(i\), then for each compact set \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) there is a constant \(\kappa_K>0\) satisfying
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leq\kappa_K\max_{1\leq i\leq m}[g_i(x)]_+\qquad(x\in K).
\]
Thus curved convex constraints possess a local-uniform feasibility error bound, although unlike a Hoffman bound its modulus may depend on \(K\) and the system’s regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Slater-feasible finite convex inequality system has, on every compact set, a distance-to-feasibility bound controlled by its largest constraint violation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic feasibility-error-bound definition; canonically belongs to the parent feasibility-error-bound scope rather than specifically to nonpolyhedral systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and let \(R:\mathbb R^n\to[0,+\infty]\) satisfy \(C=\{x:R(x)=0\}\). A local Hölder feasibility error bound of exponent \(\theta\in(0,1]\) at \(\bar x\in C\) means that \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leq\kappa R(x)^\theta\) near \(\bar x\), for some \(\kappa>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularity-dependent nonpolyhedral feasibility bound
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be finite-dimensional normed spaces, let \(F:X\to Y\) be continuous, let \(D\subseteq Y\) be closed and nonpolyhedral, and set \(C=\{x:F(x)\in D\}\). Fix \(\bar x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local feasibility geometry for curved constraint sets; no global or linear rate is implicit without an additional regularity hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The nonpolyhedral system \(F(x)\in D\) admits a local Hölder feasibility bound of order \(q>0\) at \(\bar x\) if there exist \(\kappa>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leq\kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(F(x),D)^q\qquad\text{whenever }\|x-\bar x\|<\varepsilon.\] Its local modulus is the infimum of admissible \(\kappa\) for the specified exponent. The linear regularity regime is \(q=1\); exponents \(0<q<1\) describe weaker Hölder control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonpolyhedral feasibility bound locally controls distance to a curved feasible set by a power of the distance of the constraint image to the target set. Both the exponent and constant are part of the certificate because curvature or degeneracy may prevent a linear bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(\kappa,\varepsilon>0\) such that \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(F(x),D)^q\) on \(B(\bar x,\varepsilon)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(G(x)=F(x)-D\), the case \(q=1\) is metric subregularity of \(G\) at \((\bar x,0)\).
special_cases_latex: Nonlinear inequalities correspond to \(D=-\mathbb R_+^m\).
Semidefinite constraints correspond to a target set given by a positive-semidefinite cone.
immediate_consequences_latex: Vanishing violation along points near \(\bar x\) forces convergence in distance to \(C\).
boundary_notes: Nonpolyhedrality alone neither guarantees nor rules out a linear bound.
The local exponent and modulus can vary between feasible reference points.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Growth–regularity correspondence schema
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\). Fix \(\bar x\in S\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A definition of the paired certificate structure, not an assertion that every listed implication holds without additional hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A growth–regularity correspondence on \(U\) is a quantitatively specified pair \((\psi,\rho)\) of nondecreasing functions \(\psi,\rho:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty)\), vanishing only at zero, for which the growth certificate \[f(x)-\min f\geq\psi(\operatorname{dist}(x,S))\qquad(x\in U)\] and the residual regularity certificate \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\rho(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x)))\qquad(x\in U)\] are treated as matched local properties. A power-type correspondence has \(\psi(t)=ct^p\) and \(\rho(s)=\kappa s^q\) for positive constants and exponents.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A growth–regularity correspondence records, on one common neighborhood, both objective separation from the minimizer set and control of distance to that set by the subdifferential residual. The correspondence includes the moduli and exponents, rather than merely naming the two properties.

\(\psi\) and \(\rho\) are nondecreasing and vanish only at zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The paired inequalities hold for every \(x\in U\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The residual inequality is metric subregularity of \(\partial f\) for \(0\) relative to its inverse \((\partial f)^{-1}(0)=S\) when \(\rho(s)=\kappa s\).
special_cases_latex: Quadratic growth uses \(\psi(t)=ct^2\).
Weak sharp minima use \(\psi(t)=ct\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Either certificate supplies a quantitative stopping interpretation in its own residual variable.
boundary_notes: A logical equivalence between the two certificates requires hypotheses beyond this paired definition.
Set-relative distance is essential when minimizers are nonunique.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. Let \(S=(\partial f)^{-1}(0)=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\), and fix \(\bar x\in S\).

\]
for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) satisfying \(\|x-\bar x\|<\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse-Calmness Formulation of Subdifferential Subregularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent inverse-mapping formulation specialized to the convex subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, with \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)\). Metric subregularity of \(\partial f\) at \((\bar x,0)\) with modulus \(\kappa\) is equivalent to calmness of \((\partial f)^{-1}\) at \((0,\bar x)\): there are neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(0\) such that \[(\partial f)^{-1}(v)\cap U\subseteq(\partial f)^{-1}(0)+\kappa\|v\|\mathbb B\qquad(v\in V).\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space and let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. For \(\bar x\in H\) with \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)\), the subdifferential \(\partial f\) is metrically subregular at \((\bar x,0)\) if there exist \(\kappa>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that
\[
\operatorname{dist}\bigl(x,(\partial f)^{-1}(0)\bigr)
\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\partial f(x)\bigr)
\]
whenever \(\|x-\bar x\|<\varepsilon\), with the right side interpreted as \(+\infty\) when \(\partial f(x)=\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Error-bound rate-transfer interface
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(S\neq\varnothing\) be a target set, let \(r:X\to[0,+\infty]\) be a residual, and let \((x_k)\subseteq U\subseteq X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract deterministic transfer from a residual estimate to a distance estimate; the definition does not itself supply an algorithmic residual rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An error-bound rate-transfer interface on \(U\) is an inequality \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\omega(r(x))\qquad(x\in U),\] where \(\omega:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty)\) is nondecreasing, \(\omega(0)=0\), and \(\omega(t)\downarrow0\) as \(t\downarrow0\). For any sequence \(x_k\in U\) with a certified residual estimate \(r(x_k)\leq a_k\), the transferred estimate is \[\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)\leq\omega(a_k).\] A Hölder interface has \(\omega(t)=\kappa t^q\), \(\kappa,q>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An error-bound rate-transfer interface is a modulus that converts any available residual bound into a bound on distance to the solution or feasible set. In the Hölder case, a residual rate is raised to the error-bound exponent.
assumptions_latex: \(\omega\) is nondecreasing, vanishes at zero, and is continuous at zero from the right.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)\leq\omega(a_k)\) for every \(k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(\omega(t)=\kappa t^q\) and \(a_k=O(k^{-\alpha})\), the interface records \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)=O(k^{-\alpha q})\).
special_cases_latex: A linear error bound has \(q=1\).
If \(a_k\leq C\rho^k\) with \(0<\rho<1\), then the Hölder interface gives \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)\leq\kappa C^q\rho^{qk}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Residual convergence implies convergence in distance to \(S\).
boundary_notes: The interface transfers only while iterates remain in the region where the error bound holds.
It does not imply convergence to a particular point when \(S\) is not a singleton.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sublevel-Tube Characterization of a Hölder Error Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric reformulation through containment of objective sublevels in metric enlargements of the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) attain its minimum \(f^*\) on \(S\neq\varnothing\), let \(U\subset X\), and let \(c,\theta>0\). The bound
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq c\bigl(f(x)-f^*\bigr)^\theta
\qquad(x\in U\cap\operatorname{dom}f)
\]
holds if and only if, for every \(t\geq0\),
\[
U\cap\{x:f(x)\leq f^*+t\}
\subseteq
\{x:\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq ct^\theta\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Hölder error bound is equivalent to every gap-t sublevel lying, within U, inside the solution-set tube of radius c times t to the theta.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pointwise Hölder error bound is equivalent to the stated family of sublevel-set tube inclusions.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, suppose that \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\), and set \(f^*=\inf f\). For \(c>0\), \(\theta>0\), and \(U\subset H\), the Hölder error bound
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq c\bigl(f(x)-f^*\bigr)^\theta
\]
for every \(x\in U\cap\operatorname{dom}f\) is equivalent to
\[
x\in S+c\bigl(f(x)-f^*\bigr)^\theta\mathbb{B}
\]
for every such \(x\), where \(\mathbb{B}\) is the closed unit ball of \(H\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Objective Convergence under the Polyak–Łojasiewicz Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-value contraction for fixed-step gradient descent under a slope error bound valid along the iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:H\to\mathbb R\) be convex and Fréchet differentiable with nonempty minimizer set and \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient. Suppose \(\frac12\|\nabla f(x)\|^2\geq\mu(f(x)-f^*)\) on a set containing every iterate and its gradient step. For \(x^{k+1}=x^k-L^{-1}\nabla f(x^k)\), \[f(x^{k+1})-f^*\leq\left(1-\frac{\mu}{L}\right)(f(x^k)-f^*).\] Thus the objective residual converges Q-linearly while the hypotheses remain applicable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Polyak–Łojasiewicz slope bound converts the smooth descent inequality into linear objective-value convergence of gradient descent.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance contraction for the exact proximal-point iteration under quadratic growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space and let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\). Suppose \(f(y)-f^*\geq(\mu/2)\operatorname{dist}(y,S)^2\) on a neighborhood containing the iterates. For fixed \(\lambda>0\), define \(x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x^k)\). Then, while the iterates remain in that neighborhood,
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x^{k+1},S)
\leq\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+\lambda\mu}}\operatorname{dist}(x^k,S).
\]
Hence the distances converge locally at a Q-linear rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic growth turns exact proximal-point steps into a local linear contraction of distance to the solution set.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regimes are finite termination for \(\theta=0\), linear convergence for \(0<\theta\leq1/2\), and polynomial sublinear convergence for \(1/2<\theta<1\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualitative KL rate trichotomy for standard descent sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((x^k)\) converge to \(\bar x\), and suppose that for some \(a,b>0\),
\[
f(x^k)-f(x^{k+1})\geq a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2,
\qquad
\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x^{k+1}))\leq b\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|.
\]
If near \(\bar x\), \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\geq c(f(x)-f(\bar x))^\theta\), then the induced regimes are: finite termination when \(\theta=0\); local linear convergence when \(0<\theta\leq1/2\); and polynomial sublinear decay when \(1/2<\theta<1\), with objective residual of order \(O(k^{-1/(2\theta-1)})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under standard descent and relative-error conditions, the KL exponent separates finite, linear, and polynomially sublinear convergence regimes.
knowledge_statements.title: Rate-Transfer Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The qualitative KL trichotomy fits the leaf, but the function, ambient space, subdifferential, residual positivity, and eventual applicability of the inequalities are not fully specified. A source is needed to determine the correct abstract hypotheses and whether each rate concerns values, iterates, or both.

children.title: Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz Exponent Interface
children.top_down_role: Exponent-based bridge between growth geometry and convergence regimes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz Slope Exponent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power-form KL inequality for a proper closed convex function at a minimizing critical point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)\). An exponent \(\theta\in[0,1)\) is admissible at \(\bar x\) if there exist \(c,\eta>0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\geq c\bigl(f(x)-f(\bar x)\bigr)^\theta\] whenever \(x\in U\) and \(f(\bar x)<f(x)<f(\bar x)+\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A KL exponent specifies the power relating subgradient slope to the positive objective residual near a critical value.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\geq c(f(x)-f(\bar x))^\theta\) locally above the critical value.
knowledge_statements.title: Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz Slope Exponent

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex KL Inequality Implies Power Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse direction of the local convex growth–KL exponent interface, with existential constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\), and let \(\bar x\in S\). Suppose that for some \(c>0\) and \(\theta\in[0,1)\), \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\geq c(f(x)-f^*)^\theta\] holds for all \(x\) sufficiently near \(\bar x\) whose objective value lies in a sufficiently small interval above \(f^*\). Then there exist \(\alpha,\varepsilon>0\) such that \[f(x)-f^*\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^{1/(1-\theta)}\] whenever \(\|x-\bar x\|<\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For closed convex functions, a local KL slope inequality with exponent theta yields local power growth of order one over one minus theta.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
The KL slope inequality with exponent \(\theta\in[0,1)\) holds locally and uniformly for sufficiently small positive residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)-f^*\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^{1/(1-\theta)}\) locally for some \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Convex KL Inequality Implies Power Growth

assumptions_latex: \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\geq\mu^{1/p}(f(x)-f^*)^{1-1/p}\) locally outside \(S\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convex subgradient inequality transfers power growth to a KL slope inequality
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex power growth implies a KL inequality with the conjugate exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space and let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\). Suppose that locally around \(S\),
\[
f(x)-f^*\geq\mu\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^p
\]
for some \(\mu>0\) and \(p>1\). Then every nearby \(x\notin S\) satisfies
\[
\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))
\geq\mu^{1/p}\bigl(f(x)-f^*\bigr)^{1-1/p}.
\]
Thus power growth of order \(p\) yields a Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz slope inequality with exponent \(\theta=1-1/p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For convex functions, power growth of order p transfers to a KL slope inequality with exponent 1−1/p.
knowledge_statements.title: Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz Exponent Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the exponent-interface leaf and the exponent is plausible, but the exact constant and the meaning of growth locally around the entire solution set require verification from a specifically located source.

children.title: Growth-Certificate Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Flat, degenerate, nonuniform, and locality-limited regimes.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure boundary of a prescribed growth certificate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\), let \(U\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\), and let \(\psi:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty)\) satisfy \(\psi(0)=0\) and \(\psi(t)>0\) for \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-relative definition for a fixed modulus and region; it distinguishes failure of uniform constants from total absence of local growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The \(\psi\)-growth certificate holds on \(U\) with constant \(c>0\) when \[f(x)-\min f\geq c\,\psi(\operatorname{dist}(x,S))\qquad(x\in U).\] Its failure boundary consists of those regimes for which no uniform \(c>0\) is admissible, equivalently \[\inf_{x\in U\setminus S}\frac{f(x)-\min f}{\psi(\operatorname{dist}(x,S))}=0.\] Local failure at \(\bar x\in S\) means this infimum is zero on every neighborhood of \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A prescribed growth certificate fails uniformly when the ratio of objective gap to the chosen distance-growth modulus can become arbitrarily small. Local failure means this happens in every neighborhood of a selected minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform failure is characterized by \(\inf_{x\in U\setminus S}(f(x)-\min f)/\psi(\operatorname{dist}(x,S))=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Failure is equivalent to the existence of a sequence \(x_k\in U\setminus S\) such that \((f(x_k)-\min f)/\psi(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S))\to0\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\psi(t)=t^2\), this is failure of quadratic growth.
For \(\psi(t)=t\), this is failure of weak sharpness.
immediate_consequences_latex: No positive uniform growth constant can be inferred on the specified region.
boundary_notes: Failure for one modulus does not imply failure for every weaker modulus.
Global failure may coexist with a valid local certificate near each individual minimizer.
review_flags: No inspected source states this named failure-boundary definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure boundary of a prescribed growth certificate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ratio characterization is a coherent negation of a fixed growth certificate, but the named failure-boundary concept and its exact scope are unsupported.

children.title: Flat Minimum Valleys
children.top_down_role: Weak objective separation from the solution set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sequential Criterion for Order-p Flatness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential characterization of failure of every uniform order-p growth modulus on tubular neighborhoods of the minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) attain its minimum \(f^*\) on \(S\neq\varnothing\), where \(X\) is a metric space, and let \(p>0\). A positive order-\(p\) growth modulus fails on every tubular neighborhood of \(S\) if and only if there exists \((x_k)\subset\operatorname{dom}f\setminus S\) such that
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)\to0,
\qquad
\frac{f(x_k)-f^*}{\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)^p}\to0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform order-p growth fails arbitrarily near the solution set exactly when normalized objective gaps approach zero along nonoptimal points approaching that set.
assumptions_latex: \(p>0\), and locality is measured by tubular neighborhoods \(\{x:\operatorname{dist}(x,S)<r\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every positive uniform local order-\(p\) modulus fails if and only if such a normalized-gap sequence exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Criterion for Order-p Flatness

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Although \(f(x,y)=\operatorname{dist}((x,y),S)^4\), no positive local quadratic-growth modulus exists relative to \(S\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonisolated valley with exact fourth-order, but not quadratic, separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(f:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}\) by \(f(x,y)=x^4\). This function is convex, its minimum value is \(0\), and its minimizer set is the valley \(S=\{0\}\times\mathbb{R}\). Moreover,
\[
f(x,y)=\operatorname{dist}((x,y),S)^4.
\]
For every \(\mu>0\) and every neighborhood of \(S\), points with sufficiently small nonzero \(|x|\) violate
\[
f(x,y)\geq\frac{\mu}{2}\operatorname{dist}((x,y),S)^2.
\]
Hence exact higher-order separation may coexist with failure of every quadratic growth certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The valley function x⁴ has exact fourth-order separation from its minimizers but no quadratic separation, however locally it is examined.
knowledge_statements.title: Flat Minimum Valleys

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Flat minimum valley of order \(p\)
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\). Fix \(p>0\) and \(\bar x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local, set-relative notion of inadequate objective separation; it permits a non-singleton minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The minimum valley is \(p\)-flat at \(\bar x\) if, for every \(c>0\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists \(x\in B(\bar x,\varepsilon)\setminus S\) such that \[0<f(x)-\min f<c\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^p.\] Equivalently, there is a sequence \(x_k\to\bar x\), \(x_k\notin S\), for which \[(f(x_k)-\min f)/\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)^p\to0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimum valley is flat of order p at a minimizer when the objective gap can be arbitrarily smaller than every positive multiple of the p-th power of distance to the full solution set, even arbitrarily close to that minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No local positive constant \(c\) yields \(f(x)-\min f\geq c\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^p\) near \(\bar x\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\liminf_{x\to\bar x,\ x\notin S}(f(x)-\min f)/\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^p=0\).
special_cases_latex: \(p=2\) describes failure of local quadratic growth.
\(p=1\) describes failure of local weak sharpness.
immediate_consequences_latex: Objective gaps alone cannot provide a local \(p\)-power distance estimate with a uniform positive constant.
boundary_notes: A non-singleton solution set is not by itself a flat valley because distance is measured to the entire set.
Flatness of order \(p\) does not determine flatness for every other exponent.
review_flags: The formulation is an exact negation of local power growth, but the supplied sources do not establish this terminology.
knowledge_statements.title: Flat minimum valley of order \(p\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement precisely characterizes failure of local \(p\)-power growth, but no source supports the “flat minimum valley” terminology or exact definition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Minima and Subgradient Optimality for Convex Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained minimization of a convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be convex and let \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\). Every local minimizer \(x\) of \(f\) is a global minimizer. Moreover, \[x\in\operatorname*{argmin} f\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\partial f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex function, every local minimizer is global, and a point is a global minimizer if and only if zero belongs to its subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ local minimizer}\Rightarrow x\text{ global minimizer},\qquad x\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\Longleftrightarrow 0\in\partial f(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ridge Index
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local conditioning measure based on the radial eccentricity of nearby level sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a minimum point x^*, define L_\delta=\{x:f(x)=f(x^*)+\delta\}. When the limit is defined, the ridge index is
\mu=\lim_{\delta\to0}\frac{\sup_{x\in L_\delta}\|x-x^*\|^2}{\inf_{x\in L_\delta}\|x-x^*\|^2},
with \mu\ge1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ridge index of a minimum is the limiting ratio of the largest to smallest squared distance from the minimum along nearby level sets. It is at least one and measures local level-set elongation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimizers of a Convex Functional
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex functionals on convex subsets of normed spaces; the infimum need not be attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let C be a convex subset of a normed space, let f:C\to\mathbb{R} be convex, and set \mu=\inf_{x\in C}f(x). Then \Omega=\{x\in C:f(x)=\mu\} is convex. Moreover, if x_0\in C is a local minimizer of f, then f(x_0)=\mu, so x_0 is a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex functional on a convex domain, the set of points attaining the infimum is convex. Every local minimizer attains that infimum and is therefore global.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Omega=\{x\in C:f(x)=\mu\}\text{ is convex},\qquad x_0\text{ local minimizer}\Longrightarrow f(x_0)=\mu\Longrightarrow x_0\text{ global minimizer}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ideal vanishing-regularization method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithmic principle only; this extract motivates but does not prove convergence of the auxiliary minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a convex objective $f$ and a chosen regularization function $g$, solve the auxiliary problems
\[
x_{\varepsilon}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x}\bigl(f(x)+\varepsilon g(x)\bigr),\qquad \varepsilon>0,
\]
exactly while sending $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. The scalar $\varepsilon$ is the regularization parameter and $g$ is the regularization function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perturb a convex objective by a small weighted regularization function, exactly minimize each perturbed objective, and let the positive weight tend to zero. The extract presents convergence to an original solution as the motivation, not as an established guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The method generates exact auxiliary minimizers }x_\varepsilon\text{ of }f+\varepsilon g\text{ as }\varepsilon\downarrow0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Selection by vanishing strongly convex regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact regularization with a positive parameter tending to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be convex and continuous with nonempty minimizer set $X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}f$, and let $g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be strongly convex and continuous. For $\varepsilon>0$, define
\[
\Phi_\varepsilon(x)=f(x)+\varepsilon g(x),\qquad x_\varepsilon=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\Phi_\varepsilon(x).
\]
Then, as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$,
\[
x_\varepsilon\to x^*,\qquad x^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X^*}g(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous convex objective with at least one minimizer and a continuous strongly convex regularizer, the exact minimizer of the regularized objective converges, as the positive regularization weight vanishes, to the original minimizer that minimizes the regularizer over the solution set.
assumptions_latex: g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is strongly convex and continuous}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_\varepsilon\xrightarrow[\varepsilon\downarrow0]{}x^*,\qquad x^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X^*}g(x).
