knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\ge1\) be an integer. The positive-semidefinite and positive-definite cones in the space \(\mathbb S^n\) of real symmetric \(n\times n\) matrices are \[\mathbb S_+^n:=\{X\in\mathbb S^n:v^TXv\ge0\text{ for every }v\in\mathbb R^n\},\qquad \mathbb S_{++}^n:=\{X\in\mathbb S^n:v^TXv>0\text{ for every }v\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\}.\] Equivalently, \(X\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) exactly when \(\lambda_{\min}(X)>0\). Moreover, \[\mathbb S_{++}^n=\operatorname{int}(\mathbb S_+^n).\] The set \(\mathbb S_{++}^n\) is an open convex cone and is invariant under congruence by every invertible matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive integer n, positive-definite real symmetric n by n matrices have strictly positive quadratic forms, equivalently strictly positive eigenvalues, and form the interior of the positive-semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definite Cone

source_witnesses.locator: 8 Convex Functions p. 139

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary Distance and Inverse Blowup on the Positive-Definite Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interior-to-boundary geometry of the symmetric positive-definite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), \[\operatorname{dist}_F(X,\operatorname{bdry}\mathbb S_+^n)=\lambda_{\min}(X).\] Moreover, \[\overline{\mathbb S_{++}^n}=\mathbb S_+^n,\qquad \operatorname{bdry}\mathbb S_+^n=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^n:\lambda_{\min}(X)=0\}.\] Consequently, if \(X_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) converges to a singular \(\bar X\in\mathbb S_+^n\), then \(\|X_k^{-1}\|_2=1/\lambda_{\min}(X_k)\to+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The PSD cone is the closure of the positive-definite cone, its boundary consists of singular PSD matrices, and the Frobenius distance from a positive-definite matrix to that boundary is its smallest eigenvalue. Inversion blows up at the boundary.
assumptions_latex: Distance uses the Frobenius norm and inverse size uses the spectral operator norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\overline{\mathbb S_{++}^n}=\mathbb S_+^n\), the boundary is characterized by \(\lambda_{\min}=0\), and inverse norms diverge along positive-definite approaches to it.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Distance and Inverse Blowup on the Positive-Definite Cone

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure, Boundary, and Inverse Blowup of the Positive-Definite Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interior-to-boundary geometry of the symmetric positive-definite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), the Frobenius distance to the boundary of the positive-semidefinite cone is \[\operatorname{dist}_F(X,\operatorname{bdry}\mathbb S_+^n)=\lambda_{\min}(X).\] Moreover, \[\overline{\mathbb S_{++}^n}=\mathbb S_+^n,\qquad \operatorname{bdry}\mathbb S_+^n=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^n:\lambda_{\min}(X)=0\}.\] Consequently, if \(X_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) converges to a singular \(\bar X\in\mathbb S_+^n\), then \(\|X_k^{-1}\|_2=1/\lambda_{\min}(X_k)\to+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive-semidefinite cone is the closure of the positive-definite cone, its boundary consists of singular positive-semidefinite matrices, and distance to that boundary equals the smallest eigenvalue. Inversion therefore blows up on approach to a singular boundary point.
assumptions_latex: Distances use the Frobenius norm and inverse norms use the spectral norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\overline{\mathbb S_{++}^n}=\mathbb S_+^n\), \(\operatorname{dist}_F(X,\operatorname{bdry}\mathbb S_+^n)=\lambda_{\min}(X)\), and inverse norms diverge along positive-definite approaches to a singular boundary point.
knowledge_statements.title: Closure, Boundary, and Inverse Blowup of the Positive-Definite Cone

children.title: Eigenvalue-Induced Divergences
children.top_down_role: Matrix divergences organized through eigenvalue-level structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unordered Spectra Do Not Determine Divergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of any formula based only on the two separately unordered spectra when their relative eigenvector alignment is unspecified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(X)=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(X^2)\), \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(1,0)\), \(Y_1=\operatorname{Diag}(1,0)\), and \(Y_2=\operatorname{Diag}(0,1)\). Although \(Y_1\) and \(Y_2\) have the same unordered eigenvalues, \[D_F(X,Y_1)=0,\qquad D_F(X,Y_2)=\tfrac12\lVert X-Y_2\rVert_F^2=1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate unordered spectra do not determine a spectral Bregman divergence because relative eigenspace alignment matters.
assumptions_latex: The matrices are real symmetric \(2\times2\) matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda(Y_1)=\lambda(Y_2)\) as unordered multisets but \(D_F(X,Y_1)\ne D_F(X,Y_2)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Unordered Spectra Do Not Determine Divergence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Commuting Eigenvalue Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aligned scalar decomposition for commuting symmetric matrices; eigenvalues are paired in a common eigenbasis rather than independently sorted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=U\operatorname{diag}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)U^\top\) and \(Y=U\operatorname{diag}(y_1,\ldots,y_n)U^\top\), where \(x_i,y_i\in I\), and let \(F(X)=\operatorname{tr}f(X)\) for differentiable convex \(f:I\to\mathbb R\). Then \[D_F(X,Y)=\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl(f(x_i)-f(y_i)-f'(y_i)(x_i-y_i)\bigr).\] If \(f\) is strictly convex, this quantity is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when \(X=Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For commuting symmetric matrices, a trace-spectral Bregman divergence is the sum of scalar divergences between eigenvalues aligned in a common eigenbasis.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\in\mathbb S^n\) commute and have spectra in an interval \(I\).
Strict convexity is additionally assumed for the stated equality characterization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_F(X,Y)=\sum_i d_f(x_i,y_i)\ge0\), with equality under strict convexity exactly when \(X=Y\).

notation.meaning: scalar Bregman divergence generated by f

knowledge_statements.title: Commuting Eigenvalue Reduction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Log-Determinant Matrix Divergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bregman divergence generated by the negative log determinant on the positive-definite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(X)=-\log\det X\) and \(X,Y\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), \[D_F(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}(Y^{-1}X)-\log\det(Y^{-1}X)-n.\] If \(\mu_i>0\) are the eigenvalues of \(Y^{-1/2}XY^{-1/2}\), then \[D_F(X,Y)=\sum_{i=1}^n(\mu_i-\log\mu_i-1)\ge0,\] with equality exactly when \(X=Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative-log-determinant Bregman divergence is a sum of scalar Burg divergences of relative generalized eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_F(X,Y)=\sum_i(\mu_i-\log\mu_i-1)\ge0\), with equality iff \(X=Y\).
knowledge_statements.title: Log-Determinant Matrix Divergence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trace-Entropy Matrix Divergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix Bregman divergence induced by the trace negative-entropy generator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(X)=\operatorname{tr}(X\log X)\) and \(X,Y\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), \[D_F(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(X(\log X-\log Y)-X+Y\bigr)\ge0,\] with equality exactly when \(X=Y\). If \(\operatorname{tr}X=\operatorname{tr}Y\), this reduces to the Umegaki relative entropy \(\operatorname{tr}(X(\log X-\log Y))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trace negative entropy generates the nonnegative matrix relative-entropy divergence, reducing to Umegaki relative entropy for equal-trace matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_F(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}(X(\log X-\log Y)-X+Y)\ge0\), with equality iff \(X=Y\).
knowledge_statements.title: Trace-Entropy Matrix Divergence

assumptions_latex: \(f:I\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable and strictly convex on an interval containing their spectra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[D_F(X,Y)=\sum_{i=1}^n d_f(\lambda_i(X),\lambda_i(Y))\ge 0,\] with equality exactly when \(X=Y\).

notation.meaning: Spectral trace function induced by the scalar generator
Eigenvalues paired in a common eigenbasis

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the commuting-matrix reduction; noncommuting spectral divergences generally depend on eigenvectors as well.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=U\operatorname{diag}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)U^\top\) and \(Y=U\operatorname{diag}(y_1,\ldots,y_n)U^\top\), with every \(x_i,y_i\in I\). For \(F(X)=\operatorname{tr}f(X)\), its matrix Bregman divergence is
\[D_F(X,Y)=F(X)-F(Y)-\langle f'(Y),X-Y\rangle_F=\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl(f(x_i)-f(y_i)-f'(y_i)(x_i-y_i)\bigr).\]
Thus the divergence is the sum of scalar eigenvalue divergences. Strict convexity of \(f\) gives \(D_F(X,Y)\ge 0\), and equality holds if and only if \(x_i=y_i\) for every \(i\), equivalently \(X=Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For commuting symmetric matrices, a trace-spectral Bregman divergence equals the sum of scalar Bregman divergences between correspondingly paired eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.title: Eigenvalue-Induced Divergences

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The commuting, simultaneously diagonalized representation is mathematically plausible and the representation content kind fits this leaf, but the record supplies no citation supporting the matrix-gradient formula, aligned eigenvalue reduction, and strict equality condition. Source support is required before the formulation can be reliably reviewed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectra Alone Do Not Determine Noncommuting Divergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of an eigenvalue-only pairing formula without a common eigenbasis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(X)=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(X^2)\) on \(\mathbb S^2\), \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(1,0)\), \(Y_1=\operatorname{Diag}(1,0)\), and \(Y_2=\operatorname{Diag}(0,1)\). The matrices \(Y_1\) and \(Y_2\) have the same unordered eigenvalues, but \[D_F(X,Y_1)=0,\qquad D_F(X,Y_2)=\tfrac12\lVert X-Y_2\rVert_F^2=1.\] Therefore the separate unordered spectra of \(X\) and \(Y\) do not determine a spectral Bregman divergence when eigenvector alignment is unspecified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two reference matrices with identical eigenvalues can give different spectral Bregman divergences because their eigenvectors are aligned differently with the first argument.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda(Y_1)=\lambda(Y_2)\) but \(D_F(X,Y_1)\ne D_F(X,Y_2)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Spectra Alone Do Not Determine Noncommuting Divergence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quantum Relative-Entropy Divergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix Bregman divergence induced by the trace negative-entropy generator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(X)=\operatorname{tr}(X\log X)\) on \(\mathbb S_{++}^n\), \[D_F(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(X(\log X-\log Y)-X+Y\bigr).\] If \(\operatorname{tr}X=\operatorname{tr}Y\), this reduces to the Umegaki relative entropy \(\operatorname{tr}(X(\log X-\log Y))\), which is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when \(X=Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The trace-entropy Bregman divergence is matrix relative entropy, reducing to Umegaki relative entropy for equal-trace positive-definite matrices.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) is a Legendre function if it is essentially smooth and essentially strictly convex. Essential strict convexity means that \(f\) is strictly convex on every convex subset of \(\operatorname{dom}\partial f\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine Stability and Failure Boundaries of the Legendre Class
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary invariance properties of finite-dimensional Legendre functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be Legendre. If \(\alpha>0\), \(a\in E^*\), and \(c\in\mathbb R\), then \[g(x)=\alpha f(x)+\langle a,x\rangle+c\] is Legendre and \(\operatorname{dom}g=\operatorname{dom}f\). If \(A:F\to E\) is an affine isomorphism, then \(f\circ A\) is Legendre on \(F\). These restrictions are essential in general: zero scaling destroys essential strict convexity, negative scaling destroys convexity, and a noninjective affine pullback can destroy essential strict convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive scaling, affine perturbation, and invertible affine changes of variables preserve Legendre functions; zero or negative scaling and noninjective pullbacks need not.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) and \(F\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha f+\langle a,\cdot\rangle+c\) and \(f\circ A\) are Legendre, subject to the stated sharp restrictions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gradient-growth characterization of co-finiteness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential characterization for differentiable convex functions on the full Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and convex. Then \(f\) is co-finite if and only if, for every sequence \((x_i)_{i\ge1}\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(\|x_i\|\to+\infty\), one has \(\|\nabla f(x_i)\|\to+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A differentiable convex function on Euclidean space is co-finite exactly when its gradient norm tends to infinity along every sequence whose points escape to infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is co-finite}\iff\forall (x_i)\subset\mathbb{R}^n,\;\|x_i\|\to+\infty\Longrightarrow\|\nabla f(x_i)\|\to+\infty.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Essential Smoothness and Single-Valuedness of the Subdifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes essential smoothness of closed proper convex functions and specifies the subdifferential both inside and outside the domain interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be closed, proper, and convex. Then \(\partial f\) is single-valued, meaning \(|\partial f(x)|\le 1\) for every \(x\), if and only if \(f\) is essentially smooth. When these conditions hold, \(\partial f(x)=\{\nabla f(x)\}\) for \(x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\), and \(\partial f(x)=\varnothing\) for \(x\notin\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed proper convex function, essential smoothness is equivalent to the subdifferential having at most one value everywhere. In that case the subdifferential equals the gradient on the domain interior and is empty outside that interior.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is closed, proper, and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial f\text{ is single-valued}\iff f\text{ is essentially smooth},\qquad \partial f(x)=\begin{cases}\{\nabla f(x)\},&x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f),\\ \varnothing,&x\notin\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f).\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict and Essential Strict Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes ordinary strict convexity on a convex set from essential strict convexity relative to the subdifferential domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A real-valued function \(f\) on a convex set \(C\) is strictly convex on \(C\) if, for all distinct \(x_1,x_2\in C\) and every \(\lambda\in(0,1)\), \(f((1-\lambda)x_1+\lambda x_2)<(1-\lambda)f(x_1)+\lambda f(x_2)\). A proper convex function \(f\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) is essentially strictly convex if its restriction to every convex subset of \(\operatorname{dom}\partial f=\{x\mid\partial f(x)\ne\varnothing\}\) is strictly convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict convexity requires a strict chord inequality between every two distinct points. A proper convex function is essentially strictly convex when this property holds on every convex subset of the domain where its subdifferential is nonempty.
assumptions_latex: C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is convex and }f:C\to\mathbb{R}\text{ for strict convexity}
f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper and convex for essential strict convexity}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is essentially strictly convex}\iff \forall D\subseteq\operatorname{dom}\partial f\text{ convex},\ \forall x_1\ne x_2\in D,\ \forall\lambda\in(0,1),\ f((1-\lambda)x_1+\lambda x_2)<(1-\lambda)f(x_1)+\lambda f(x_2)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Essential Smoothness of a Proper Convex Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the whole-space smoothness convention and the boundary gradient blow-up condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An extended-real-valued function on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) is smooth if it is finite and differentiable throughout \(\mathbb{R}^n\). A proper convex function \(f\) is essentially smooth if, for \(C=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\), (i) \(C\ne\varnothing\), (ii) \(f\) is differentiable on \(C\), and (iii) for every sequence \((x_i)\subset C\) converging to a boundary point of \(C\), \(\|\nabla f(x_i)\|\to+\infty\). Every smooth convex function on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) is essentially smooth because \(C=\mathbb{R}^n\) has no boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper convex function is essentially smooth when its domain has nonempty interior, it is differentiable throughout that interior, and its gradient norm diverges along every interior sequence approaching the boundary. A finite differentiable convex function on all of Euclidean space is essentially smooth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is essentially smooth}\iff C\ne\varnothing,\ f\in C^1(C)\text{ in the differentiability sense, and }\forall (x_i)\subset C,\ x_i\to x\in\partial C\Rightarrow \|\nabla f(x_i)\|\to+\infty

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex functions of Legendre type
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the Legendre-type class, states the boundary of unrestricted Legendre conjugation, and records the injective-subdifferential characterization. The referenced essential-smoothness conditions are not expanded in this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pair \((C,f)\) is called a convex function of Legendre type when \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and convex and \(f\) is strictly convex on \(C\) and satisfies conditions \((a),(b)\), and \((c)\) (or \((c')\)) from the referenced definition of essential smoothness. The Legendre transformation gives a symmetric one-to-one correspondence on this class. In contrast, the Legendre conjugate of a general differentiable convex function need not be differentiable or convex, so its iterated Legendre conjugate need not be defined. Moreover, if \(\bar f\) is closed, proper, and convex and \(C=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}\bar f)\), then \(\partial\bar f\) is one-to-one if and only if \((C,\bar f|_C)\) is of Legendre type.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Legendre-type pair consists of an open convex set and a strictly convex function satisfying the cited essential-smoothness conditions. Legendre transformation is a symmetric one-to-one correspondence on this class, whereas unrestricted Legendre conjugation can fail to remain differentiable or convex. For a closed proper convex function, the subdifferential is one-to-one exactly when the function restricted to the interior of its domain is of Legendre type.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is strictly convex on }C\text{ and satisfies the cited conditions }(a),(b),\text{ and }(c)\text{ or }(c')
\bar f\text{ is closed, proper, and convex, with }C=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}\bar f),\text{ for the subdifferential characterization}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (C,f)\text{ is of Legendre type};\quad \text{Legendre transformation is symmetric and one-to-one on this class};\quad \partial\bar f\text{ is one-to-one}\iff(C,\bar f|_C)\text{ is of Legendre type}.

The function \(f\) is essentially smooth when \(U=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\) is nonempty, \(f\) is differentiable on \(U\), and for every sequence \((x_k)\subset U\) converging to any \(\bar x\in\operatorname{bdry}(\operatorname{dom}f)\),

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interior Differentiability Does Not Imply Essential Smoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure when the boundary-gradient condition is omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(f:\mathbb R\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) by \[f(x)=\begin{cases}x^2,&x\ge0,\\+\infty,&x<0.\end{cases}\] Then \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and differentiable on \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)=(0,\infty)\), but for \(x_k\downarrow0\), \(f'(x_k)=2x_k\to0\). Thus \(f\) is not essentially smooth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex function may be differentiable throughout its domain interior but fail essential smoothness because its gradient stays bounded near the boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Interior differentiability alone does not imply essential smoothness.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Essential Smoothness–Essential Strict Convexity Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel-conjugate characterization of essential smoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be a proper lower-semicontinuous convex function on a finite-dimensional real vector space. Then \[f\text{ is essentially smooth}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f^*\text{ is essentially strictly convex}.\] Equivalently, \(f\) is essentially strictly convex if and only if \(f^*\) is essentially smooth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fenchel conjugation exchanges essential smoothness and essential strict convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is essentially smooth if and only if \(f^*\) is essentially strictly convex.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and essentially smooth, and put \(U=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\). Then \[\operatorname{dom}\partial f=U,\qquad \partial f(x)=\{\nabla f(x)\}\quad(x\in U).\] In particular, \(\partial f(x)=\varnothing\) for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\setminus U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an essentially smooth closed convex function, subgradients exist exactly in the domain interior and there equal the ordinary gradient; finite boundary points have no subgradient.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and essentially smooth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dom}\partial f=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\), with singleton subdifferentials there and empty subdifferentials at finite boundary points.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Disciplined Curvature Verification System
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal E\) be a typed expression language whose expressions are finite rooted trees formed from leaves and registered atoms. Let \(\mathcal K=\{\mathsf{constant},\mathsf{affine},\mathsf{convex},\mathsf{concave},\mathsf{unknown}\}\), and let \(\mathcal D\) be a language of domain constraints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static, syntax-directed certification of scalar expression curvature and effective-domain conditions. It establishes sufficient certificates and is not assumed complete for all mathematically convex or concave functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A disciplined curvature verifier is a sound partial map \[\mathcal V:\mathcal E\longrightarrow \mathcal K\times\mathcal D\times\mathcal R,\qquad \mathcal V(e)=(\kappa_e,\Gamma_e,R_e),\] defined recursively from leaf metadata and atom metadata. Here \(\Gamma_e\) describes the inferred domain, \(R_e\) is an abstract sign or range, and \(\kappa_e\) is obtained only through registered curvature-preserving rules. Soundness means that whenever \(\Gamma_e(x)\) holds, \(e(x)\) is defined and lies in \(R_e\); moreover, \(\kappa_e=\mathsf{convex}\), \(\mathsf{concave}\), or \(\mathsf{affine}\) implies that the represented function has that curvature on the inferred convex domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disciplined curvature verification is a static recursive analysis of an expression tree. It combines leaf facts with registered facts about each atom to infer a domain, a sign or range, and a curvature label. Any returned non-unknown curvature label must be mathematically sound, although a mathematically convex expression may remain unknown.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal V(e)=(\kappa_e,\Gamma_e,R_e),\quad \kappa_e\neq\mathsf{unknown}\Longrightarrow\text{the curvature assertion encoded by \(\kappa_e\) is valid on \(\{x:\Gamma_e(x)\}\)}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The verifier may equivalently be viewed as a derivability relation \(\mathcal M\vdash e:(\kappa,\Gamma,R)\), where \(\mathcal M\) is the registered metadata environment.
special_cases_latex: If \(e\) is affine, both convexity and concavity certificates are valid.
If the root is a single registered atom applied to affine arguments, verification reduces to checking its declared domain and affine-composition metadata.
immediate_consequences_latex: A successful certificate is checkable from the finite expression tree and metadata table.
Failure to derive a certificate does not imply that the represented function lacks the requested curvature.
boundary_notes: This definition does not specify graph reduction, cone selection, or numerical solver compilation.
Soundness requires truthful atom metadata; unverified metadata invalidates the guarantee.
The verifier treats syntax as evidence, so equivalent formulas can receive different outcomes.
review_flags: No inspected local source directly formalized the complete static verifier, metadata state, and soundness contract used in this definition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expression-Tree Abstract Curvature Propagation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(T_e\) be the finite rooted tree of an expression \(e\). Each node \(v\) represents either a leaf or an atom application \(a_v(v_1,\ldots,v_k)\). Let \(\mathcal A\) be an abstract-state space containing well-formedness, domain, range, sign, and curvature components.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bottom-up structural analysis of a fixed expression tree. The definition concerns propagation of certificates, not semantic simplification or canonicalization of algebraically equivalent expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Expression-tree curvature propagation is the unique bottom-up assignment \[S:T_e\to\mathcal A\] determined by leaf initializers \(S(v)=I(v)\) at leaves and registered transfer maps \[S(v)=F_{a_v}(S(v_1),\ldots,S(v_k))\] at internal nodes. A transfer map may return a certified curvature only when the children's domain and range states satisfy the atom's declared domain and monotonicity conditions. The analysis result for \(e\) is the root state \(S(\operatorname{root}(T_e))\). Every transfer map is required to be sound with respect to the concrete functions denoted by its node and children.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expression-tree curvature propagation assigns an abstract state to every tree node, beginning with leaf states and applying an atom-specific transfer function at each parent. The root state is the analysis result. A curvature certificate may be propagated only when the child states satisfy the atom's domain, range, and monotonicity requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[S(v)=\begin{cases}I(v),&v\text{ is a leaf},\\F_{a_v}(S(v_1),\ldots,S(v_k)),&v=a_v(v_1,\ldots,v_k),\end{cases}\qquad \operatorname{Analysis}(e)=S(\operatorname{root}(T_e)).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The assignment is equivalently a postorder fold of \(T_e\) with leaf algebra \(I\) and atom algebras \(F_a\).
special_cases_latex: For a one-node expression, the root state is its leaf initializer.
For a composition chain, propagation reduces to successive unary transfer-map applications.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every reported root certificate has a finite certificate tree mirroring a subtree of \(T_e\).
Changing a child state can affect every ancestor state but cannot directly affect nodes outside the ancestor path.
boundary_notes: The definition does not require the abstract state to be complete.
Common-subexpression sharing may replace the tree by a directed acyclic graph without changing the local transfer rule.
Rewriting the tree before analysis can change the result.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: A leaf \(\ell\) denotes a constant, parameter, or decision-variable object in a finite-dimensional vector or matrix space \(E_\ell\). Its abstract metadata state is \(M(\ell)=(\tau_\ell,\kappa_\ell,R_\ell,D_\ell,\nu_\ell)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Base metadata used to initialize static curvature analysis. Parameter attributes are treated as declared assumptions, while decision-variable values remain unknown except for explicitly declared structural domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The expression-leaf metadata taxonomy consists of: \[(i)\ \tau_\ell=\mathsf{constant}:\quad \kappa_\ell=\mathsf{constant},\ D_\ell=E_\ell,\ R_\ell\ni\nu_\ell;\] \[(ii)\ \tau_\ell=\mathsf{parameter}:\quad \kappa_\ell=\mathsf{constant},\ D_\ell\subseteq E_\ell\text{ is the declared parameter domain},\ R_\ell\supseteq D_\ell;\] \[(iii)\ \tau_\ell=\mathsf{variable}:\quad \kappa_\ell=\mathsf{affine},\ D_\ell\subseteq E_\ell\text{ is its declared structural domain},\ R_\ell\supseteq D_\ell.\] A leaf initializer is valid only if its concrete value, when fixed, belongs to \(D_\ell\cap R_\ell\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Leaves are classified as constants, parameters, or decision variables. Constants and parameters are constant with respect to optimization variables, while decision-variable leaves are affine. Each leaf also carries its ambient type, declared domain, inferred range or sign, and, when applicable, a fixed value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[M(\ell)=(\tau_\ell,\kappa_\ell,R_\ell,D_\ell,\nu_\ell),\qquad \kappa_\ell=\begin{cases}\mathsf{constant},&\tau_\ell\in\{\mathsf{constant},\mathsf{parameter}\},\\\mathsf{affine},&\tau_\ell=\mathsf{variable}.\end{cases}\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A constant may be regarded as a parameter whose admissible set is a singleton.
A parameter is affine as a function of decision variables, but the more informative label \(\mathsf{constant}\) is retained.
special_cases_latex: A nonnegative scalar parameter has \(D_\ell=R_\ell=\mathbb R_+\).
A symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix variable may have \(D_\ell=\mathbb S_+^n\) while retaining affine curvature.
immediate_consequences_latex: All recursive analysis begins from locally checkable leaf states.
Structural-domain declarations can refine signs or spectral ranges before any atom is visited.
boundary_notes: A variable constrained elsewhere by a general constraint is not automatically assigned that constraint's range unless the analysis explicitly imports it.
Incorrect parameter attributes can make downstream certificates unsound.
Boolean and integer variables require an extended taxonomy not covered here.

notation.meaning: Fixed value when the leaf is a constant or instantiated parameter.

review_flags: No inspected local source provided this exact leaf taxonomy and parameter-attribute semantics.
knowledge_statements.title: Metadata Classes for Expression Leaves

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this leaf taxonomy. The role and availability of \(\nu_\ell\) for variables are also unclear, and the validity condition refers to a concrete value even when a decision-variable leaf has no fixed value.

children.title: Constant Metadata
children.top_down_role: Structural metadata attached to fixed expression values.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constant-Leaf Metadata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scalar metadata for a stored value independent of all decision variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a scalar constant leaf with stored value \(c\in\mathbb R\), the exact range is \(R(c)=\{c\}\), and its sign follows from comparison with zero. As a function of the decision variables it is constant and affine, hence both convex and concave. Any additional declared structural attribute must agree with the stored value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar constant leaf has exact singleton range and sign and is simultaneously constant, affine, convex, and concave.
assumptions_latex: The stored scalar value \(c\) is fixed and independent of every decision variable.
The stored value is represented exactly for the metadata comparisons being asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R(c)=\{c\},\qquad K(c)\supseteq\{\mathrm{constant},\mathrm{affine},\mathrm{convex},\mathrm{concave}\}.

notation.meaning: Range metadata of the constant leaf
Curvature categories assigned to the constant leaf

review_flags: Implementation-specific sign lattices may encode zero and overlapping nonnegative/nonpositive categories differently.
knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Leaf Metadata

assumptions_latex: A constant leaf has fixed value \(c\) independent of all decision variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Its metadata are exact value/range and sign information together with constant, affine, convex, and concave curvature labels.

notation.meaning: Singleton range of the constant leaf

review_flags: sign lattice convention must be aligned with implementation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract scalar-leaf metadata; implementation-specific sign lattices may add zero or unknown categories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a scalar constant leaf with value \(c\in\mathbb R\), initialize its range by \(R(c)=\{c\}\) and its sign from the exact comparisons \(c<0\), \(c=0\), or \(c>0\). Since the represented function is independent of every decision variable, assign
\[K(c)=\{\mathrm{constant},\mathrm{affine},\mathrm{convex},\mathrm{concave}\}.\]
Any additional structural metadata, such as integrality, symmetry, or positive semidefiniteness, may be inferred directly from the stored value but cannot contradict its exact range.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant leaf has an exact singleton range and sign, and it belongs simultaneously to the constant, affine, convex, and concave curvature categories.
knowledge_statements.title: Constant Metadata

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar constant-leaf metadata is coherent and property is an appropriate content kind, but no source is supplied for the curvature-label set, sign lattice, or distinction between core and optional structural metadata. These conventions must be tied to an inspectable DCP specification or implementation reference.

children.title: Parameter Metadata
children.top_down_role: Structural metadata attached to externally specified symbolic values.

assumptions_latex: A parameter value is fixed during one verification or solve instance.
Declared sign and range attributes are valid for every admissible parameter assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A parameter is constant with respect to decision variables, while its sign and range come from declarations rather than a symbolic fixed value.

notation.meaning: Curvature-label set of a parameter leaf

review_flags: parameter update policy is implementation dependent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameters are treated as data relative to optimization variables, with declarations supplying uniform metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a parameter leaf take a value \(p\in P\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), where \(P\) is fixed by its declarations. Relative to the model's decision variables, \(p\) is constant, so initialize
\[K(p)=\{\mathrm{constant},\mathrm{affine},\mathrm{convex},\mathrm{concave}\}.\]
Its propagated range is the declared set \(P\), or a sound enclosure of \(P\), and its sign metadata are the strongest sign claims valid for every \(p\in P\). Updating the numerical value within \(P\) does not change this symbolic curvature classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A declared parameter is constant relative to decision variables; its uniform sign and range metadata follow from its admissible parameter set.
knowledge_statements.title: Parameter Metadata

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement is plausible under the declared-set interpretation of parameters, and property fits the terminal container. However, treating a parameter as constant with range equal to its full admissible set is analyzer-specific, and no source establishes the update or metadata semantics.

children.title: Variable Metadata
children.top_down_role: Structural metadata attached to optimization variables.

assumptions_latex: \(x\) is a scalar unconstrained decision-variable leaf.
No domain or sign attribute has yet restricted \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The leaf is affine, hence both convex and concave, but initially has unknown sign and range \(\mathbb R\).
review_flags: constrained and structured variable variants omitted
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Base scalar-variable metadata before constraints or declared attributes refine sign and range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an unconstrained scalar decision-variable leaf \(x\), initialize \(R(x)=\mathbb R\) and assign unknown sign because both positive and negative values are admissible. The coordinate map from the decision vector to \(x\) is affine, so
\[K(x)=\{\mathrm{affine},\mathrm{convex},\mathrm{concave}\}.\]
It is not constant. Declared attributes or subsequently analyzed domain restrictions may soundly narrow \(R(x)\) and its sign, but they do not remove its affine curvature classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unconstrained scalar variable initially has full real range and unknown sign; as a coordinate map, it is affine, convex, and concave.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Metadata

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For an unconstrained scalar coordinate variable, the full-real range, unknown sign, and affine curvature classification are coherent, and property fits the leaf. The record nevertheless lacks an inspectable source for the analyzer's initialization conventions and attribute-refinement behavior.

children.title: Base-Category Initialization
children.top_down_role: How base expression categories seed later structural analysis.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Base-Category Initialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Leaf initialization for an abstract scalar expression-tree curvature analyzer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Classify every leaf \(v\) as a stored constant, parameter, or decision variable. Initialize \(M(v)=(K(v),S(v),R(v))\): constants receive exact value-derived metadata; parameters receive metadata valid uniformly over their declared admissible values and are constant relative to decision variables; variables receive affine curvature and sound declared attributes, with unknown sign and an unrestricted scalar range when no stronger facts are declared. With constant-time leaf declarations, initialization of \(L\) leaves takes \(O(L)\) time and \(O(L)\) output storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize constants from exact values, parameters from uniformly valid declarations, and variables as affine with sound declared attributes; a direct pass is linear in the number of leaves.
assumptions_latex: Each leaf has exactly one base category: constant, parameter, or decision variable.
All declarations used for initialization are sound.
Reading and validating a bounded-size leaf declaration costs \(O(1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Initialization is sound and costs }O(L)\text{ time for }L\text{ leaves}.

notation.meaning: Curvature, sign, and range metadata initialized at leaf v

review_flags: Metadata lattices and validation costs are implementation dependent; the complexity bound states its cost model.
knowledge_statements.title: Base-Category Initialization

children.title: Recursive Curvature Propagation
children.top_down_role: Curvature classification propagated through composition structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear-Time Tree Propagation Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost of one postorder pass when atom arity and local metadata operations have bounded cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an expression tree with \(N\) nodes and height \(H\), if atom arity and each local initialization or rule evaluation have \(O(1)\) cost, one postorder propagation pass uses \(O(N)\) time, \(O(N)\) stored node metadata, and \(O(H)\) auxiliary traversal space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With constant-cost local rules, one postorder propagation pass is linear in the expression-tree size.
assumptions_latex: The representation is a finite tree with \(N\) nodes and height \(H\).
Atom arity and local rule-evaluation cost are uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T(N)=O(N),\qquad S_{\mathrm{metadata}}(N)=O(N),\qquad S_{\mathrm{aux}}=O(H).
review_flags: The analogous DAG bound requires memoization and is measured in distinct nodes and edges.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Time Tree Propagation Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inductive Soundness of Recursive Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional soundness of bottom-up curvature certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a finite expression tree. If every leaf annotation is valid and every internal-node rule soundly maps valid child annotations to an asserted parent curvature label on the certified domain, then every label returned by postorder propagation is valid for its represented subexpression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound leaf annotations and sound local rules make recursively propagated curvature labels sound.
assumptions_latex: Every registered atom rule is sound on its certified domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat K(e)\subseteq K_{\mathrm{true}}(e)\quad\text{for every node }e.

notation.meaning: Curvature labels certified at node e
Mathematically valid curvature labels at node e

knowledge_statements.title: Inductive Soundness of Recursive Propagation

assumptions_latex: The expression is a finite rooted tree whose internal nodes are registered atoms.
Every atom supplies curvature, coordinatewise monotonicity, domain, sign, and range rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A postorder traversal returns a sound curvature classification, or unknown when no composition rule applies.

notation.meaning: Expression rooted at a tree node

review_flags: handling of shared subexpressions and extended-valued domains unspecified
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bottom-up scalar DCP classification using atom-specific composition certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Traverse the tree in postorder. Initialize each leaf's metadata. At an internal node \(e=h(e_1,\ldots,e_m)\), first propagate child signs and ranges, restrict them by the atom domain, and then test registered composition rules. For convexity, each argument must be affine, or convex where \(h\) is nondecreasing, or concave where \(h\) is nonincreasing; additionally, \(h\) must be convex on the certified child ranges. Apply the sign-reversed criterion for concavity and the affine rule when applicable. Store the strongest certified \(M(e)\); if no rule succeeds, store unknown. Output \(M(e_{\mathrm{root}})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A postorder analyzer combines child metadata with each atom's curvature, monotonicity, and domain rules, returning the strongest sound classification or unknown.
knowledge_statements.title: Recursive Curvature Propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind matches recursive curvature propagation, but no source supports the exact multivariate composition test or the claimed strongest-classification behavior. Shared subexpressions, extended-valued domains, and the ordering used to define 'strongest' are also not specified sufficiently to validate the algorithm independently.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recursive Composition Rule for Curvature Labels
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(e(x)=h(g_1(x),\ldots,g_k(x))\). The outer function \(h\) has a convex domain, a curvature label, and a coordinatewise monotonicity label \(m_i\in\{\uparrow,\downarrow,0,?\}\) on the inferred argument range.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient finite-dimensional composition calculus for convex, concave, affine, and constant child expressions, including domain-sensitive coordinatewise monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Recursive curvature propagation assigns \(e=h(g_1,\ldots,g_k)\) the label \(\mathsf{convex}\) when \(h\) is convex and, for every \(i\), either \(g_i\) is affine, or \(h\) is nondecreasing in coordinate \(i\) and \(g_i\) is convex, or \(h\) is nonincreasing in coordinate \(i\) and \(g_i\) is concave. It assigns \(e\) the label \(\mathsf{concave}\) when \(h\) is concave and, for every \(i\), either \(g_i\) is affine, or \(h\) is nondecreasing in coordinate \(i\) and \(g_i\) is concave, or \(h\) is nonincreasing in coordinate \(i\) and \(g_i\) is convex. The inferred domain is \[\{x:x\in\bigcap_i\operatorname{dom}g_i,\ (g_1(x),\ldots,g_k(x))\in\operatorname{dom}h\}.\] If no rule applies, the propagated curvature is \(\mathsf{unknown}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each composition node, convexity propagates through convex nondecreasing coordinates fed by convex children, convex nonincreasing coordinates fed by concave children, and arbitrary coordinates fed by affine children. Concavity uses the dual rule. Failure of these sufficient conditions produces an unknown label.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\kappa(h\circ g)=\begin{cases}\mathsf{convex},&h\text{ and all child-coordinate pairs satisfy the convex rule},\\\mathsf{concave},&h\text{ and all child-coordinate pairs satisfy the concave rule},\\\mathsf{unknown},&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For scalar \(h\circ g\), the convex rule is: \(h\) convex and nondecreasing with \(g\) convex, or \(h\) convex and nonincreasing with \(g\) concave, with affine \(g\) admissible in either case.
special_cases_latex: Composition with an affine mapping preserves the declared curvature of the outer function on the affine preimage of its domain.
A sum atom is affine and coordinatewise nondecreasing, so a sum of convex children is certified convex.
immediate_consequences_latex: The rule is local and can be applied recursively to every internal node.
The inferred effective domain must accompany the curvature label.
boundary_notes: These rules are sufficient but not necessary.
Monotonicity must hold on a domain or range adequate for the actual child values.
The definition does not certify curvature by Hessian calculations or algebraic rewriting.

notation.meaning: Monotonicity of the outer atom in coordinate \(i\).

source_refs.locator: §3.2.4 Composition, equations (3.11) and the vector composition rules

knowledge_statements.title: Recursive Composition Rule for Curvature Labels

source_witnesses.locator: §3.2.4 Composition, equations (3.11) and the vector composition rules

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited section supports the mathematical composition rules and composition domain, but not the complete recursive label-propagation system or the stipulated unknown outcome.

children.title: Sign-Range Propagation Calculus
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary metadata supporting domain-sensitive composition analysis.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Abstract Sign-and-Range Propagation Calculus
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For each typed space \(E\), let \(\mathfrak R(E)\) be a family of representable range enclosures ordered by inclusion. Typical scalar elements include \(\mathbb R\), \(\mathbb R_+\), \(\mathbb R_-\), \(\{0\}\), and intervals; matrix elements may include order cones such as \(\mathbb S_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound auxiliary abstract interpretation of possible expression values, used to check domains and select monotonicity branches. It need not compute the smallest possible range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sign-range propagation calculus assigns every expression node \(v\) an enclosure \(R_v\in\mathfrak R(E_v)\). Leaves receive declared enclosures. For an atom node \(v=a(v_1,,v_k)\), a sound range transformer \(\widehat a\) returns \[R_v=\widehat a(R_{v_1},\ldots,R_{v_k})\] such that \[a\bigl((R_{v_1}\times\cdots\times R_{v_k})\cap\operatorname{dom}a\bigr)\subseteq R_v.\] The node is domain-compatible only if the inferred argument product is contained in, or is separately constrained to, \(\operatorname{dom}a\). The scalar sign is the coarsening of \(R_v\) into positive, negative, zero, or unknown classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The calculus encloses every possible value of each expression node. Atom-specific range transformers map child enclosures to a sound parent enclosure. These enclosures determine coarse signs and help decide whether an atom's domain and monotonicity conditions apply.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{range}(v)\subseteq R_v,\qquad R_v=\widehat a(R_{v_1},\ldots,R_{v_k})\text{ at every atom node}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The calculus is an abstract interpretation with concretization \(\gamma(R)=R\) and soundness \(\operatorname{range}(v)\subseteq\gamma(R_v)\).
special_cases_latex: For scalar addition, interval enclosures propagate by Minkowski addition: \([a,b]+[c,d]=[a+c,b+d]\).
For a square atom, any real input enclosure yields a nonnegative output enclosure.
A positive-semidefinite matrix enclosure may establish the domain of spectral atoms requiring \(X\succeq0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A tighter sound range can enable a curvature rule that an unknown-sign range cannot enable.
Range propagation can identify explicit domain incompatibility before curvature propagation reaches the root.
boundary_notes: An enclosure overlapping invalid and valid atom inputs does not by itself prove that the expression is malformed.
Floating-point interval arithmetic and numerical rounding are outside this static definition.
Relational facts between siblings require a richer domain than independent range products.

notation.meaning: Sound abstract range transformer for atom \(a\).

review_flags: No inspected source directly supported the stated abstract range-enclosure calculus and its domain-compatibility semantics.
knowledge_statements.title: Abstract Sign-and-Range Propagation Calculus

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the abstract range calculus. The atom expression contains the malformed argument list \(a(v_1,,v_k)\), and the alternative that inputs are “separately constrained” does not formally define domain compatibility.

children.title: Sign Propagation
children.top_down_role: Transfer of sign metadata through expression trees.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Correlation Loss in Sign Multiplication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precision boundary of nonrelational sign propagation for repeated expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x\) has unknown sign, treating the two occurrences in \(x\cdot x\) independently gives \(\{-,0,+\}\cdot\{-,0,+\}=\{-,0,+\}\), while the exact sign set of \(x^2\) is \(\{0,+\}\). A nonrelational sign transformer may therefore miss nonnegativity when argument occurrences are correlated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent sign multiplication may fail to infer that x times itself is nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: Both occurrences of \(x\) are represented only by the unknown sign set \(\{-,0,+\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha_{\mathrm{sgn}}(\{x^2:x\in\mathbb R\})=\{0,+\}\subsetneq\{-,0,+\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Correlation Loss in Sign Multiplication

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Powerset Sign Abstract Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical scalar sign abstraction underlying containment-based propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(V\subseteq\mathbb R\), define \(\alpha_{\mathrm{sgn}}(V)=\{\operatorname{sgn}(v):v\in V\}\). Ordered by inclusion, \(\mathcal P(\{-,0,+\})\) is a finite lattice with intersection as meet and union as join. The full set represents unknown sign, and \(\varnothing\) represents no attainable value. A sign annotation \(S\) is sound exactly when \(\alpha_{\mathrm{sgn}}(V)\subseteq S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Possible scalar signs form a finite powerset lattice in which inclusion expresses conservative approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is sound for }V\iff\alpha_{\mathrm{sgn}}(V)\subseteq S.

notation.meaning: Abstraction from real value sets to possible signs

knowledge_statements.title: Powerset Sign Abstract Domain

assumptions_latex: Each child expression has a sound sign or range enclosure.
The parent atom has a sound sign-transfer rule on those enclosures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computed parent sign contains every attainable parent value's sign.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued scalar sign analysis; unknown sign is represented by all three possibilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a leaf, initialize \(S(e)\) from its exact value or declared range. For an internal expression \(e=h(e_1,\ldots,e_m)\), compute
\[S(e)\supseteq\{\operatorname{sgn}(h(t_1,\ldots,t_m)):t_i\in R(e_i),\ (t_1,\ldots,t_m)\in\operatorname{dom}h\}.\]
Use the smallest available registered sign category containing this set; if none is sharper, return \(S(e)=\{-,0,+\}\). The containment, rather than equality, is the soundness requirement and permits conservative atom-specific rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate signs by enclosing every sign attainable from the children over the atom's valid domain; return unknown when no sharper enclosure is certified.
knowledge_statements.title: Sign Propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The containment-based sign propagation rule is internally sound as an abstract algorithm and its content kind fits the leaf. The registered sign categories, range representation, and atom transfer rules are analyzer-specific and have no cited source.

children.title: Range Propagation
children.top_down_role: Transfer of value-range metadata through expression trees.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dependency Loss in Independent Range Arithmetic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precision boundary of nonrelational interval propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in[-1,1]\) and \(e=x-x\). The exact attainable range is \(\{0\}\), whereas independent interval subtraction gives \([-1,1]-[-1,1]=[-2,2]\). Thus componentwise range propagation can be sound but strictly inexact when repeated subexpressions are correlated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent interval arithmetic maps x minus itself to [-2,2] although its exact range is {0}.
assumptions_latex: The two occurrences are represented only by independent interval enclosures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{range}(x-x)=\{0\}\subsetneq[-2,2].
knowledge_statements.title: Dependency Loss in Independent Range Arithmetic

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compositional Soundness of Range Enclosures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional structural soundness of recursively propagated outer range enclosures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every leaf enclosure contains all attainable leaf values and every atom transformer outer-encloses the atom image over its feasible child enclosure, then every recursively computed enclosure \(R(e)\) contains all values attainable by the represented subexpression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound leaf ranges and sound atom image bounds yield sound range enclosures throughout a finite expression tree.
assumptions_latex: Every atom transformer outer-encloses its image over the feasible child enclosure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{range}(e)\subseteq R(e)\quad\text{for every node }e.
knowledge_statements.title: Compositional Soundness of Range Enclosures

assumptions_latex: Each child range is a sound enclosure of all attainable child values.
The atom's range transformer is sound on the intersection with its domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The propagated range encloses every attainable value of the parent expression.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract range-enclosure propagation, independent of whether intervals or richer sets are stored.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an internal expression \(e=h(e_1,\ldots,e_m)\), form the feasible input enclosure
\[Q=\bigl(R(e_1)\times\cdots\times R(e_m)\bigr)\cap\operatorname{dom}h.\]
Choose a representable set \(R(e)\) satisfying
\[\{h(t):t\in Q\}\subseteq R(e).\]
When the exact image is representable, use it; otherwise use a certified outer enclosure, such as interval bounds derived from endpoint evaluation, monotonicity, or an atom-specific bound. If \(Q=\varnothing\), report domain infeasibility rather than an ordinary range.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersect child ranges with the atom domain, map the feasible enclosure through the atom, and store an exact image or certified outer bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Range Propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The outer-enclosure formulation and separate domain-infeasibility outcome are coherent, and algorithm is appropriate for this leaf. No source identifies the supported enclosure domain, certified transformers, or endpoint and monotonicity rules, so the operational claim cannot yet be validated.

children.title: Propagation Interactions
children.top_down_role: Mutual refinement between inferred sign metadata plus inferred range metadata.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Height Refinement Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination of repeated sound metadata refinement on a finite-height precision order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((L,\preceq)\) be a finite-height metadata poset ordered from less precise to more precise, and let \(F:L\to L\) satisfy \(m\preceq F(m)\). Then \(m_{k+1}=F(m_k)\) stabilizes after at most \(\operatorname{ht}(L)-1\) strict refinements. If each iterate soundly overapproximates the concrete metadata, the stabilized result remains sound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Precision-increasing refinement on a finite-height metadata order terminates after finitely many strict improvements and preserves soundness.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is inflationary in the precision order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists k<\operatorname{ht}(L)\quad m_{k+1}=m_k.

notation.meaning: Order from less precise to more precise metadata

review_flags: The bound counts elements in a longest strict chain; infinite-height domains require a different termination policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Height Refinement Termination

assumptions_latex: Sign and range transformers are individually sound.
Curvature rules declare the regions on which their monotonicity and curvature hypotheses hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Iterated refinement may strengthen metadata but must never exclude an attainable value or assert an invalid curvature class.

notation.meaning: Range enclosure compatible with a sign class

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mutual refinement of sign, range, and curvature metadata in a sound abstract interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given sound metadata \((K,S,R)\), refine sign by \(S\leftarrow S\cap\alpha(R)\) and range by \(R\leftarrow R\cap\gamma(S)\), where both abstractions contain all concrete possibilities. Re-evaluate atom domains, monotonicity regions, and curvature rules after either refinement. Repeat until no stored category changes or a prescribed finite-lattice fixed point is reached. Every update must be contracting in the metadata order yet sound for the concrete expression; an empty feasible range signals domain infeasibility, while failure to sharpen leaves the previous metadata unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sign and range information refine one another, and each refinement can activate stronger domain, monotonicity, or curvature rules without sacrificing soundness.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Interactions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mutual-refinement principle is plausible when the sign and range abstractions are sound and the metadata order is finite. Principle fits the interaction leaf, but no citation defines the abstraction/concretization operators, ordering, fixed-point policy, or termination assumptions needed for the stated iteration.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Lattice Refinement Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination of repeated sound metadata refinement on a finite-height abstract domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((L,\preceq)\) be a finite-height metadata lattice ordered from less precise to more precise, and let \(F:L\to L\) be monotone and inflationary in precision: \(m\preceq F(m)\). Then the iteration \(m_{k+1}=F(m_k)\) stabilizes at a fixed point after at most \(\operatorname{ht}(L)-1\) strict refinements. If every abstract element encountered soundly contains the concrete metadata, the stabilized result remains sound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monotone precision-increasing refinement on a finite-height metadata lattice terminates after finitely many strict improvements and preserves soundness.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is monotone and inflationary in the precision order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists k<\operatorname{ht}(L)\;\;m_{k+1}=m_k=F(m_k).

children.title: Atom Metadata Interface
children.top_down_role: Declarative curvature, monotonicity, sign, and domain information for atomic functions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Declarative Metadata Contract for Atomic Functions
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: An atom is a typed function \(a:E_1\times\cdots\times E_k\to F\) with effective domain \(D_a\subseteq E_1\times\cdots\times E_k\). A verifier consumes metadata without inspecting an atom implementation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Declarative interface sufficient for static domain, sign-range, monotonicity, and curvature propagation. Computational graph implementations and conic reductions are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An atom metadata record is a tuple \[M_a=(E_1,\ldots,E_k;F;D_a;\kappa_a;\{(Q_j,m_{j1},\ldots,m_{jk})\}_{j\in J};\widehat a),\] where \(D_a\) is the effective domain, \(\kappa_a\in\{\mathsf{constant},\mathsf{affine},\mathsf{convex},\mathsf{concave}\}\) is valid on \(D_a\), the cells \(Q_j\subseteq D_a\) cover the supported argument region, \(m_{ji}\) declares monotonicity in coordinate \(i\) on \(Q_j\), and \(\widehat a\) is a sound range transformer. The interface is valid when all declarations hold for the concrete atom on their stated domains and ranges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An atom exposes its input and output types, effective domain, curvature, region-dependent coordinate monotonicity, and a sound output-range transformer. These declarations form a contract: every item must be true of the concrete atomic function on the region where it is advertised.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[M_a\text{ is valid}\Longleftrightarrow D_a,\kappa_a,m_{ji},\widehat a\text{ are sound descriptions of \(a\) on every supported cell \(Q_j\)}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A global monotonicity declaration is represented by one cell \(Q_1=D_a\).
An affine atom may declare both convex and concave behavior through the single label \(\mathsf{affine}\).
special_cases_latex: For \(a(u,v)=u+v\), \(D_a=E\times E\), the atom is affine, and it is nondecreasing in both scalar arguments.
For \(a(t)=-\log t\), \(D_a=\mathbb R_{++}\), the atom is convex and decreasing, with positive output not guaranteed globally.
immediate_consequences_latex: The verifier can analyze a new atom once a valid metadata record is registered.
Separating metadata from implementation permits certificate checking without evaluating derivatives during analysis.
boundary_notes: The interface does not provide a numerical evaluation routine.
Metadata valid only on a restricted cell must not be used outside that cell.
Shape compatibility and broadcasting rules must be included in the type component when the language supports them.

notation.meaning: Argument region supporting a monotonicity profile.

children.title: Atom Curvature Metadata
children.top_down_role: Curvature classifications attached to atomic functions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conservative Meaning of Curvature Labels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness boundary of atom curvature metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A non-unknown curvature declaration is a sufficient certificate usable by recursive composition rules. Failure to obtain such a declaration, or propagation of the label unknown, does not imply that the atom or resulting expression lacks the mathematical curvature property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Curvature labels are conservative certificates: unknown means that the verifier has no certificate, not that the expression is nonconvex or nonconcave.
assumptions_latex: The verifier propagates only sound atom metadata and sound composition rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{unknown}\) denotes absence of a curvature certificate rather than a certificate of curvature failure.
knowledge_statements.title: Conservative Meaning of Curvature Labels

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Atom Curvature Metadata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain-relative curvature declarations for atomic functions in a disciplined-curvature verifier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an atom \(f:D_f\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) on a convex declared domain, curvature metadata may certify that \(f\) is constant, affine, convex, or concave on \(D_f\); an unknown classification makes no curvature assertion. These properties are not mathematically exclusive: a constant atom is affine, and an affine atom is both convex and concave. Any single implementation may store a most-specific tag while retaining these implications.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Curvature metadata gives a sound domain-relative constant, affine, convex, concave, or unknown classification; unknown means uncertified, not nonconvex.
assumptions_latex: \(D_f\) is the atom's declared convex domain.
The metadata system uses sound curvature declarations rather than empirical guesses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every declared non-unknown label certifies its stated curvature property on \(D_f\), while unknown asserts no curvature property.
knowledge_statements.title: Atom Curvature Metadata

children.title: Atom Monotonicity Metadata
children.top_down_role: Argument-wise monotonicity used by composition verification.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Domain-Relative and Conservative Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness boundary for monotonicity metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A monotonicity declaration applies only to feasible comparable pairs in the declared domain, or to a certified attainable subrange when range-refined metadata is used. An unknown declaration means that no usable direction has been certified; it does not assert that the atom is mathematically nonmonotone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monotonicity labels are conservative and domain-relative; unknown means uncertified rather than nonmonotone.
assumptions_latex: Only sound domain or range information is supplied to the verifier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unknown monotonicity is absence of a certificate, and declared monotonicity cannot be applied outside its certified feasible range.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Relative and Conservative Semantics

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Argument-Wise Monotonicity Metadata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise order declarations consumed by disciplined composition rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each argument \(i\), monotonicity metadata may certify that an atom \(f:D_f\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is nondecreasing, nonincreasing, constant, or unknown in that coordinate. For feasible \(x,z\in D_f\) agreeing outside coordinate \(i\) with \(x_i\le z_i\), these labels respectively certify \(f(x)\le f(z)\), \(f(x)\ge f(z)\), \(f(x)=f(z)\), or no order relation. Constant is equivalently the simultaneous availability of both directional certificates on comparable feasible pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monotonicity metadata records sound coordinatewise order behavior on feasible comparable inputs; unknown supplies no order certificate.
assumptions_latex: The atom has a declared domain \(D_f\subseteq X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\).
Each coordinate space carries the order used by the verifier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each non-unknown coordinate label certifies the corresponding comparison for feasible comparable pairs in \(D_f\).
knowledge_statements.title: Argument-Wise Monotonicity Metadata

assumptions_latex: The atom \(f:D_f\subseteq X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) has a declared domain.
Each coordinate space carries the order used by the verifier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coordinate labels state exactly which order comparisons may be used in curvature composition rules.

notation.meaning: Argument-wise monotonicity label for coordinate i.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports DCP argument-wise monotonicity metadata; a DCP reference is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise order metadata used by disciplined composition rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each argument \(i\), the monotonicity metadata is \(\mu_{f,i}\in\{\mathrm{nondecreasing},\mathrm{nonincreasing},\mathrm{constant},\mathrm{unknown}\}\). For any \(x,y\in D_f\) agreeing outside coordinate \(i\) and satisfying \(x_i\leq y_i\), nondecreasing requires \(f(x)\leq f(y)\), nonincreasing requires \(f(x)\geq f(y)\), and constant requires \(f(x)=f(y)\). The unknown label asserts none of these relations. Every declared relation is restricted to comparable feasible pairs in \(D_f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monotonicity metadata records, for each argument, whether the atom is nondecreasing, nonincreasing, constant, or unclassified on feasible comparable inputs.
knowledge_statements.title: Atom Monotonicity Metadata

children.title: Sign-Refined Atom Metadata Coupling
children.top_down_role: Atom metadata refined by inferred signs and argument ranges.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coupling Inferred Ranges to Regional Atom Metadata
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an atom \(a\) have metadata cells \(Q_j\subseteq\operatorname{dom}a\), each carrying curvature and coordinate-monotonicity declarations. Let child analysis provide a product enclosure \(R=R_1	imes\cdots	imes R_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regional refinement of atom metadata using inferred signs or ranges. A metadata branch is usable only when its validity region contains the entire relevant child enclosure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Sign-refined metadata coupling selects the admissible branch set \[J(R):=\{j:R\subseteq Q_j\}.\] A curvature transfer may use branch \(j\) only when \(j\in J(R)\), and it must combine the branch's monotonicity profile with the children's curvature labels. If \(J(R)=\varnothing\), or if admissible branches yield incompatible conclusions, the coupled curvature result is \(\mathsf{unknown}\). Range refinement is sound when \(R'\subseteq R\) implies that every branch enabled at \(R\) remains valid at \(R'\), while additional branches may become enabled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inferred child ranges select which regional monotonicity and curvature declarations of an atom may be used. A declaration is eligible only if its region contains all inferred argument values. No eligible branch, or disagreement among eligible branches, produces an unknown result.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[J(R)=\{j:R\subseteq Q_j\},\qquad \operatorname{Couple}(M_a,R)=\begin{cases}\text{common sound propagated label},&J(R)\neq\varnothing,\\\mathsf{unknown},&J(R)=\varnothing\text{ or conclusions conflict}.\end{cases}\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For scalar sign cells, branch selection may be indexed by \(R\subseteq\mathbb R_+\), \(R\subseteq\mathbb R_-\), or \(R=\{0\}\).
special_cases_latex: For the square atom, a nonnegative input range enables the increasing branch, while a nonpositive input range enables the decreasing branch.
If an atom is globally monotone, its sole metadata cell is the whole effective domain and sign refinement is unnecessary.
immediate_consequences_latex: Tighter range information can convert an unknown composition into a certified one.
A branch selected from a strict range enclosure remains valid for any tighter enclosure.
boundary_notes: An enclosure merely intersecting a metadata cell is insufficient for universal certification.
Disjunctive reasoning over several cells requires explicit case analysis and is not implicit in this definition.
Sign refinement cannot repair incorrect atom metadata.

notation.meaning: Validity cell for one atom metadata profile.
Product enclosure inferred for the atom arguments.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sign-Dependent Curvature of the Cubic Atom
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical scalar example of a curvature label changing with certified sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=x^3\), the restriction \(f|_{[0,\infty)}\) is convex and the restriction \(f|_{(-\infty,0]}\) is concave. Neither label is valid on all of \(\mathbb R\). On the singleton regime \(\{0\}\), the restriction is constant and hence affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cubic atom is convex on nonnegative inputs and concave on nonpositive inputs, so neither restricted label is globally valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f|_{[0,\infty)}\text{ is convex},\qquad f|_{(-\infty,0]}\text{ is concave}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Sign-refined curvature metadata is a partial map \(\kappa_f:\mathcal S\to\{\mathrm{constant},\mathrm{affine},\mathrm{convex},\mathrm{concave},\mathrm{unknown}\}\). A regime \(S\in\mathcal S\) specifies coordinate sign constraints such as \(x_i\geq0\), \(x_i\leq0\), or \(x_i=0\). The value \(\kappa_f(S)\) must satisfy the corresponding curvature inequality for all feasible segments contained in \(D_f\cap S\). It may be used only after the verifier has certified that the atom's arguments lie in \(S\); outside that regime it makes no assertion.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Sign-refined monotonicity metadata consists of partial maps \(\mu_{f,i}:\mathcal S\to\{\mathrm{nondecreasing},\mathrm{nonincreasing},\mathrm{constant},\mathrm{unknown}\}\). For \(S\in\mathcal S\), take \(x,y\in D_f\cap S\) that agree outside coordinate \(i\) and satisfy \(x_i\leq y_i\). children.title: Argument-Range Refinements
children.top_down_role: Metadata refinements enabled by restricted argument ranges.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistence under Range Restriction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistence, but not automatic strengthening, of metadata on smaller certified ranges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R'_i\subseteq R_i\), \(D_R=D_f\cap\prod_iR_i\), and \(D_{R'}=D_f\cap\prod_iR'_i\). Every curvature or coordinatewise-monotonicity inequality valid on \(D_R\) remains valid on \(D_{R'}\). A stronger label on \(D_{R'}\) requires a separate certificate and cannot in general be extrapolated to \(D_R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shrinking certified argument ranges preserves sound metadata, but stronger metadata on the smaller region requires its own certificate and cannot be extrapolated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_{R'}\subseteq D_R\Longrightarrow\text{ every metadata predicate valid on }D_R\text{ remains valid on }D_{R'}.

notation.meaning: Domain restricted by the original certified ranges.
Domain restricted by smaller certified ranges.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistence under Range Restriction

assumptions_latex: The verifier has certified argument ranges \(R_i\subseteq X_i\).
The atom has valid metadata on the restricted feasible set \(D_f\cap(R_1\times\cdots\times R_m)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restriction to certified ranges may justify stronger curvature or monotonicity labels, but never labels whose defining inequalities fail on the restricted feasible set.
review_flags: A source on range-sensitive DCP metadata and inference is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strengthening atom metadata by restricting arguments to certified ranges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(D_R=D_f\cap(R_1\times\cdots\times R_m)\). Curvature and coordinatewise monotonicity metadata may be recomputed on \(D_R\) using only feasible segments and comparable pairs contained in \(D_R\). Thus an atom globally labeled unknown may receive a definite label on \(D_R\). Refinement is valid only when the expression analysis certifies \(g_i(z)\in R_i\) for every feasible \(z\) and every argument \(i\). If this inclusion is not certified, metadata valid merely on \(D_R\) cannot be used for the composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified argument ranges restrict the feasible domain and may strengthen curvature or monotonicity metadata, provided every composed argument is proved to remain in range.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R'_i\subseteq R_i\) and set \(D_R=D_f\cap\prod_iR_i\), \(D_{R'}=D_f\cap\prod_iR'_i\). Thus restriction cannot invalidate an existing sound label, although a stronger label on \(D_{R'}\) requires a separate certificate and need not extend to \(D_R\).
